items.head: Cleared to face Miami
items.body: Shavers (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Shavers was activated from the reserve/PUP list Saturday, and the San Diego State product has been officially cleared to play Sunday in what will be his first game since the Bills AFC wild-card round win over the Jaguars in January, when he tore his ACL. Shavers will likely operate in a rotational role on offense behind DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

items.head: Makes return from PUP list
items.body: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports. Shavers' 21-day evaluation window was set to close this week, so the Bills elected to add him back to the 53-man roster to ensure that he would be available to play this season. The wideout has been a full practice participant for the past two weeks, so he appears to be fully recovered from the torn ACL he sustained in January and should be available for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If active for the Week 11 contest, Shavers will likely slot in as a depth option at receiver behind the trio of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

items.head: Haynes King (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Remaining backup QB for Week 11
items.body: Daniels is set for his usual role as Tampa Bay's backup quarterback Sunday versus Detroit, as Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) is active and will start, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. Mayfield entered Sunday deemed questionable due to his injuries, but he's ultimately going to be able to suit up. As such, Daniels will retain his role as Mayfield's backup. Easton Stick (coach's decision) is serving as Tampa Bay's emergency third quarterback.

items.head: Trending toward backup duties for Week 11
items.body: Head coach Todd Bowles expressed optimism Friday that Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) would start against the Lions on Sunday, which would leave Daniels as the Buccaneers' QB2, Scott Smith and Brianna Dix of the team's official site report. Mayfield injured his foot in Week 10 against the Bears and sat out of Wednesday's practice, which resulted in Daniels taking all of the first-team reps during that session. Mayfield returned to practice Thursday and Friday as a limited participant, and it appears as though the 2018 first-overall pick will be under center for Sunday's game, and that would result in Daniels operating as the backup and Easton Stick as the emergency third quarterback. Daniels started from Weeks 4 through 6 and went 1-2 over that stretch, when he completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions while turning 19 carries into 117 yards.

items.head: Getting first-team reps Wednesday
items.body: Daniels is slated to take all of the first-teams reps Wednesday with Baker Mayfield (foot) sidelined for the Buccaneers' first Week 11 practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.

items.head: Could be headed for Week 11 start
items.body: Daniels "seems to be trending" toward drawing the start at quarterback for the Buccaneers on Sunday in Detroit while Baker Mayfield tends to a foot strain, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Does individual work, but iffy for Week 12
items.body: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Jacobs (finger) did some individual work Saturday, but the running back will "have to show a lot of progress" over the next two days to be available Week 12 versus the Rams, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Practicing Saturday
items.body: Jacobs (finger) is participating in Saturday's practice session, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.

items.head: Unlikely to play Wednesday
items.body: Jacobs (finger) isn't expected to play Wednesday against the Rams, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Could be back for Week 12
items.body: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Undergoes finger surgery
items.body: Jacobs underwent surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday and "should be back in the next few weeks," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Set for surgery on finger Friday
items.body: Jacobs (finger) will undergo surgery Friday, and the Packers will have a better sense of his recovery timetable afterward, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Could return in 2-to-3 weeks
items.body: Jacobs will undergo surgery on his broken right ring finger later this week and could be cleared to play in as soon as 2-to-3 weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Finger surgery on tap, IR a possibility
items.body: When asked if IR is a possibility for Jacobs (finger), coach Matt LaFleur said Monday, "I think everything is a possibility," Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, LaFleur confirmed Monday that Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured ring finger. As a result of the looming procedure, Pelissero adds that that the running back is out indefinitely, which supports the notion that an IR stint for Jacobs could be on the table.

items.head: Inactive despite Spears' absence
items.body: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Week 11 marks the fifth time in six games that Singleton will be a healthy scratch, despite the fact that Tyjae Spears (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. As such, Michael Carter and Julius Chestnut will operate as the Titans' rotational options in the backfield behind workhorse running back Tony Pollard on Sunday. Singleton's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Nov. 29.

items.head: Nicholas Singleton (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Could see role grow in second half
items.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that Singleton is "getting better," and the rookie running back could be a candidate to see added opportunities in the second half of the season if lead back Tony Pollard is dealt ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports. A fifth-round pick out of Penn State, Singleton was a healthy inactive for four of the Titans' first eight games prior to a Week 9 bye and has logged more snaps on special teams than offense thus far during his rookie season. However, with the 29-year-old Pollard set to become a free agent after the season and likely not part of the 1-7 Titans' rebuilding effort, playing time could become up for grabs in the backfield if Tennessee receives an appealing trade offer for the veteran. Along with Singleton, Tyjae Spears (knee) and Michael Carter would be vying for reps in the event Pollard is traded, while Julius Chestnut is another option in the backfield but has been utilized almost exclusively on special teams.

items.head: Active in Week 11
items.body: Wilson (hand/finger) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles. The third-year wideout was activated from injured reserve Saturday, foreshadowing his availability for Sunday's contest following a four-game absence. Wilson recorded at least three receptions in his first four games of the season on his way to a 14-188-2 line on 25 targets, and he then failed to reel in his only target in Week 5 against the Colts before exiting that game at halftime with his injury. In his return Sunday against Philadelphia, Wilson should slot into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, the latter who leapfrogged Wilson on the depth chart over the last several games while filling in for both him and Michael Pittman (IR, foot).

items.head: Roman Wilson (Hand) is Questionable
items.body: Wilson (finger) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Another full practice
items.body: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over the last handful of games to retain a notable role in the Steelers' receiving corps.

items.head: Cleared to practice Wednesday
items.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Wilson (finger) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. McCarthy suggested earlier in the week that Wilson could be cleared to play Sunday in Philadelphia, and the Steelers' decision to open the wideout's 21-day practice window is the first step in him potentially playing for the first time since Week 5. Through the Steelers' first five games of the season, Wilson recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 25 targets, but it's not clear where exactly he'll settle in the pecking order at receiver once healthy. Like Wilson, veteran wideout Michael Pittman (foot) had his 21-day window opened Wednesday and could be on a similar timeline for a return. Additionally, rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard has proven to be a reliable target for Aaron Rodgers in the short and intermediate areas of the field over the past few weeks and could maintain a notable role once Wilson and Pittman are back in the fold.

items.head: Roman Wilson (Finger) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he's "hopeful" Wilson (finger) will be able to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.

items.head: Active in Week 11
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is listed as active Sunday versus the Buccaneers. Vaki has been tending to an ankle issue for three weeks running, but he's still suited up on the previous two occasions, combining for nine carries for 42 yards (4.7 YPC) and three catches (on three targets) for 19 yards. With active status confirmed for Week 11, he'll continue to serve as a complement to No. 1 RB Jahmyr Gibbs.

items.head: Listed questionable
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers. If Vaki is unable to play against Tampa Bay, Jacob Saylors would move up to RB2 status, but Jahmyr Gibbs would have a chance to see an even bigger share of the backfield opportunities in that scenario.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Vaki (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. A limited participant for Wednesday's walkthrough, Vaki continued to operate with some restrictions while the Lions held a more traditional practice Thursday. Vaki's involvement in any capacity is nonetheless a good sign for his Week 11 status, though he may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

items.head: Limited during Wednesday's practice
items.body: Vaki (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice. Vaki has been listed on Lions injury reports over the past two weeks due to the lingering ankle issue, but it hasn't kept him from playing in either contest. With the Lions running away with a 25-point win over the Patriots in Munich in Week 10, Vaki saw more work than usual behind lead back Jahmyr Gibbs, finishing with six carries for 28 yards and a 17-yard reception.

items.head: Accumulates 45 yards in Week 10 win
items.body: Vaki turned six carries into 28 yards and added a 17-yard catch on his only target during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. Lead back Jahmyr Gibbs dominated with 252 yards and three touchdowns on 29 total touches (22 carries, seven catches on eight targets), but Vaki also had his moments during Sunday's game, including a 17-yard catch on the first play of the second quarter. Vaki was working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep before being cleared to play, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield behind Gibbs. Through eight regular-season games, Vaki has turned 36 carries into 163 yards (4.5 YPC) and eight catches on nine targets for 81 yards. The Lions will be at home for three of their next four games, starting with Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

items.head: Suiting up in Week 10
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich. Vaki is playing through an ankle issue for a second straight contest, but last Sunday at Miami he was able to handle an above average 34 percent snap share, indicating he again is good to serve as Jahmyr Gibbs' top backup. On the season, such a workload has amounted to 37 touches for 199 yards from scrimmage and no TDs in eight appearances for Vaki.

items.head: Deemed questionable for Week 10
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports. Vaki played through the same injury last week, taking five touches for 21 yards in a 19-9 win over the Dolphins. He didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday this week, but a return to practice Friday puts him on track to avoid the inactive list ahead of Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. If Vaki doesn't end up playing, Jacob Saylors will step into the No. 2 RB role behind workhorse Jahmyr Gibbs.

items.head: Active for Week 9
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Miami. Vaki didn't practice Friday, resulting in a questionable tag for Week 9. However, he will be out there against the Dolphins and may continue to be more involved after totaling 11 carries in the Week 8 win over the Vikings.

items.head: Suiting up in Week 11
items.body: Tremble (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports. Tremble opened Week 11 prep as a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, which he followed up with limited sessions Thursday and Friday and a questionable tag for Sunday. The same can be said for fellow TE Darren Waller (knee), and both now are available to the Panthers offense. In nine outings this season, Tremble has compiled a 25-227-3 line on 35 targets.

items.head: Tommy Tremble (injury) is Active
items.body: Tremble (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Both Tremble and Darren Waller (knee) were upgraded to limited work after being DNP on Wednesday. Friday's participation levels and injury designations will tell a better story for their Week 11 availability versus Baltimore. Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are next in line at tight end for Carolina.

items.head: Managing knee issue in Week 11
items.body: Tremble didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, with head coach Dave Canales noting after the session that the tight end's injury is a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports. Canales said the same about Darren Waller (knee), who was also a non-participant to open Week 11 prep. The practice activity of the Panthers' top two tight ends will thus warrant monitoring over the next two days to get a sense if either player will be available to play Sunday versus the Ravens. Beyond Tremble and Waller, the Panthers have three other tight ends -- Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders -- on the 53-man roster.

items.head: Tommy Tremble (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Four catches in Week 10 win
items.body: Tremble caught four of five targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. The tight end's five targets tie Chuba Hubbard for second on the team behind Tetairoa McMillan's seven. Tremble has yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, and his four catches matched his season high. More of a blocker and red-zone specialist, Tremble has very little fantasy appeal in a Carolina offense that likes to use three tight ends.

items.head: Four grabs, TD in loss to Denver
items.body: Tremble caught four of six targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.

items.head: AJ Dillon (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Good to go Sunday
items.body: Schoonmaker (illness) is active for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against Tennessee. Schoonmaker was unable to practice Thursday or Friday because he was under the weather, but the tight end appears to be feeling well enough to suit up Sunday. Meanwhile, Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) will miss his second straight game, opening the door for Schoonmaker to potentially log a larger workload than usual on offense. With Ferguson out last Sunday versus San Francisco, Schoonmaker posted a season-high 35 percent offensive snap share and caught one of two targets for 12 yards.

items.head: Easton Stick (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Gets bumped up from practice squad
items.body: The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports. Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who had been out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

items.head: Audric Estime (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.

items.head: Rough day against Panthers
items.body: Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina. Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

items.head: Backfield role shrinking for Week 10
items.body: Estime's role in the backfield will likely be diminished after Travis Etienne (hamstring) was cleared to return for Sunday's game against the Panthers. Estime -- who the Saints claimed off waivers from the Browns on Nov. 3 -- turned 15 carries into 72 yards and a touchdown while logging a five-yard catch during New Orleans' 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland in Week 9. He split backfield duties with Alvin Kamara in that contest, but both running backs figure to have their snaps reduced due to the return of Etienne on Sunday.

items.head: Makes splash in New Orleans debut
items.body: Estime carried the ball 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also caught his only target for five yards. It was a revenge game for the third-year RB, who was cut loose by Cleveland last week and got claimed on waivers by New Orleans to offer some depth for a depleted backfield. Estime played for the Saints in 2025 and didn't need to learn Kellen Moore's playbook, putting him in prime position to step into a big role right away, and he led the team with 16 touches ahead of Alvin Kamara's nine. Estime capped his big performance with a two-yard TD run in the fourth quarter. While he certainly made a case for a consistent role in the offense, rookie CJ Donaldson (shoulder) could be back next week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) might be close to returning from IR. Estime could still be atop the depth chart, at least temporarily, for a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

items.head: Scooped up by Saints
items.body: The Saints claimed Estime off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday. New Orleans released kicker Daniel Carlson to clear room on the 53-man roster for Estime, who began the season with the Saints before being cut on an injury settlement Sept. 22. After moving past a thigh injury, Estime caught on with the Browns and made his lone appearance for the team back in Week 6, when he carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Ravens. Upon rejoining the Saints, Estime will provide depth to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara, Kendre MIller and CJ Donaldson (shoulder).

items.head: Cleared to return for Week 11
items.body: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh. Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

items.head: Will Shipley (injury) is Active
items.body: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.

items.head: Activated from IR
items.body: The Eagles activated Shipley (foot) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers. Shipley logged an LP/LP/DNP practice regimen during Week 11 prep, with Friday's absence attributed to an illness. He appears to be closing in on his first game action since Week 5, when he suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia, but his status for Sunday's matchup won't be confirmed until about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Assuming Shipley returns to action this weekend, he may serve as the direct backup to top RB Saquon Barkley.

items.head: Will Shipley (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Officially limited Wednesday
items.body: Shipley (foot) was a limited practice participant Wednesday. Shipley sustained a partial tear of his plantar fascia in Week 5 against the Jaguars in London, resulting in an IR stint. He missed the last four games before a Week 10 bye before the Eagles designated him for return Monday. No. 1 RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) practiced fully Wednesday, so if Shipley gains clearance to play Sunday versus the Steelers, it'll likely be in a complementary role out of the backfield.

items.head: Practice window being opened
items.body: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday. Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If he's able to suit up this weekend, Shipley would reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

items.body: Waller (knee) is listed as active Sunday against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.

items.head: Present for practice Friday
items.body: Waller (knee) is practicing again Friday, Joseph Person of The Athletic reports. The same applies to fellow TE Tommy Tremble (knee), with both players having logged limited practices Thursday after being deemed 'DNPs' a day earlier. The Panthers' upcoming Friday injury report will clarify the duo's game statuses heading into the weekend. Waller is coming off a two-catch, 24-yard effort on four targets in Week 10 versus the Saints, but the week prior he put up an 8/90/1 receiving line on 10 targets versus the Broncos.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN reports.

items.head: Practicing Thursday
items.body: Waller (knee) is suited up for Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Head coach Dave Canales called knee injuries for Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble concerning when they didn't practice Wednesday, but both players returned to drills one day later. Ultimately, Thursday's injury report will reveal their respective activity levels.

items.head: DNP due to knee injury
items.body: Waller didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, and afterward head coach Dave Canales called the tight end's injury a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports. The Panthers' top two tight ends in Waller and Tommy Tremble (knee) showed up as DNPs to begin Week 11 prep, and Canales' "concern" comment also extended to Tremble. It's unclear if either of both are in danger of missing Sunday's game against the Ravens, but Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are the healthy TEs on Carolina's active roster.

items.head: Darren Waller (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Waller didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, and afterward head coach Dave Canales called the tight end's injury a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Two catches in Week 10
items.body: Waller caught two of four targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. One week after his 8-90-1 receiving outburst, Waller came back to normalcy in the Panthers' three-man committee at tight end. Waller has big upside, but his ceiling games are difficult to predict. He's been held below 40 yards with no touchdowns in five of nine games this season. Waller will be a low-floor TE2 with upside for Week 11 against the Ravens.

items.head: Leading receiver in Week 9 loss
items.body: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.

If the tight end is limited or unavailable, Buffalo could have to lean more on DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in the middle of the field, while Dawson Knox, Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu would handle tight-end duties.

items.body: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice Wednesday, David Furones of the Sun Sentinel reports.

items.head: Gains 58 yards on three targets
items.body: Kincaid caught two of three targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Kincaid contributed catches of four and 54 yards to finish second on the team in receiving yards behind DJ Moore (90). The 2023 first-round pick has seen his usage fluctuate throughout the campaign, as Kincaid has failed to exceed three targets on five occasions but has drawn at least six looks from Josh Allen in each of the other four games. Kincaid is making the most of his opportunities for a second consecutive regular season, averaging 11.9 yards per target in 2026 after leading all qualified TEs with 11.7 YPT in 2025. Next up for Kincaid is a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

items.body: Kincaid (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.

items.body: Tate (shoulder) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.body: Tate (shoulder), who was a full participant in Friday's practice, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Earlier Friday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site relayed that coach Robert Saleh said Tate had a really good week, noting that the WR had a moment during Thursday's session when he made a diving catch, landed on shoulder, and was able to get up without any problem.

items.head: Faces uncertain status Sunday
items.body: Bowers (ankle) said Friday that his availability for Sunday's game against the Broncos remains up in the air, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "We still have some conversations to have, so we'll see," Bowers said. With the tight end already slated to carry a questionable tag into the weekend, his own comments don't provide added clarity about whether he'll suit up Sunday. The Raiders may wait until closer to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff before making a final call on Bowers' status. Jack Bech was the big winner in terms of playing time and targets after Bowers left last Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

items.head: Listed as questionable versus Denver
items.body: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end will nonetheless head into the weekend with a 'questionable' designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 pm ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer would merit fantasy lineup consideration while facing 7-2 Denver.

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Bowers (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. After not practicing Wednesday, Bowers logged a limited session Thursday, and the tight end's presence on the field again Friday offers hope that he'll be able to give it a go Sunday against the Broncos. Per Warren, Bowers sported a wrap on his injured right ankle Friday, with his official participation level/game status set to arrive once the Raiders' Week 11 injury report comes out later in the day.

items.head: Out at least six weeks, per Rapoport

items.head: Patriots QB Drake Maye has fractured fibula, sources say
items.body: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has a fractured right fibula, and receiver A.J. Brown has a hamstring injury, sources told ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter.

items.head: Out indefinitely with fractured fibula
items.body: Maye has suffered a fractured right fibula that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him for some time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

items.head: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
items.body: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.

items.head: Not expected to be available in Week 12, per Vrabel
items.body: Coach Mike Vrabel noted of Maye (ankle) on Monday, "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.

items.head: Ankle fracture feared
items.body: The the Patriots are concerned that it's possible Maye fractured his ankle in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Could be dealing with significant lower-leg inury
items.body: Maye is believed to have sustained a significant lower-leg injury that could sideline him for an extended period of time, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reports. Maye, who was forced out of Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich with what the Patriots at the time reported as an ankle injury, is slated to seek additional medical information, with Rapoport suggesting that it's even possible the QB will miss the rest of the season. In the event that he does miss time following New England's Week 11 bye, Tommy DeVito -- who replaced Maye on Sunday -- and Behren Morton are currently next in line for the team's signal-caller snaps. Moreover, while the NFL trade deadline has come and gone, it's still possible that the Patriots could explore options at the position via other team's practice squads or by considering one of the remaining available veteran free agents.

items.head: Confirmed starter for Week 11
items.body: Johnson will start for the Cardinals on Sunday against the Chiefs due to the absence of Carson Beck (back), Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. Beck popped up on Thursday's injury report due to back spasms, and the injury is severe enough for the rookie third-round quarterback to be inactive for Sunday's game. It will be Johnson's 12th career NFL start since entering the league in 2008 as a fifth-round pick of the Buccaneers, and he has a 2-9 record heading into Week 11. He started in each of the final two games of the 2025 regular season for Washington, when he completed 64.4 percent of his passes for 329 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning 11 carries into 55 yards and a score.

items.head: Cardinals rule out rookie Carson Beck, turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson vs. Chiefs
items.body: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to start against the Chiefs.

items.head: Expected to start Sunday
items.body: Johnson is expected to start Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. With Carson Beck (back) not expected to practice Friday or play Sunday, Johnson appears in line to step into the starting quarterback role for Arizona. Johnson has a career 14:18 TD:INT across 50 regular-season appearances. The entire Arizona offense is one to avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions for Week 11.

items.head: Unlikely to play in 2026
items.body: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Saturday that he doesn't anticipate Musgrove (neck) returning from the PUP list this season, according to NFL reporter Jason B. Hirschhorn. LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

items.head: Deemed day-to-day by Harbaugh
items.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

items.head: Sources: Ex-Colts QB Daniel Jones likely to wait before signing with new team
items.body: If Daniel Jones clear waivers and becomes a free agent, the QB is unlikely to sign immediately, preferring to wait for the right opportunity, sources said.

items.head: Being let go by Indianapolis
items.body: Jones will be waived by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Following Thursday's loss to Houston, James Boyd of The Athletic relayed that Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that he planned to "evaluate everything" in terms of the team's QB situation going forward. Now, as a result of Friday's decision, the team's new starter ahead of Week 12 action is Anthony Richardson, per Schefter. Jones -- who is subject to waivers, but would become  a free agent if unclaimed by Monday -- will now look for a job elsewhere, and despite his struggles this season, he figures to find a new team relatively quickly, given the signal-caller injury issues that exist around the league.

items.head: Another forgettable performance in loss
items.body: Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed once for three yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday before being replaced by Anthony Richardson with 7:51 remaining. Jones' final line underscores how ineffective he was for the fifth straight game, once again finishing well under 200 passing yards and extending his streak of games with at least one interception to six. Although the 3-8 Colts don't have any realistic designs on the postseason, James Boyd of The Athletic reports Colts head coach Shane Steichen said "I'll evaluate everything" when asked if he'd consider benching Jones ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Forgettable numbers in win
items.body: Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while adding five carries for nine yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.

items.head: Citing short week, Colts sticking with Daniel Jones at QB despite dreadful start
items.body: Colts coach Shane Steichen said the team will stick with Daniel Jones as starter despite a two-interception start that earned him a 2026-worst 1.7 QBR.

items.head: RB Jonathan Taylor, QB Daniel Jones remain with Colts as trade deadline passes
items.body: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor and QB Daniel Jones were the subject of trade overtures in recent days and weeks but were not traded before Tuesday's trade deadline.

items.head: Pedestrian numbers in loss
items.body: Jones completed 20 of 34 passes for 180 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding three rushes for 11 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. Jones took a pair of sacks and averaged a modest 5.3 yards per attempt in what would have to be termed a disappointing performance overall considering the struggles the Cowboys defense had endured. Jones' one touchdown pass came on a 55-yard catch-and-run off a wide receiver screen by Ashton Dulin late in the third quarter. Jones has now failed to eclipse 180 passing yards in three straight games while also tossing six interceptions over his last four contests, and reports emerged late in the week that the Colts were fielding calls from multiple teams about a potential trade for the veteran signal-caller before Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Questionable for Week 11
items.body: Mayfield (foot/thumb) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Detroit. Mayfield came out of the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye with a foot injury that sidelined him at Wednesday's practice. He proceeded to be a limited participant Thursday and Friday, and after the latter session, head coach Todd Bowles told Scott Smith of the team's official site that Mayfield "looked good" and is trending toward starting Sunday. Ultimately, Mayfield's status for Week 11 will be confirmed about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.head: Trending toward Sunday start
items.body: Mayfield (foot) is trending in the right direction to start Sunday's game against the Lions after looking good in Friday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. With Mayfield back on the field again Friday after managing the foot issue earlier this week, Tampa Bay appears to be gaining optimism about its starting quarterback's availability for Sunday's matchup. His official game designation for Sunday still will be key, but coach Todd Bowles' comments point toward Mayfield having a chance to avoid another absence.

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Mayfield (foot) is practicing again Friday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. With Mayfield having progressed from sitting out Wednesday to being limited Thursday, Friday's participation is another positive sign for his availability Sunday against Detroit. The Buccaneers' upcoming injury report is destined to reveal both Mayfield's participation level Friday, as well as his Week 11 game status.

items.body: As he manages the whirlwind of his professional and personal life this month, Vikings QB Kirk Cousins has relied on a maxim he often heard from his college coach Mark D'Antonio at Michigan State -- when things speed up, try to slow down.

items.head: Gets questionable tag
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers will make a decision on Evans' (Achilles) Week 11 status Saturday after listing the wide receiver as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of ESPN.com reports. Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status until about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.head: Sidelined for months
items.body: Coach Sean McVay revealed Friday that Nacua (knee) had surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday and is on track to miss a couple of months, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Given that timetable, Nacua -- who already is on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, which is a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In Nacua's continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12 following the team's bye.

items.body: Croskey-Merritt (groin) is trending toward playing in Monday night's game against the Bengals, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Wants to play Monday
items.body: Croskey-Merritt (groin) said Friday he's taking things "day by day," but his goal is to play Monday against the Bengals, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Croskey-Merritt remains on injured reserve, meaning he'll need to be activated by Monday afternoon to have a chance to return in Week 11. Considering he logged full practices Thursday and Friday, he's on track to do so, and if he's able to suit up, he'll rejoin a backfield currently composed of Rachaad White (heel, limited Friday) and Austin Ekeler.

items.head: Full practice Thursday
items.body: Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt for return from injured reserve Tuesday, and in the team's first official practice of Week 11 prep, he was uninhibited. Assuming he's able to maintain that activity level Friday and Saturday, he's a good bet to miss the minimum four games on IR due to the groin injury that bothered him multiple weeks through the first five contests of the campaign.

items.head: Back at practice Thursday
items.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Croskey-Merritt (groin) will practice Thursday, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports. Washington opened Croskey-Merritt's 21-day evaluation window two days earlier, but he'll take part in his first practice Thursday since landing on injured reserve Oct. 19. Per Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C., Quinn said that Croskey-Merritt is considered fully recovered from his groin injury, but the Commanders want to see how he responds to football activity over the course of the team's three practices this week before deciding his next step. If Croskey-Merritt is able to practice fully by Saturday and checks out well from a physical standpoint, he could be reinstated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals.

items.head: Cleared to resume practicing
items.body: The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt (groin) for return from injured reserve Tuesday.

items.head: Trending in right direction, per coach
items.body: Coach Dan Quinn said Monday that while the 21-day practice window for Croskey-Merritt (groin) hasn't been opened yet, he notes that the running back is "trending in the right direction," Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Comfortably outpaced by Corum and Rivers
items.body: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Bottled up by Commanders
items.body: Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington. Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

items.head: Rushing touchdown in Week 8 win
items.body: Williams rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown and brought in his sole target for three yards in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday. Williams had a difficult time finding running room against a game Chargers defense, but he salvaged his fantasy day with a one-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Williams has five of his six rushing scores on the season in the last four games, and he's still averaging a robust 4.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

items.head: Unlikely to play Monday
items.body: Iosivas (thumb) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Commanders. Iosivas was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but it looks like the fourth-year wide receiver will stay on injured reserve for at least one more week while recovering from a thumb injury. If he's inactive for Monday's game, then his next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Won't return for Week 10
items.body: Iosivas (thumb) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Steelers. Iosivas was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Steelers despite logging full practices Thursday and Friday. He'll remain on IR for at least one more game, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

items.head: Set to return to practice
items.body: Iosivas (thumb) was cleared to return to practice Thursday. Iosivas, who landed on IR on Sept. 26, is bouncing back from surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, and the wideout's looming return to Thursday's practice has him trending the right direction ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers. Once he's back in action, Iosivas will slot back in behind top WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, a role that doesn't typically yield steady volume.

items.head: Not ruled out for Week 10
items.body: Head coach Zac Taylor said Monday that Iosivas is doing well in his recovery from left thumb surgery, and the Bengals will "continue to work through this week" to determine when the receiver might return from injured reserve, Laurel Pfahler of the Dayton Daily News reports. Cincinnati has yet to open Iosivas' 21-day practice window since he landed on IR on Sept. 26, so until that happens, the wideout's return to game action shouldn't be considered imminent. While Iosivas has been sidelined for the Bengals' past six games, Dohnte Meyers has been serving as the primary No. 3 wideout behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and tight end Mike Gesicki has also benefited from an expanded profile in the passing attack.

items.head: Good to go against Cincinnati
items.body: Burks (foot) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals. Burks was held out of Friday's practice while managing a foot injury, but he returned Saturday as a full participant, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Monday's contest. Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6 against the 49ers.

items.head: DNP on Friday
items.body: Burks (foot) did not practice Friday. The Commanders have been managing Burks' practice reps, as he deals with a foot injury that's been nagging him for several weeks. He missed practice time last week but still was able to play against the Giants last Thursday, securing two of three targets for 27 yards. Washington will provide final injury designations Saturday ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

items.head: Treylon Burks (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: Burks (foot) did not practice Friday.

items.head: Logs two catches in return from foot injury
items.body: Burks caught two of three targets for 27 yards Thursday in a 24-21 win over the Giants. Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production given their higher spots in the pecking order.

items.head: Cleared for TNF
items.body: Burks (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Giants. Despite logging DNPs Monday and Wednesday, Burks is good to go after getting in a limited session Tuesday. He missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams but figures to return to his role in three-wide sets alongside rookie Antonio Williams and veteran slot man Stefon Diggs, which would push Van Jefferson down the depth chart after he popped up for 5-58-1 receiving against Los Angeles. Burks has produced seven catches for 147 yards on 11 targets over his last two games with Terry McLaurin (knee) sidelined.

items.head: Upgrades to limited activity
items.body: Burks (foot) was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice. After sitting out the Commanders' Week 9 loss to the Rams, Burks was listed as a non-participant to kick off Week 10 prep but was able to take a step forward in terms of activity during Tuesday's session. The wideout's availability for Thursday's game against the Giants remains murky, but if he's able to turn in another limited practice Wednesday, he'll stand a good chance at taking a questionable tag into the contest. Burks has drawn exactly five targets in each of his last three appearances, and he could end up holding down a top-three role in the Commanders' wideout corps for the rest of the season while Washington is without Terry McLaurin (knee).

items.head: Estimated as DNP on Monday
items.body: Burks (foot) was deemed a non-participant on the Commanders' practice report Monday, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Washington didn't actually practice Monday, so Burks' participation -- or lack thereof -- Tuesday should be more useful in providing insight into the wideout's chance of suiting up Thursday against the Giants. Burks didn't play this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams after sitting out practice all of last week. Terry McLaurin (knee) is out for the season, and Dyami Brown (calf) landed on IR on Saturday, so Burks will likely have a prominent role in the Commanders' passing game Sunday if he's able to suit up.

items.head: Cut by San Francisco
items.body: The 49ers waived Cooks on Saturday. The impending return of Mike Evans (Achilles), coupled with the 49ers acquisition of Keenan Allen at the trade deadline, resulted in no room on the roster for Cooks, who was a healthy inactive for Week 10 against the Cowboys. Cooks will now go on waivers, and if he goes unclaimed, then he would have the opportunity to sign with a team in need of veteran depth at wide receiver. He has five catches on 10 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

items.body: Cooks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

items.head: Tallies two catches against Las Vegas
items.body: Cooks brought in both of his targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense would decrease if one or both of Evans or Samuel was cleared to return.

items.head: Dontayvion Wicks (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Eagles placed Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve Saturday.

items.head: Dontayvion Wicks (Ankle) is Out
items.body: Wicks (ankle/foot) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. As was fellow WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who worked fully Thursday. Wicks -- who last played in Week 6 -- has logged consecutive 'LPs' thus far this week, but if he upgrades to full participation Friday he'd be positioned to head into Sunday's game against the Steelers without an injury designation.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday. Wicks is seeking his first game action since Week 6 due to an ankle injury, and he still has some work to do after kicking off Week 11 prep with back-to-back capped sessions. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to play Sunday versus the Steelers.

items.head: Practicing Thursday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) is participating in practice Thursday, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports. Wicks now has logged back-to-back practices to begin Week 11 prep, with his activity level to become known once the Eagles post an injury report Thursday. He practiced in a limited fashion Wednesday, which marked his first on-field work since Week 6.

items.head: Practices in limited fashion
items.body: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday. Wicks was sidelined by an ankle issue in Weeks 7-9, but a Week 10 bye has him trending toward a return to action after getting back on the practice field Wednesday. Friday's injury report will reveal his odds to suit up Sunday against the Steelers.

items.head: Practicing Wednesday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) participated in Wednesday's practice, Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports. Wicks is taking his first on-field reps since Week 6 prep, as he's been sidelined in the meantime due to an ankle injury. Following a Week 10 bye, head coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday that he feels good about Wicks' chances to return to action Sunday against the Steelers, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Ultimately, how Wicks fares in drills Wednesday through Friday will determine if he's cleared ahead of the weekend.

items.head: Could be back this week
items.body: Coach Nick Sirianni relayed Wednesday that he feels good about the chances of Wicks (ankle) returning to action Sunday against the Steelers, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.

items.head: Elevated from practice squad
items.body: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. The move gives the Jets much-needed depth at wide receiver given the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. It will be the third elevation of the season for Shepard and first since Week 4 against the Bears, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Jets beyond Week 11.

items.head: Officially ruled out
items.body: Beck (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Cardinals QB Carson Beck dealing with back spasms; Josh Johnson may start
items.body: The Cardinals are preparing veteran quarterback Josh Johnson to start Sunday vs. the Chiefs as rookie Carson Beck deals with back spasms, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday.

items.head: Questionable for Sunday
items.body: Beck (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. Beck showed up on the Cardinals' Week 11 injury report Thursday as limited due to back spasms that have flared up, per Darren Urban of the team's official site. Beck then didn't practice Friday, but Arizona still is giving him a chance to play Sunday. If Beck isn't able to go, though, Josh Johnson is lined up to be under center in his place.

items.head: Won't practice Friday
items.body: Beck (back) will not practice Friday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. After being listed as limited Thursday, Beck's looming absence from Friday's practice -- the result of back spasms flaring up -- per Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site, clouds his status for Sunday's game at Kansas City. For now, coach Mike LaFleur said the team will proceed as if Josh Johnson will make the start at quarterback, though the door hasn't been completely closed on the possibility of Beck being available. It's a situation to avoid in most fantasy formats.

items.head: Limited by back injury
items.body: Beck was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report due to a back issue, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Cards rookie QB Beck struggles in debut, but keeps optimism
items.body: Beck faced Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett in his first game, and it wasn't easy.

items.head: Throws two picks in NFL debut
items.body: Beck was 11-for-18 passing for 108 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions and had one rush for one yard during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens after Week 8, and then Gardner Minshew tore the UCL in his right elbow in Week 9, setting the stage for the first appearance (a start) of Beck's career. Beck, a rookie third-rounder, generated just two drives of 30-plus yards among his nine possession overall, and two others ended in interceptions in Rams territory. He also didn't find much success with his top available skill-position talent, TE Trey McBride, who gathered in all five of his targets for 37 yards. They'll look to improve their rapport next Sunday in Kansas City.

items.head: Tyjae Spears (Knee) is Injured Reserve
items.body: ir

items.head: Questionable despite full practice
items.body: Spears (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Dallas. The running back practiced fully Friday, so he should be good to go for Sunday's contest after he returned from a two-game absence last week against the Jaguars to play 16 snaps behind Tony Pollard. Spears is a desperation fantasy play in a week with six teams on bye.

items.head: Back to limited practice
items.body: Spears (knee) was limited in practice Thursday. The running back returned to action last Sunday against the Jaguars and logged 16 snaps behind Tony Pollard's 41. Spears is only playable in Week 11 against Dallas as a desperation fantasy option.

items.head: Sits out Wednesday's practice
items.body: Spears (knee) didn't practice Wednesday. Spears has been regularly listed with a knee issue on Titans injury reports dating back to Week 6, but he was able to put an end to a two-game absence in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars and finished with four carries for 28 yards to go with one reception for no gain. The Titans haven't indicated that Spears experienced a setback with his knee coming out of that game, so it's possible that his absence from practice to kick off Week 11 prep may be maintenance-related. Spears' activity over the next two days should help determine his status for Sunday's game in Dallas.

items.head: Five touches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He turned one catch into zero yards on one target. After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Spears returned to play 16 offensive snaps. Tony Pollard (41 snaps) remains the clear-cut lead back on this cellar-dwelling Tennessee team. Spears has minimal fantasy appeal now that Pollard survived the trade deadline and will finish out the season with the Titans.

items.head: Cleared to return for Week 10
items.body: Spears (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. After entering the weekend listed as questionable, Spears has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a knee injury. Nick Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's AFC South tilt, so Spears and Julius Chestnut will serve as the Titans' backfield depth options behind RB1 Tony Pollard.

items.head: On track to return Sunday
items.body: Spears (knee) is expected to play Sunday against the Jaguars, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Spears, who hasn't played since Week 6, advanced from a 'DNP' on Wednesday to a limited session Thursday, before working fully Friday and being listed as questionable heading into the weekend. His looming return would provide a boost the Titans' Week 10 RB depth, but prior to his injury, Spears' fantasy impact was modest, with 18 carries for 66 yards and 15 catches for 75 yards on 17 targets in six contests.

items.head: Upgrades to limited Thursday
items.body: Spears (knee) was a limited participant at practice Thursday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. Spears worked out on a side field for at least part of Thursday's practice, per Turron Davenport of ESPN.com, which is a step in the right direction after Spears didn't practice Wednesday. Tony Pollard (finger/rest) didn't practice Thursday, but with Tennessee's coaching staff suggesting that rookie Nicholas Singleton could start to get more involved moving forward, Spears is unlikely to handle more than a handful of touches even if the latter gets the green light for his first action since Week 6.

items.head: Expected to play Monday
items.body: White (heel) is trending toward being available for Monday's game against the Bengals, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.

items.head: Not spotted at Saturday's practice
items.body: White (heel) was not on the field during the opening portion of Saturday's practice session, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Limited by heel issue
items.body: White was limited at Friday's practice due to a heel injury. White was tacked on to the Commanders' Week 11 practice report Friday, joining Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), who has been a full participant this week but remains on injured reserve. It adds another question mark to the team's backfield situation ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals, and Saturday's injury report will reveal the odds of both players to suit up in the coming days.

items.head: Rachaad White (Heel) is Questionable
items.body: White was limited at Friday's practice due to a heel injury.

items.head: Leads backfield in win
items.body: White rushed 11 times for 47 yards and brought in one of two targets for five yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

items.head: Finds little running room in Week 9 loss
items.body: White carried the ball seven times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. The 28 rushing yards led the Commanders on the afternoon, although Austin Ekeler saw one more carry than White did. With jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) set to miss at least one more contest while on IR, White seems likely to lead the backfield again in Week 10 against the Giants. Over the three games Croskey-Merritt has been sidelined so far, White has produced 186 scrimmage yards and two TDs, one rushing and one receiving, while averaging 4.4 yards per carry.

items.head: Steps up late as team's top RB
items.body: White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for five yards in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Eagles. Most of White's production came during a three-play span on Washington's final possession, as he ripped off a 33-yard run down to the four-yard line, followed by a three-yard gain and a one-yard touchdown run to put the game out of reach. The Commanders have divided up backfield duties while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is on IR, as Austin Ekeler notched eight carries, while Jeremy McNichols (foot) had five carries and one catch prior to exiting in the second half. White continues to have the highest touch floor among Washington's available running backs heading into Week 9 against the Rams, and he has scored in three of the last four games, with the previous two touchdowns both coming on receptions.

items.head: Still viewed as Jets' top backfield option
items.body: Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday that Hall could see a bump in touches for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Howie Kussoy of the New York Post reports. "Obviously, [Hall] and Garrett Wilson are guys that we really try to target for the most part...Hall will end up getting a tick more [touches] because, again, he's our starting running back," Glenn said Friday. In his two outings since returning from a five-game absence due to a quad injury, Hall has turned 26 carries into 102 yards (3.9 YPC) while catching seven of eight passes for 93 yards, and he topped 100 scrimmage yards against the Bills in Week 10. Braelon Allen has reverted to RB2 duties in Hall's return, but the former has still been efficient with his touches, and the duo will face a Chargers defense Sunday that ranks 15th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (110.2) and limited Derrick Henry to 10 yards on 10 carries (albeit with two touchdowns) in a 23-20 win over the Ravens in Week 10.

items.head: In line to start in Week 12
items.body: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that DeVito will start in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29, Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN report. Drake Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, which he sustained in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich. DeVito filled in for the rest of that contest and completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning four carries into 19 yards. It appears he will be New England's starter coming out of the bye, with rookie seventh-rounder Behren Morton operating as the backup. However, the Patriots have emerged as a team reportedly interested in the services of Daniel Jones, who was released by the Colts on Friday and available on waivers until 4:00 p.m. ET on Monday.

items.head: Could continue to fill in for Maye
items.body: Mike Reiss of ESPN notes via ESPN's Adam Schefter that there are fears  DeVito's teammate, Drake Maye, may have sustained a fractured ankle during Week 10 action.

items.head: Forced into action in Munich
items.body: DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. He added 19 yards on four carries.

items.head: Two catches in loss
items.body: Dulin caught two of his four targets for 30 yards and assisted two tackles on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.

items.head: Hauls in 30-yard catch vs. Miami
items.body: Dulin caught one of two targets for 30 yards and returned three kickoffs for 77 yards during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles on special teams. Even with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being sent out at the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Dulin's 13 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Colts wide receivers behind Laquon Treadwell (52), Deion Burks (34) and Anthony Gould (32). Dulin did connect on a 30-yard pass from Daniel Jones on a 30-yard pass late in the second quarter, which was a pivotal part of the Colts' nine-play, 92-yard drive that ended with a seven-yard touchdown catch by Treadwell. Dulin has logged catches of 55 and 30 yards in each of his last two outings, and he could be the Colts' WR3 for Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Texans if Gould is not cleared to play due to a toe injury.

items.head: Will help fill in for departed Allen
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Dulin will be one of the Colts receivers who absorb the snaps vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports. Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.
