items.head: Back at practice again, Bengals QB Burrow optimistic he'll be at full strength
items.body: A full participant at practice for the second straight day despite the bug that he has battled, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is optimistic that he'll be at full strength when Cincinnati plays the Washington Commanders on "Monday Night Football."

items.head: Expects to be full strength for MNF
items.body: Burrow (illness) said Friday that he's getting better, noting that he "for sure" feels optimistic he'll be at full strength for Monday night's game against the Commanders, Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer reports. Burrow is managing what the Bengals list as an illness, but the QB was a full participant in Thursday's practice, and is trending toward approaching Monday night's game without a Week 11 designation. Official confirmation of that expected outcome will arrive Saturday, either way.

items.head: Turns in full practice Thursday
items.body: Burrow (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Joe Burrow's 4-TD effort puts him in company of Tom Brady, Peyton Manning
items.body: Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday night, becoming just the third player in NFL history after Tom Brady and Peyton Manning to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span.

items.head: Record-tying performance in win
items.body: Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added one rush for eight yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night.

items.head: Sportsbook liability Joe Burrow overtakes Josh Allen as NFL MVP favorite
items.body: Bengals QB Joe Burrow has overtaken Bills star Josh Allen as the betting favorite for NFL MVP honors, a development that could prove costly for sportsbooks.

items.head: Joe Burrow reaching new heights as Bengals face big test
items.body: Burrow led the Bengals to their fourth straight win, and AFC North rival Pittsburgh is on deck.

items.head: Another stellar effort in Week 9 win
items.body: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries. It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

items.head: Shifting to WR2 in Smith's return
items.body: Lemon will operate as the Eagles' WR2 against the Steelers on Sunday due to the return of DeVonta Smith (hamstring). Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former will still be heavily involved in the offensive gameplan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. Joe Milton is getting the start at quarterback for a second straight game, and the Eagles are facing a Steelers defense that ranks 30th in the NFL in receiving yards allowed per game (260.6). Over his last five outings, Lemon has put together a 27-247-1 receiving line on 39 targets.

items.head: Will maintain larger role sans Nacua
items.body: The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Adkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report. Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angels' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

items.head: Team-high receiving yardage total
items.body: Mumpfield brought in three of four targets for 81 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

items.head: Taking on larger role
items.body: Mumpfield will take on an increased role for the Rams while Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) are unavailable, Rams Wire reports. Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell have taken most of the WR snaps alongside Nacua since Adams landed on injured reserve. It now sounds like Adams may return in a few weeks, while Nacua is out for at least a month and uncertain beyond that. There's a big opportunity ahead, but Mumpfield has been targeted on just 23 of 168 routes (13.7 percent), which is a low rate even for someone sharing the field with Nacua/Adams. Atwell has an even lower target rate (11.6 percent), so the Rams likely need their RBs and TEs to take on more offensive burden in Nacua's absence. While targets aren't assured, Mumpfield does seem like the safest bet to log a lot of WR snaps over the next few weeks.

items.head: Brings in two passes vs. Washington
items.body: Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

items.head: Not in line to be ready following bye
items.body: With regard to the availability of Adams (hamstring)  -- who remains on IR -- head coach Sean McVay said Friday "we'll take it a week at a time" with the wideout, while adding that he doesn't "think he's ready quite yet," Zach Edwards of the Rams' official site reports.

items.head: Not yet ready to practice
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted Friday that Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to practice this weekend, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports. Regarding the looming practice status of Adams, who is on IR and last played in Week 6, McVay said Friday, "We're not quite there yet." On the plus side, Beacham relays that the Rams are still hopeful Adams will be ready re-take the field next week. The veteran pass-catcher's availability gains added import going forward, following Friday's report that fellow starting WR Puka Nacua is on track to miss a couple of months after undergoing an MCL procedure.

items.head: Reportedly targeting Week 12 return
items.body: According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN,  Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return to action Nov. 25 against the Packers.

items.head: Sean McVay: Rams optimistic WR Davante Adams will return 'sooner than later'
items.body: The Rams are optimistic that injured wide receiver Davante Adams will return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later," coach Sean MVay said.

items.head: Davante Adams (Hamstring) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted of Adams (hamstring) on Wednesday that he thinks a return to action by the wideout on Nov. 25 against the Packers "is a realistic timeline for us," Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Welcoming back Monangai
items.body: Swift will be rejoined in the Bears backfield by Kyle Monangai (toe) on Sunday against the Saints, Larry Mayer of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Trending to be Buffalo's TE1 vs. Miami
items.body: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports. Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he is trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox would operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches on 20 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season games, and the Bills face a Dolphins defense that ranks 25th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

items.head: Catches one pass in win
items.body: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills' offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of the Bills' 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

items.head: Asserted by McDaniel as top RB
items.body: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports. "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week...I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Thursday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

items.head: Season-best rushing yardage in win
items.body: Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered.

items.head: Leading rusher as Chargers remain winless
Nets just 27 scrimmage yards in loss
items.body: Hampton rushed nine times for 20 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Hampton logged just one more carry than Kimani Vidal and five more than Keaton Mitchell, as the Chargers' ground game continued to resemble a committee scenario. Hampton now has 45 rushing yards or fewer in four straight games, and he's logged single-digit carries in three of those contests. The second-year back is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry behind an injury-hampered offensive line as well, leaving his outlook bleak for a Week 9 home matchup against an aggressive Texans defense next Sunday.

items.head: Jeshaun Jones (injury) is Active
items.body: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

items.head: Jeshaun Jones (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: The Vikings elevated Jones from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.

items.head: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) cleared to start vs. Chargers
items.body: Jets quarterback Geno Smith made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Chargers.

items.head: Cleared to play in Week 11
items.body: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

items.head: Geno Smith (injury) is Active
items.body: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.head: Looking good for Week 11
items.body: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

items.head: Limited, but plans to play Sunday
items.body: Smith (ankle), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, said afterward that he intends to play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) intends to play vs. Chargers: 'That's the plan'
items.body: Jets quarterback Geno Smith says he intends to play Sunday against the Chargers despite still walking with a noticeable link due to an ankle injury.

items.head: Opening Week 11 with limited practice
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith (ankle) will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.

items.head: Jaylen Waddle (injury) is Active
items.body: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.

items.head: Another full practice
items.body: Waddle (concussion) was a full practice participant Thursday.

items.head: Practices fully Wednesday
items.body: Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Practices Wednesday
items.body: Waddle (concussion) was present for Wednesday's practice, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.

items.head: In clear for Week 11 action
items.body: Barkley (hamstring) told EJ Smith of PHLY Sports on Friday that he "feels better physically" after the team's Week 10 bye, and the running back doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Steelers.

items.head: LeQuint Allen Jr. (injury) is Active
items.body: Allen (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

items.head: LeQuint Allen Jr. (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Cleared for Week 11
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

items.head: Limited in Thursday's session
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

items.head: Limited to kick off Week 11
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. Rodriguez was listed on injury reports both of the past two weeks due to the hand issue, but he proceeded to suit up for wins against the Ravens and Titans and handled his usual backup duties behind lead back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot). Assuming his limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related and not the result of any setback, Rodriguez should be ready to play Sunday against the Giants.

items.head: Not involved much in Week 10 win
items.body: Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. Rodriguez was out-carried 26 to four by Bhayshul Tuten, who has very much proven himself as the Jaguars' clear RB1 in one of the league's best offenses. Tuten also out-snapped Rodriguez 52 to 10, while LeQuint Allen (12 snaps) also saw more playing time. Rodriguez is little more than a deep-league bench stash should something happen to Tuten.

items.head: Cleared to face Titans on Sunday
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports. Rodriguez was listed as a limited practice participant all week,  but his hand issue is something he'll play through, while working alongside Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who returned to a limited session Friday and was also cleared for Week 10 action. Rodriguez has 55 carries in eight games to date, while Tuten has logged 122 rushes in that span, but Rodriguez has at least helped out his fantasy managers of late by scoring in each of his last two contests.

items.head: Limited at practice Thursday
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was a limited practice participant Thursday, while Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't participate. The catch is that Tuten didn't practice last week and ended up playing in a 33-10 win at Baltimore on Thursday night. Rodriguez played through his hand injury, so he should be able to take on an expanded workload this week if Tuten doesn't play.

items.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (Hand) is Questionable
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: Chris Bell (injury) is Active
items.body: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bills.

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Bell (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Bell was sidelined for the Dolphins' final two Week 10 practices before being listed as doubtful and ultimately ruled out ahead of Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, but the rookie wideout looks to be in a better spot on the health front in Week 11. After head coach Jeff Hafley described Bell as day-to-day prior to Wednesday's session, the receiver was able to turn in a limited practice. Bell will likely need to upgrade to full activity by Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

items.head: Considered day-to-day
items.body: Bell (knee) is viewed as day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports. Bell, who was inactive for Miami's Week 10 contest against the Colts, didn't practice this past Thursday and Friday after taking what coach Jeff Hafley described as a knock to his knee last week. In his absence versus Indianapolis, Kevin Coleman logged added WR snaps alongside Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas.

items.head: Chris Bell (Knee) is Out
items.body: Bell (knee) is inactive for Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Colts.

items.head: Unlikely to play
items.body: Bell (knee) is unlikely to play in Sunday's game against the Colts, but his injury isn't considered long-term and isn't related to the ACL repair surgery he had last December, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Bell reportedly got hit in his surgically repaired knee, and coach Jeff Hafley said the current injury has "nothing to do with [Bell]'s surgery." Hafley even left the door open for Bell to play Sunday, though the coach's other comments suggests it's highly unlikely. An absence would leave more playing time for fellow rookie Kevin Coleman, who has been been Miami's No. 4 receiver for most of the season.

items.head: Chris Bell (Knee) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: Not seen at practice Thursday
items.body: Bell (knee) wasn't spotted at practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Bell was listed as limited Wednesday, so his apparent downgrade in participation a day later puts the focus what the wideout is able to do Friday, as it relates to his status for Sunday's game against the Colts. Through eight contests overall, Bell has 12 catches for 148 yards and no TDs on 27 targets, but he's coming off a zero-catch effort in the Dolphins' Week 9 loss to the Lions, during which the 2026 third-rounder was on the field for 63 percent of his team's snaps on offense.

items.head: Limited on injury report
items.body: Bell (knee) is listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. This is likely just maintenance for Bell's surgically repaired knee. His role as the No. 3 wide receiver in Miami hasn't yielded much, with Bell drawing targets on just 16.7 percent of routes and catching only 44.4 percent of his targets. Things can't get much worse, at least from a statistical standpoint, with QB Kyle McCord replacing Malik Willis (abdomen) for at least the next four weeks.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday's game
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Tuten was limited at practice Wednesday, listed as a 'DNP' on Thursday, and then returned to a limited session Friday as he continues to manage the ankle and toe issues he has played through over the last two weeks. Also cleared to play versus New York were fellow RBs Chris Rodriguez (hand) and LeQuint Allen (hamstring), but Tuten nonetheless remains the clear top option in Jacksonville's backfield on the heels of recording a 70 percent snap share en route to carrying 26 times for 88 yards and a TD, to go along with three catches on four targets for 25 yards, in last weekend's 40-23 win over the Titans.

items.head: At stretching portion of Friday's practice
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

items.head: Could do some running Friday
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot), per head coach Liam Coen, "will maybe run around a little bit" at Friday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Tuten did not get any work in Thursday after being limited at Wednesday's practice, but Coen's comments suggest he could be back on the field Friday. Tuten was listed as either limited or as a non-participant the last eight times the Jaguars released an injury report but has not missed a game, so while his status is up in the air there is reason to believe he will be out there Sunday. Tuten's status for Week 11 will officially be revealed when the Jaguars release their next injury report later Friday.

items.head: Logs a 'DNP' Thursday
items.body: Tuten (ankle) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXMNF reports.

items.head: Works off to the side at start of Thursday's practice
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) was working off to the side during the stretching portion of Thursday's practice, according to Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union.

items.head: Tops 100 scrimmage yards against Titans
items.body: Tuten carried the ball 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown and caught three of four targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over Tennessee.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, ESPN's Michael DiRocco reports.

items.head: Bhayshul Tuten (injury) is Active
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) will practice Friday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: No designation for Sunday
items.body: Likely didn't practice Friday due to a strained groin, but he doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Jaguars, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports. There was some worry about the breakout tight end's status for Week 11 when he wasn't spotted at Friday's session, but head coach John Harbaugh allayed some of those fears, telling Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com that Likely was dealing with a "minor thing" and should be good to play Sunday. With no designation in tow, Likely is in the clear and probably is set for his typical 8.9 targets per game.

items.head: Should be OK for Week 11
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Likely is tending to a "minor thing" but should be good to play Sunday against the Jaguars, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports. Likely appears poised to go down as a non-participant on the final practice report of this week due to an undisclosed injury. A designation ahead of Week 11 action thus seems likely for the tight end, which will become known later Friday.

items.head: Not spotted at practice Friday
items.body: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports. That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

items.head: Career-high receiving yardage in loss
items.body: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

items.head: Catches TD from Winston in win
items.body: Likely caught five of six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Likely finished two targets shy of Malik Nabers' team-leading total and one receiving yard shy of Darnell Mooney's team-best mark, but the TE scored the Giants' lone touchdown of the game. That TD came on a five-yard pass in the third quarter from Jameis Winston, who replaced J.J. McCarthy (hip) for a drive and change before McCarthy returned to the game. Whether it's Winston or McCarthy under center, Likely projects to remain a key cog in the Giants' passing game for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, whose defense Likely carved up for 11 catches, 94 yards and two TDs in their Week 5 tie.

items.head: Good to go for Week 11
items.body: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

items.head: Remains limited in practice
items.body: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

items.head: Three grabs in Week 10 win
items.body: Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.

items.head: Good to go this week
items.body: Myers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, ESPN's Michael DiRocco reports. Meyers has fought through one injury or another for most of the season. This week, he managed limited practices Thursday and Friday, setting him up to play against the last-place Titans.

items.head: Jakobi Meyers (injury) is Active
items.body: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

items.head: Doesn't practice Wednesday
items.body: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week, before playing 68 percent of snaps and catching four passes for 65 yards in a Thursday blowout at Baltimore. It's unclear if he ankle has worsened or Wednesday's absence is just a matter of caution/maintenance. Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would all be candidates for additional WR snaps if Meyers were to miss time this year.

items.head: Jakobi Meyers (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: Paces pass catchers in win
items.body: Meyers brought in four of six targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. Meyers set the pace for the Jaguars in both receptions and receiving yards on the night, bouncing back nicely from a quiet 2-24-0 line just four days earlier in a blowout win over the Colts. The veteran wideout has multiple catches in all but one game, although Meyers hasn't topped 83 receiving yards in any contest to date in 2026. Meyers remains a key target for Trevor Lawrence, but he could see at least a slight boost in his outlook heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15, if Brian Thomas is moved at the trade deadline.

items.head: Cleared for Week 11
items.body: Kelce (ankle/calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Kelce was forced from last Sunday's game against the Falcons with the ankle injury, but he's good to go for Week 11 against a hapless Arizona squad. The Chiefs should run all over the Cardinals defense and likely won't need much pass volume from Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is more of a fringe TE1 for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Managing injuries, but practices fully
items.body: Kelce was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, despite being listed with ankle and calf injuries. During this past Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons, Kelce exited for a brief spell in the first half after injuring his ankle, but he ultimately returned to the contest. In addition to the ankle issue, Kelce may have tweaked his calf at some point in Week 10, but head coach Andy Reid indicated prior to Wednesday's practice that the veteran tight end was "doing well" in his recovery from the injuries, per Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com. His ability to take every rep for the Chiefs' first Week 11 session suggests his status for Sunday's game againt the Cardinals isn't in any peril.

items.head: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's top moments at Arrowhead Stadium
items.body: Kelce's greatest Arrowhead moments include his first catch, lots of playoff magic, and meeting the love of his life, Taylor Swift.

items.head: Quiet after ankle injury
items.body: Kelce secured both targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

items.head: Back in Sunday's game
items.body: Kelce (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the team's official site reports. Kelce had been listed as questionable to return to the contest, but was able to return to the field in the second quarter. While team's backfield is banged up this week, Kelce ability to resume action Sunday at least assures the Chiefs that their top pass-catchers are available for QB Patrick Mahomes to target.

items.head: Travis Kelce (injury) is Active
items.body: Kelce (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Travis Kelce (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Kelce went to the locker room during Sunday's game in Atlanta due to an apparent ankle injury, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Team-high receiving yards in win
items.body: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard. Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.head: Ticketed for lead-back duties again
items.body: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Johnson is in line to handle workhorse duties for the second straight week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. There was no sense in pushing Walker to play against a Cardinals team that is injury-ruined and likely to be blown out at Arrowhead. Johnson will get another crack at RB1 duties after he dismantled Atlanta's defense for 171 total yards and two touchdowns on 28 touches last Sunday. He's a top fantasy RB play.

items.head: Stellar showing in Week 10 win
items.body: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

items.head: Will be Kansas City's RB1 vs. Atlanta
items.body: Johnson will be the Chiefs' top running back for Week 10 after Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Could lead backfield Sunday
items.body: Coach Andy Reid noted that Johnson would take the bulk of the Chiefs' carries in the event that Kenneth Walker -- who didn't practice Friday due to groin tightness -- is forced to miss Sunday's game against the Falcons, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.

items.head: Scores rush TD in easy win
items.body: Johnson rushed six times for 34 yards and a touchdown and returned one kickoff for 29 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. The Chiefs held a 28-12 lead by the end of three quarters, which provided the opportunity for head coach Andy Reid to give Kenneth Walker, who scored three total touchdowns, some down time in the latter portion of the contest. Johnson took advantage of his opportunities, recording a six-yard touchdown run with 3:35 remaining in the contest. The rookie fifth-round pick's yardage total was a new career high, while his carry tally was his highest since Week 3. Johnson will remain in a modest No. 2 role for a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.head: Huge day as pass catcher in Week 8 loss
items.body: Johnson carried the ball once for 15 yards and caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added 44 yards on his only kickoff return. The rookie running back flashed his explosiveness on a 73-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that produced Johnson's first career NFL touchdown. He came into Sunday with a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through six games, and his six touches were firmly behind Kenneth Walker's 25, but Johnson's breakout performance can only encourage Andy Reid to find more ways to get the ball in his hands. Johnson will look to build on this effort in Week 9 against the Jets.

items.head: Ray Davis (injury) is Active
items.body: Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Davis (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice. It's a new injury for the running back, which clouds his status for Week 11 against the Dolphins. If Davis is unable to handle his normal handful of snaps, Frank Gore could be elevated from the practice squad.

items.head: Nursing hamstring injury
items.body: Davis was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury. Davis is making his first appearance on the injury report since Week 8, when he missed a practice due to an illness. Unless the hamstring issue was something that resulted in him exiting Wednesday's session early, Davis should still have decent odds of being ready to play Sunday against the Dolphins. The third-year back has seen limited playing time behind James Cook and Ty Johnson this season, earning no more than six touches in any of his nine appearances to date.

items.head: Ray Davis (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Minimal production in Monday night win
items.body: Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings. Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in the Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

items.head: Tallies 30 rushing yards in win
items.body: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.

items.head: Will play Sunday
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. However, Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) is expected to play Sunday against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Douglas said earlier this week that he was planning to play Sunday, and head coach Jeff Hafley backed up that statement while speaking prior to Friday's practice. The Dolphins will reveal whether or not Douglas carries an injury designation into Sunday's contest at some point Friday afternoon.

items.head: Another limited practice session
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) remained a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

items.head: Still in non-contact jersey
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) continued to don a non-contact jersey during Thursday's practice, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Nursing shoulder injury
items.body: Douglas was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a shoulder injury, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Per C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald, Douglas was spotted wearing a red non-contact jersey during the open portion of practice, but the rookie wideout said afterward that he fully expects to play Sunday against the Bills. So long as Douglas continues practicing in some fashion over the next two days, he should be on track to suit up in Buffalo, though he may need to upgrade to full participation to avoid taking a designation into the weekend.

items.head: On track to be available Sunday
items.body: Douglas (undisclosed) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, but he said he will play Sunday against  the Bills, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Team-high yardage total in loss
items.body: Douglas brought in three of eight targets for 71 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

items.head: Leads team in receiving yards
items.body: Douglas secured six of eight targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.

items.head: Ruled out for Sunday's game
items.body: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. With the Chiefs erring on the side of caution with Walker with a short week ahead, Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and TDs in the team's Week 10 win over the Falcons -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

items.head: Likely out in Week 11
items.body: Head coach Andy Reid said Friday that Walker (groin) "most likely" won't be available Sunday against the Cardinals, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Walker showed up at the Chiefs' facilities last Friday with a tight groin and eventually was ruled out for this past Sunday's game in Atlanta. With no practice reps to speak of yet during Week 11 prep, he appears to be trending toward another absence this Sunday, which again will thrust rookie Emmett Johnson into a workhorse role out of Kansas City's backfield.

items.head: Not spotted Friday
items.body: Walker (groin) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports. Walker hasn't practiced at all this week and should be expected to be ruled out for Sunday's game against Arizona later Friday. With the Cardinals bringing their minor-league team to Kansas City this weekend, there's no reason to push Walker when the Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround with a game against the Bills on Thanksgiving. Emmett Johnson will be a top fantasy RB for Week 11 once Walker is officially ruled out.

items.head: Misses Thursday's practice
items.body: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday.

items.head: Set to log 'DNP' on Wednesday
items.body: Walker (groin) won't practice Wednesday, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.

items.head: Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III (groin) to sit out, sources say
items.body: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will miss Sunday's game due to a minor groin strain, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

items.head: Kenneth Walker III (Groin) is Out
items.body: Walker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

items.head: Sits out Friday's practice
items.body: Walker (groin) sat out Friday's practice due to groin tightness, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.

items.head: Listed as questionable
items.body: Pittman (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Mark Kaboly reports. Pittman was designated for return from injured reserve earlier this week and had progressed to full participation Thursday, so his questionable tag keeps him in the mix for a potential activation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Eagles. With both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger) nearing a return, it's unclear what that will mean for rookie Germie Bernard's role going forward, as the rookie has hit a slow spot in the box score the last couple weeks.

items.head: Practices fully Thursday
items.body: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Pittman (foot) participated in practice Thursday, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.

items.head: Limited in first practice back
items.body: Pittman (foot) was limited in his return to practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

items.head: Back practicing Wednesday
items.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Pittman (foot) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. As a result of the transaction, the wide receiver can resume practicing.

items.head: Could be back for Week 11 action
items.body: Could Mike McCarthy said Monday that the Steelers are 'hopeful' they can get Pittman -- who last played in Week 4 -- back from his foot injury this week, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.

items.head: Takes part in Thursday's warmups
items.body: Pittman (foot) is warmed up with his teammates Thursday, though he remains on IR and wasn't wearing a helmet, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

items.head: Not ready to practice
items.body: Pittman (foot) is making progress but won't have his practice window opened this week, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Ready to return in Week 11
items.body: Monangai (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Saints. After being listed as full on all three of the Bears' Week 11 practice reports, Monangai officially is in the clear for his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a right thumb issue and a turf toe injury. While working in tandem with fellow RB D'Andre Swift this season, Monangai has racked up 60 carries for 324 yards and three touchdowns and caught all five targets for 39 yards in four appearances.

items.head: Listed as full Wednesday
items.body: Monangai (toe) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate. Monangai told Courtney Cronin of ESPN on Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints, and after being spotted in full pads at Tuesday's unofficial practice, the running back would have logged an uncapped session one day later if the team had held drills. Monangai is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a turf toe injury and a right thumb concern.

items.head: Kyle Monangai (injury) is Active
items.body: Monangai (toe) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate.

items.head: Practices again Tuesday
items.body: Monangai (toe/thumb) was seen wearing full pads for the Bears' unofficial practice Tuesday, Adam Jahns of AllCHGO.com reports.

items.head: 'On track' to be back in Week 11
items.body: Monangai (thumb/toe) said Monday that he's "on track" to return to action Sunday against the Saints, Courtney Cronin of ESPN reports.

items.head: Bears RB Kyle Monangai says he's 'on track' to return Sunday against Saints
items.body: Bears running back Kyle Monangai said Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints after missing five games with a thumb injury and turf toe.

items.head: Eyeing return in Week 11
items.body: Monangai (toe/thumb) was spotted working out during Monday's unofficial practice and is eyeing a return to action Sunday against the Saints, Chris Emma of 104-3 The Score Chicago reports.

items.head: Inactive in Week 9
items.body: Monangai (thumb/toe) is inactive for Sunday's contest against the Buccaneers. Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.

items.head: Clear for Week 11
items.body: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago. Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.

items.head: Jordyn Tyson (injury) is Active
items.body: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: Tyson (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.

items.head: Present for practice Thursday
items.body: Tyson (chest) took part in the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports. Tyson was limited at Wednesday's session due to a chest injury, and he at least is maintaining that activity level one day later. Thursday's practice report will reveal if he again was limited or upgraded to full. In the second game of his career this past Sunday against the Panthers, Tyson gathered in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards.

items.head: Limited by chest issue
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Tyson was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. Tyson missed the first seven games of the campaign due to a hamstring issue, but he increased his sway in the Saints offense from Week 9 to 10, upping his snap share (24 to 71 percent) and target count (five to 13). In this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers, he recorded an 11-80-0 line, but he emerged from that contest with a new health concern. As a result, Tyson's status will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

items.head: Jordyn Tyson (Chest) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Breakout performance in Week 10 loss
items.body: Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.

items.head: Increased role on tap?
items.body: Tyson was working with the Saints' first-team offense pregame ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.

items.head: Good to go for Week 11
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers. After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.

items.head: T.J. Hockenson (injury) is Active
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.

items.head: Another limited practice
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday.

items.head: Chance to return in Week 11
items.body: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that the Vikings hope Hockenson (wrist/chest) returns to action Sunday against the 49ers in Mexico City, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Expected to progress ahead of Week 11 action
items.body: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that the Vikings expect Hockenson (wrist/chest) to make progress ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Ruled out for Week 10
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay.

items.head: Not spotted Friday
items.body: Hockenson (wrist/chest) wasn't seen during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Expected to miss multiple weeks
items.body: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

items.head: A.J. Brown (Hamstring) is Doubtful
items.body: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Limping following loss Sunday
items.body: Brown (hamstring) was spotted limping out of the locker room following Sunday's Week 10 loss to Detroit, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.

items.head: A.J. Brown (Hamstring) is Out
items.body: Brown (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against the Lions, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.

items.head: A.J. Brown (injury) is Active
items.body: Brown (knee/ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Listed as questionable to face Detroit
items.body: Brown (knee/ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Practices again Friday
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) practiced Friday for a third straight day, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: New starting QB in Indy
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen announced Friday that Richardson will be the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward after the team waived Daniel Jones. Richardson made a cameo in Thursday's 26-3 loss at Houston, taking over for Jones for Indianapolis' final possession, but the former logged just a two-yard carry and two incompletions before the Texans ate up the final 6:50 of the contest. A 2023 first-round pick, Richardson himself hasn't started since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, making just four brief appearances the past two seasons combined, but he'll have a chance to boost his value (or not) in the final year of his rookie contract.

items.head: Why can't Richardson beat out struggling Jones as Colts QB1?
items.body: Daniel Jones has some of the worst numbers in the NFL, yet Anthony Richardson can't get on the field for the woeful Colts.

items.head: Listed as questionable Sunday
items.body: Brooks (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Brooks remains on injured reserve, so the questionable tag suggests Carolina at least may activate him ahead of Sunday's contest. If he's cleared to play, the running back would be in line to make his first appearance since Week 2, though he's no real threat to Chuba Hubbard's standing as the Panthers' lead back.

items.head: Full practice again Thursday
items.body: Brooks (groin) remained a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Brooks is still on injured reserve but appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Baltimore on Sunday. Chuba Hubbard should remain head-and-shoulders above Brooks on the depth chart as the clear RB1 for Carolina, but the Panthers likely also want to use the rest of the season to see if Brooks can stay healthy for a stretch and produce when given opportunities. Brooks is worth adding in fantasy, but his role will need to be defined before plugging him in lineups.

items.head: Listed as full Wednesday
items.body: Brooks (groin) was a full participant at Wednesday's walkthrough. Brooks was listed similarly last Wednesday before capping the week with back-to-back limited practices and receiving a doubtful tag for Week 10 action. He then was downgraded to out before this past Sunday's game at New Orleans. Brooks is seeking a return from injured reserve, where he's resided since after Week 2 due to core muscle surgery.

items.head: Won't return for Week 10
items.body: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

items.head: Listed as doubtful for Week 10
items.body: Brooks (groin) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at New Orleans after being limited in practice throughout the week, Kassidy Hill of panthers.com reports.

items.head: Full practice participant Thursday
items.body: Brooks (groin) was a full practice participant Thursday. The Panthers also listed Brooks as 'FP' on Wednesday's estimated practice report. Now that he's actually logged a full practice, Brooks may have a real shot to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game at New Orleans. The Panthers would need to make that move by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Brooks on the active roster Sunday.

items.head: Listed as full Wednesday
items.body: Brooks (groin) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 due to a groin injury that required core-muscle surgery and a stint on injured reserve. The Panthers designated him for return from IR on Wednesday, and he kicked off Week 10 prep with an uncapped walkthrough. How Brooks is listed on the injury report when Carolina holds practice Thursday and/or Friday may be the determining factor in his chances to play Sunday at New Orleans.

items.head: Team opens 21-day practice window
items.body: The Panthers designated Brooks (core) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Will be activated from IR
items.body: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports. Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

items.head: Could see more opportunities Sunday
items.body: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Taylor could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers. Isaiah Williams (ribs) also has been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.head: Grabs four passes vs. Buffalo
items.body: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second-most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 receiving line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 receiving line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.head: One catch in loss
items.body: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

items.head: Back practicing in full
items.body: Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. Taylor was limited Wednesday, but his return to full Thursday puts him on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. The tight end has been a surprisingly big part of the passing offense this season despite the selection of Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's Draft. Taylor has secured 17 of 23 targets for 136 yards and two touchdowns across six games.

items.head: Limited to begin Week 9 prep
items.body: Taylor was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury. Since sitting out Weeks 3 and 4 due to a thumb injury, Taylor has played north of 50 percent of the snaps on offense in each of the Jets' last four games, cobbling together a 15-138-2 receiving line on 20 targets over that stretch. Provided the back issue doesn't prevent him from practicing Thursday and Friday, Taylor should be able to handle his usual role this Sunday in Kansas City.

items.head: Three grabs against Las Vegas
items.body: Taylor caught three of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. It was a step back for Taylor after he caught all five of his targets for 62 yards and a pair of touchdowns in the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins, but he still remained the top tight end in the pecking order. Taylor out-targeted Kenyon Sadiq five to two and ran 19 routes to the rookie's 15 on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks. Taylor is a touchdown-reliant TE2 for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Could see more work with Cooper out
items.body: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers. In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) also will be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could translate to more targets in the passing game, but he's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.

items.head: Another quiet showing in Week 10
items.body: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor has typically handled larger snap shares.

items.head: Pops up for 49 yards in loss
items.body: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

items.head: One grab in loss to Las Vegas
items.body: Sadiq caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. The rookie tight end played 31 of 64 offensive snaps against Las Vegas and ran just 15 routes on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks. Sadiq continues to play behind Mason Taylor, who recorded three grabs for 19 yards on five targets across 19 routes. The Jets are using four tight ends on game days, and this offense isn't able to support more than a couple pass catchers for fantasy each week. Outside of his 7-105-1 receiving performance in Week 3 against the Lions, Sadiq has a total of 10 catches for 79 yards across his seven other contests.

items.head: Elevated role on tap sans Cooper
items.body: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, Mitchell is expected to play an elevated role on offense Sunday against the Chargers. Cooper was injured early in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, and Mitchell went on to see eight targets, as the Jets were playing catch-up most of the afternoon. They might be able to keep things closer against the 1-8 Chargers, though Los Angeles is still favored in the contest. Mitchell is a big-play threat as a WR4 for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Three catches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, it left Mitchell fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.head: Active in Week 10
items.body: Mitchell (knee) is listed as active Sunday versus the Bills. Mitchell followed up a 7-142-1 performance on nine targets in Week 8 with no catches on his seven targets last Sunday at Kansas City. It was a missed opportunity for him in Week 9 with Garrett Wilson out due to a concussion, and Mitchell himself was added to the Week 10 practice report Friday due to a knee injury, leaving him questionable for Sunday along with Wilson and Omar Cooper (ankle). All three are available this weekend, but with Wilson poised to take on his typical No. 1 role, Mitchell will be the second option, at best, among his position group.

items.head: Adonai Mitchell (injury) is Active
items.body: Mitchell (knee) is listed as active Sunday versus the Bills.

items.head: Adonai Mitchell (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: No catches in Week 9
items.body: Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now went without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

items.head: Another huge opportunity?
items.body: Mitchell and Omar Cooper will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. Mitchell is coming off the best performance of his career -- a 7-141-1 receiving line on 26 routes (nine targets) in last week's 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Cooper also ran 26 routes but finished without a target, despite topping 100 yards in back-to-back games beforehand. Both wide receivers now have a big opportunity with Wilson out of the lineup against a Kansas City defense that's missing cornerbacks Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and L'Jarius Sneed (IR - knee).

items.head: Career-high 142 yards in Week 8
items.body: Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Mitchell didn't catch any of his three targets in the Week 7 loss to Miami after returning from a four-game absence due to a finger injury, but he bounced back with a career-best Week 8 performance. His top highlights Sunday were a 12-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter and a 47-yard reception in the fourth quarter. Garrett Wilson led the team with 12 targets while Omar Cooper went without a target after back-to-back games with more than 100 yards and a TD. The 2-6 Jets could try to get all three of their talented young wideouts involved in Week 9, when they will likely be playing catch-up against the Chiefs.

items.head: Two touches in Week 11 loss
items.body: Giddens rushed one time for five yards and caught his lone target for 11 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans. With Seth McGowan (hamstring) exiting early with an injury, Giddens spelled Jonathan Taylor and played seven offensive snaps. Through three games this season, Giddens has rushed seven times for 48 yards and registered one catch for 11 yards. If McGowan's injury costs him time, Giddens figures to handle RB2 duties in his absence.

items.head: Only two offensive snaps vs. Miami
items.body: Giddens played two offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Giddens barely saw the field during Sunday's win, and his two offensive snaps were well behind fellow running backs Jonathan Taylor (40) and Seth McGowan (17). Giddens -- a fifth-round pick fo the Colts in the 2025 NFL Draft -- has seen little playing time since making his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 8 against the Jaguars. His role will likely stay minimal for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

items.head: No action in Week 9
items.body: Giddens did not appear in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan upon Taylor's departure.

items.head: Leads Colts in rushing yards in season debut
items.body: Giddens racked up 43 yards on six carries in Indianapolis' Week 8 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday. Giddens entered Sunday having not logged a snap this season, but he got an opportunity in the blowout loss and made the most of it, ripping off a pair of 12-yard runs on the way to a team-leading 43 rushing yards. However, it must be noted that he didn't enter until the game was far out of reach in the fourth quarter, so all of his production came in garbage time. Still, it was a meaningful performance by Giddens in the context of Indianapolis fielding trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor amidst a lost season. Should Taylor indeed be dealt, Giddens would immediately take on a more prominent role in the Colts backfield along with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan.

items.head: Injury not considered serious
items.body: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

items.head: Kayshon Boutte (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Goose egg versus Cleveland
items.body: Boutte failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. Even with Marvin Harrison (hamstring) out and Jaylin Noel (toe) done for the season, Boutte was targeted one just one of C.J. Stroud's 38 pass attempts versus Cleveland. His 47 snaps on offense were fewer than both Nico Collins (57) and Xavier Hutchinson (51) but 14 more than Tank Dell, though Dell out-targeted Boutte four to one. Boutte popped off for 4-125-2 in Week 9 against the Chargers but has otherwise failed to reach 40 receiving yards in any of his eight other appearances this season.

items.head: Strikes for two TDs in Week 9
items.body: Boutte erupted for four catches (on five targets) for 125 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 44-22 road win against the Chargers. Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.

items.head: Isaiah Williams (Ribs) is Out
items.body: Williams (ribs) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.head: Sits out another practice
items.body: Williams (ribs) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice. The Jets' wideout depth could be tested in Sunday's game against the Chargers, as both Williams and Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) have been sidelined for the team's first two Week 11 practices. Both receivers will likely need to practice in some fashion Friday to avoid being ruled out ahead of the weekend. If neither Williams nor Cooper can suit up against the Chargers, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick would be the available backup options behind starting receivers Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.

items.head: Sidelined for practice with rib injury
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Williams won't practice Wednesday due to a rib injury, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports. New York will be without two of its wideouts to begin Week 11 prep, as rookie Omar Cooper (ankle) is also sidelined for Wednesday's practice. Williams drew a season-high seven targets in this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills, finishing with four catches for 24 yards across 50 offensive snaps while apparently picking up an injury at some point along the way.

items.head: Isaiah Williams (Ribs) is Questionable
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Williams won't practice Wednesday due to a rib injury, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.

items.head: Season-high seven targets in Week 10
items.body: Williams caught four passes on seven targets for 24 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Williams' seven targets were his most of the season, and most of those looks came after Omar Cooper left early in the first quarter of Sunday's game due to an ankle injury. The injury was to the same foot that Cooper sustained a high-ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Titans, and an extended absence of the rookie first-rounder would result in Williams stepping into the WR3 role behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell. The Jets will hit the road for Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.head: Two grabs against Indy
items.body: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts. Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

items.head: Should benefit sans Harrison in Week 11
items.body: Hutchinson is expected to continue to benefit from elevated playing time Thursday against the Colts while Marvin Harrison (hamstring) is sidelined for a second straight game, Jared Koch of SI.com reports. Harrison hasn't exceeded a 50 percent snap share in any of his three appearances with the Texans since coming over in a trade with the Cardinals, but his absence for the Week 10 loss to the Browns still proved beneficial for Hutchinson. The fourth-year wideout out of Iowa State tied his season high with nine targets against the Browns, finishing with four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown while playing more than three-fourths of the offensive snaps for a second consecutive contest. Another healthy snap share should await Hutchinson in Week 11, and he could represent the No. 2 option in the Houston passing game behind top target Nico Collins.

items.head: Records TD grab in loss
items.body: Hutchinson brought in four of nine targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.

items.head: Back in Sunday's game
items.body: Hutchinson (head) returned to Sunday's contest at Cleveland, Aaron WIlson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. After being checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter Sunday, Hutchinson was cleared to reenter this Week 10 matchup. Before his exit, he notched four catches (on seven targets) for 58 yards and one touchdown.

items.head: Being evaluated for possible concussion
items.body: Hutchinson is under evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game in Cleveland. At the time of his exit in the fourth quarter, Hutchinson had four catches (on seven targets) for 58 yards and one touchdown. With Marvin Harrison (hamstring) inactive, Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Kayshon Boutte and Nikko Remigio are the Texans' healthy and available wide receivers.
