items.head: Scores TD in high-scoring win
items.body: Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 29 yards and a touchdown and also added a 28-yard kick return during Sunday's 44-22 win against the Chargers. Hutchinson finished tied with Kayshon Boutte for second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tank Dell (nine). Hutchinson was able to reach paydirt for the second straight contest, reeling in a 17-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud for the team's first score of the day in the first quarter. There are many mouths to feed in Houston's passing attack, so Hutchinson will remain a volatile fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Browns.

items.head: Goose egg against Houston
items.body: Treadwell failed to catch his lone target in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans. Treadwell played a position-high 40 of 50 offensive snaps but continues to run wind sprints in an offense that doesn't throw the ball down the field. Through 11 games this season, Treadwell has just 19 catches for 239 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets.

items.head: Hauls in first touchdown of 2026
items.body: Treadwell caught three passes on as many targets for 24 yards and a touchdown during Indianapolis' 24-22 win over Miami on Sunday. Week 10 was the Colts' first game without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, who were traded to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, on Tuesday. Treadwell led all Colts wide receivers with three catches and 52 offensive snaps, and he connected with Daniel Jones for a seven-yard touchdown pass late in the second quarter to give Indianapolis a 14-7 halftime lead. It was the first time Treadwell found the end zone this season, and the 2016 first-rounder figures to maintain a larger role on the offense given the departure of the Colts' top targets at the trade deadline. The Colts will hit the road for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday, and Houston's defense ranks 28th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing wide receivers.

items.head: Blanked in Week 9
items.body: Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

items.head: Records first career touchdown
items.body: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Paces pass catchers in lopsided loss
items.body: Gould secured two of three targets for 48 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. Gould was the rather unlikely leader in receiving yards for the Colts on the night, with a team-high 31-yard catch playing a big role in getting him there. The 2024 fifth-round pick has seen an expanded role in the wake of the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and for as long as Alec Pierce (IR, heel) is sidelined, Gould could function as one of Indianapolis' top downfield threats for either Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard.

items.head: Active versus Houston
items.body: Gould (toe) is active for Thursday night's game against the Texans. Gould was listed as questionable but is good to go for the divisional affair. He played 32 of 59 offensive snaps last Sunday against Miami, the Colts' first game since trading both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Gould manned the slot role vacated by Downs and secured two of four targets for 28 yards. He's a non-flashy but viable click in PPR-based fantasy formats.

items.head: Questionable for TNF
items.body: Gould (toe) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Texans, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports. Gould was deemed limited on Monday and Tuesday's practice reports, but upgraded to a 'full' listing on Wednesday's practice estimate. That suggests that the WR has a solid chance of being available Thursday, but those in leagues deep enough to consider Gould in PPR formats will need to check his availability ahead of the Colts' 8:15 pm ET kickoff. Gould was listed as a starter for this past Sunday's win over the Dolphins alongside Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks, a contest in which he logged 32 of a possible 59 snaps on offense while catching two of his four targets for 28 yards.

items.head: Limited in Tuesday's session
items.body: The Colts listed Gould (toe) as a limited participant in Tuesday's walk-through practice. Indianapolis has now estimated Gould as limited on both of its first two practice reports of Week 11, after he emerged from Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins with the toe injury. His status for Thursday's game against the Texans is muddled for the moment, but Gould could clear up any concern about his availability by turning in a full practice Wednesday. After Indianapolis shipped out two receivers (Keenan Allen and Josh Downs) at the trade deadline, Gould stepped in as the Colts' top option in the slot in Week 10 and finished with two receptions for 28 yards on four targets.

items.head: Estimated as limited Monday
items.body: Gould (toe) was estimated as limited in Monday's walkthrough practice. It's a new injury for Gould, who started Sunday against the Dolphins in the Colts' first game without both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, who were both dealt at the trade deadline last week. Gould played 32 of 59 offensive snaps versus Miami and registered two catches for 28 yards on four targets.

items.head: Stepping into slot role
items.body: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Gould is in line to step into the slot role previously held by Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass-catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.

items.head: Double-digit yardage on one catch
items.body: Schultz brought in his only target for 11 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Schultz had a minimal role on a night when C.J. Stroud threw for a modest 194 yards and recorded completions to nine different targets. The veteran tight end now has consecutive one-catch, 11-yard tallies after recording multiple receptions in each of his first eight games of the season, and Schultz's production will remain hard to trust heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: First TD of season in loss
items.body: Schultz caught one pass for an 11-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. While Schultz got into the end zone for the first time this campaign, his catches and targets were new single-game lows for 2026. Schultz has yet to produce more than 45 yards in a game when Nico Collins is healthy this season. The veteran tight end is a low-floor, TD-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.head: Two grabs in Week 9 win
items.body: Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

items.head: Three catches in Week 11 win
items.body: Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Three receptions in Week 10 loss
items.body: Dell brought in three of four targets for 21 yards and rushed once for no gain in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Dell (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Browns, while teammate Marvin Harrison (hamstring) has been ruled out. Last week, Dell caught four passes for 104 yards and a TD in a 44-22 win over the Chargers, leading Houston in targets (nine) in his second game back from a lengthy absence. His snap share (45 percent) and route share (55 percent) were less encouraging, but Dell and Kayshon Boutte are candidates for more playing time with Harrison out for at least one week.

items.head: Limited in practice Wednesday
items.body: Dell (hand) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Dell operated as the Texans' third receiver for much of last Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, running 22 routes on C.J. Stroud's 38 dropbacks. In just his second game since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, Dell turned nine targets into five catches for 104 yards and a touchdown against Los Angeles. He's become a legitimate name to add in fantasy football ahead of Sunday's Week 10 date with the Browns.

items.body: Texans WR Tank Dell scored a touchdown on Sunday in his second game back from a gruesome knee injury.

items.head: First touchdown 2024
items.body: Dell turned a team-high nine targets into four catches for 105 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 road victory against the Chargers In his second appearance since returning from a brutal left knee injury suffered in December 2024, Dell again recorded a reception of 40-plus yards, connecting with C.J. Stroud for a 63-yard TD in the second quarter. It was one of five touchdown passes for Stroud, who spread the ball around to nine different pass catchers and four that reached the end zone at least once. Dell will aim to build on the momentum next Sunday at Cleveland.

items.head: Good yardage on one catch
items.body: Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick has now recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Daniel Jones, who James Boyd of the Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.

items.head: Next to nothing with three touches
items.body: Warren rushed once for three yards and brought in two of three targets for one yard in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

items.head: More targets on tap?
items.body: Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports. The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.

items.head: Solid yardage with four catches
items.body: Warren brought in four of seven targets for 44 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. Warren tied for second in receptions and finished as the runner-up in both receiving yards and targets after a slow start to Sunday's loss. The second-year tight end's role could be even bigger by next Sunday's Week 10 home matchup against the Dolphins, as the Colts could conceivably move both Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, not to mention quarterback Daniel Jones, by Tuesday's trade deadline. Warren has at least four receptions in every game with the exception of Week 1 heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

items.head: Little with four catches Sunday
items.body: Warren secured four of 10 targets for 18 yards in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. In his return from a two-game absence due to a groin injury, Warren tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in targets on another forgettable afternoon for the Colts, as Indianapolis dropped to 2-6 on the season and Daniel Jones was benched late. With rumors swirling that both Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor could be traded by the Nov. 10 deadline, Warren could be the biggest skill-position weapon the Colts have during the second half of the season alongside Alec Pierce (IR, heel). Warren's catch and yardage totals Sunday were both his second lowest of the season, and it remains to be seen if he'll be catching passes from either Jones or Anthony Richardson in a Week 9 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday.

items.head: Keeps piling up TDs in win
items.body: Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

items.head: Three more TDs in loss
items.body: Stroud completed 20 of 38 passes for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 20 yards in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.

items.head: A 'confident' C.J. Stroud soaks in five-TD day against Chargers
items.body: Stroud matched his career high with 5 TD passes and added 384 passing yards in the win.

items.head: Tosses five touchdowns
items.body: Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception and recorded two carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win at the Chargers. Stroud matched a career high with his five TD strikes, which went to Xavier Hutchinson (17 yards), Tank Dell (63), Kayshon Boutte (12 and 63) and Nico Collins (13). Moreover, Stroud's 384 passing yards matched the second most in a game in his career. He's now thrown for multiple touchdowns in four of the last five games, a stretch in which he's accounted for a remarkable 1,457 yards through the air and a 13:2 TD:INT. Stroud will attempt to keep things rolling next Sunday, when the Texans visit the Browns.

items.head: Minimal production with 15 touches

items.head: Clears century mark in scrimmage yards
items.body: Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards and brought in two of four targets for 20 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Indianapolis.

items.head: Sticking around in Indy
items.body: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Set to play Sunday amid trade rumors
items.body: Taylor was a full participant at Thursday's practice, and Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports that both Taylor and head coach Shane Steichen have maintained that Taylor will play Sunday against the Cowboys despite ongoing trade rumors surrounding the star running back. "You can't avoid it," Taylor said of the trade rumors. "But it's more about trying to block that out." Taylor's preparing for what could well be his last game as a member of the Colts. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the 2-6 Colts have received trade calls on numerous players including Taylor, but Indianapolis doesn't intend to complete any additional trades prior to the conclusion of Sunday's game.

items.head: Logs 12 touches in potential swan song
items.body: Taylor rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in four of five targets for 24 yards in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Taylor opened the game in his usual starting role with trade rumors swirling around him, and the star running back finished with a wholly unremarkable performance. Taylor ultimately ceded plenty of snaps to backfield mates Seth McGowan and DJ Giddens, the likeliest heir-apparent candidates if Taylor is indeed moved to another team in the coming days. Taylor had exceeded 90 rushing yards in back-to-back games and on five occasions overall heading into Week 8, so even if his Colts tenure finishes with Sunday's whimper, he'll have plenty to offer in a new destination.

items.head: Trade talks heating up
items.body: Taylor is being made available via trade by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN  reports. Taylor himself was not requesting a trade earlier in the week, but Indianapolis' recent flurry of moves opened the possibility that the star running back would also be moved in the team's teardown before a rebuild. The Colts moved on from Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and got significant draft capital from the Seahawks and 49ers in return. Now a market is forming for Taylor, 27, who could help put a contender over the top. Per Schefter, the Colts are seeking a deal similar to what the Panthers got in 2022 when they traded Christian McCaffrey.

items.head: Gets into end zone Thursday
items.body: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

items.head: Very busy in Week 10 loss
items.body: Collins secured nine of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.

items.head: First TD since Week 4 on Sunday
items.body: Collins corralled all four of his targets for 55 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 victory at the Chargers. Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. He'll seek better results next Sunday in Cleveland.

items.head: Retains expanded role Sunday
items.body: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

items.head: Gets into end zone in loss
items.body: McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for minus-3 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.

items.head: Breaks one long run Week 8
items.body: McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards and returned four kickoffs for 103 yards Sunday in a loss to the Jaguars. McGowan's best run was a 16-yarder up the middle midway through the third quarter to take the ball to Jacksonville's three-yard line. That set up Indianapolis' only touchdown in the blowout loss. McGowan logged a modest 15 offensive snaps to starter Jonathan Taylor's 38, but the former outgained Taylor on the ground, 29-23. Meanwhile, DJ Giddens paced the Colts with 43 rushing yards on six totes. The big story, of course, is that the Colts are entertaining trade offers on Taylor, and if the star RB is ultimately dealt, McGowan and Giddens both figure to take on significantly larger roles, though it's unclear which of the two would become the starter. With that in mind, it's worth noting that Giddens didn't enter until the fourth quarter and racked up all of his yardage in garbage time.

items.head: Limited to return duties vs. Dallas
items.body: James returned five kickoffs for 101 yards during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. James set the tone right out of halftime with a 49-yard kickoff return, although the yards gained were mitigated by a holding penalty by the Niners. All eight of his snaps came on special teams, and it looks like the second-year pro is out of the mix for backfield touches behind RB1 Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black, the latter of whom found the end zone for the second time in his last three outings. The 49ers will travel to Mexico City for Week 11 to face the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.head: Logs three carries in Week 9 win
items.body: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas. As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second-most this season behind the four touches he logged Week 2 versus Miami. James will likely be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black were to miss time.

items.head: Ditches protective glove on left hand
items.body: Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

items.head: Weak showing in loss to Carolina
items.body: Shough completed 25 of 35 targets for 187 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added 25 rushing yards on six carries and was charged with a lost fumble.

items.head: Does just enough in OT win
items.body: Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

items.head: Still has glove on non-throwing hand
items.body: Shough was still wearing a glove on his left hand during pregame warmups ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, according to Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune. As Johnson notes, Shough wasn't listed on the Saints' Week 9 injury report, as he was (as a full participant) in Week 7, prior to the team's bye. With no reported reported setbacks, Shough -- who sustained two broken bones in his left (on-throwing) hand Oct. 5 -- is presumably simply protecting his hand until it's 100 percent healed. On the plus side from the QB's perspective as he continues to play through the issue, is that highly-touted rookie WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) -- the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft -- is making his much-awaited regular-season debut for New Orleans.

items.head: Five catches in Week 10 win

items.head: Finds end zone twice in win over Falcons
items.body: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta. While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.

items.head: Paces air attack in wild win
items.body: Higgins secured 10 of 11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over the Titans on Sunday. Higgins led the Bengals' air attack in receiving yards and touchdown catches on a day when Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdown passes overall. Higgins was responsible for a pair, making 17- and 18-yard scoring grabs in the second half. The latter erased a 36-29 deficit with 1:17 remaining in regulation to help force overtime, and Higgins now has at least 148 receiving yards in three of the last four games and a pair of TD catches in two straight. The veteran has essentially moved into a true 1-A role alongside Ja'Marr Chase in the passing attack, and Higgins will look to carry the massive momentum into a Week 9 matchup against a vulnerable Falcons secondary in Madrid next Sunday.

items.head: Recovering from meniscus surgery
items.body: Kirk announced Wednesday via his personal Instagram account that he recently underwent meniscus surgery. After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

items.head: Limited with illness
items.body: Jones (illness) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports. Jones managed to practice through his illness in a limited fashion Wednesday. It remains to be seen whether the quarterback will overcome the sickness before Sunday's contest against the Vikings. If Jones cannot suit up, Kurtis Rourke would become the backup to Brock Purdy for Week 11.

items.head: Too pricey for Minnesota
items.body: The 49ers fielded trade interest in Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports. Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders prior to the deadline.

items.head: Remains out, not yet practicing
items.body: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

items.head: In line to miss multiple weeks, per coach
items.body: According to coach Brian Schottenheimer, Ferguson (knee) is in line to miss multiple weeks, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) --when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into finding additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

items.head: Headed for imaging on knee
items.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts that Ferguson will undergo imaging on his knee Monday, the team's official site reports. Ferguson played just 27 of the Cowboys' 79 offensive snaps and finished with two catches for 21 yards and a touchdown on two targets before exiting Sunday's game in the third quarter after taking a low hit. Schottenheimer noted that Ferguson initially sustained a stinger on the hit, but the Cowboys later classified his injury as a knee issue. The upcoming MRI will reveal the severity of the injury, which tentatively clouds Ferguson's status for the Cowboys' Week 10 matchup with the 49ers.

items.head: Suffers knee injury in Week 9
items.body: Ferguson sustained a knee injury during Sunday's game against the Colts, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports. Ferguson tended to a low-ankle sprain during Week 9 prep, but it's now one of his knees that's a concern after he took a low hit in the third quarter of Sunday's matchup. He had two catches (on two targets) for 21 yards and one touchdown at the time of his exit.

items.head: Active in Week 9
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday in Indianapolis. Ferguson left last Sunday's loss to the Cardinals on the Cowboys' first possession and wasn't able to return due to an ankle injury. He was diagnosed with a low-ankle sprain, and while head coach Brian Schottenheimer relayed to Jon Machota of The Athletic on Monday that Ferguson has a chance to play in Week 9, the tight end managed just one limited practice (Friday) and was listed as questionable. Now that Ferguson is confirmed to be active, his workload is unclear with two other TEs (Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell) also available to the offense.

items.head: Could practice Friday
items.body: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer hopes that Ferguson (ankle) will be "back on the field" Friday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Ferguson did not get any work in Wednesday or Thursday due to the ankle injury he sustained in Week 8, but it appears there is a chance he could practice in some capacity Friday. The Cowboys will reveal his official status for Week 9 at some point following the conclusion of Friday's session.

items.head: Full practice Wednesday
items.body: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday. Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

items.head: Without clear timeline for return
items.body: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he had no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said. Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

items.head: Could make 2026 debut in Week 11
items.body: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that "there's a chance" that Conner (foot) could return from injured reserve and serve as the Cardinals' starting running back Sunday at Kansas City, Jess Root of USA Today reports. The Cardinals haven't provided many updates on Conner's status since he was placed on IR with a designation for return following the preseason, but LaFleur offered the most positive news on the running back to date Monday. LaFleur noted that Conner is "trending well" as he works his way back from a right foot/ankle injury that has kept him from playing since Week 3 of last season. The Cardinals have yet to clear Conner to practice, but if he has his 21-day evaluation window opened Wednesday for the start of Week 11 prep, it would leave the door open for him to suit up against the Chiefs. Arizona has an opening for a healthy Conner to carve out a notable role in the backfield with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) set to remain on IR for at least two more games.

items.head: Set to complement Montgomery in Week 11
items.body: Demercado is expected to serve as the top complement to David Montgomery in Thursday's game against the Colts, with Woody Marks (concussion) ruled out for the contest. With Montgomery sidelined for a fourth straight game this past Sunday against the Browns and with Marks making an early exit, Demercado saw his most playing time of the season in the 27-24 loss. Demercado did little to capitalize on the opportunity, finishing with 15 yards from scrimmage on eight touches (seven carries, one reception). Though Marks wasn't able to clear concussion protocol in a short week, Montgomery has been cleared to play after he was listed as a full practice participant Monday through Wednesday. Montgomery should step back in as the Texans' preferred option out of the backfield, leaving Demercado to settle for more of a change-of-pace role.

items.head: Works as lead back following Marks injury
items.body: Demercado rushed seven times for 16 yards and brought in one of two targets for minus-1 yard in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Demercado opened the game in a reserve role in his second game in a Texans uniform, but Woody Marks' third-quarter exit due to a concussion left the former in the de facto No. 1 role. That still didn't lead to much opportunity for Demercado in a game where Houston squandered a 17-0 first-half lead. However, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports Marks is unlikely to play in Week 11 due to the short turnaround for a home matchup against the Colts, meaning Demercado and Dare Ogbunwale could have expanded roles in that game unless David Montgomery (groin) is able to suit up.

items.head: Six rushes in debut with Houston
items.body: Demercado rushed six times for 16 yards and caught one of two targets for eight yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Demercado was claimed off waivers by the Texans on Oct. 28, and he made his team debut in Week 9 after the team was off in Week 8. The running back finished second on the team in carries behind Woody Marks (18), and he could operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield again in Week 10 versus Cleveland if David Montgomery (groin) remains sidelined.

items.head: Foot injury in rear-view mirror
items.body: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.

items.head: Does just enough to eke out win
items.body: Young completed 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. He added one rushing yard on his only carry.

items.head: Three TDs not enough Sunday
items.body: Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. He added 13 yards on his only carry and lost a fumble. The fourth-year QB tossed TDs in each of the last three quarters, finding Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan, but Young's attempt to engineer a game-winning drive inside the final two minutes ended on a Nik Bonitto strip sack. It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.

items.head: Ready to play, ankle improving
items.body: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Friday that Young (ankle) is ready for Sunday's game against Denver after a "great week" of practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Young has been a full practice participant throughout the week, apparently not too bothered by a sore ankle. The bigger concern for Sunday is Denver's impressive pass rush matching up against Carolina's injury-riddled offensive line.

items.head: Remains in concussion protocol

Marks' chances of clearing concussion protocol before Thursday night's game against the Colts are getting slimmer as he remains in the protocol with just over 24 hours until kickoff. David Montgomery and Emari Demercado project as the top two backs for the Texans in Week 11 at this stage.

Head coach DeMeco Ryans has already indicated that Marks is unlikely to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Colts, so expect the second-year back to get formally ruled out for the Week 11 contest following Wednesday's practice.

items.body: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

items.head: Could return after four-game minimum
items.body: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports. The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

items.head: Sticking as backup for Week 11
items.body: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports. Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

items.body: Brandon Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels have patched up their relationship after a falling out earlier this year, sources told ESPN.

items.head: Deemed 100 percent ahead of likely release
items.body: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports. After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco reinstated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him.

items.head: Reinstated, 49ers granted two-week exemption
items.body: The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk (personal) from the reserve/left squad list Monday and were granted a two-week roster exemption for the wide receiver, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to either add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

items.head: 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk reinstated by NFL
items.body: The NFL reinstated San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Monday after he reported for a physical, according to the league's transaction wire.

items.head: Meets with 49ers on Friday
items.body: Prior to meeting with 49ers officials Friday, Aiyuk (personal) told assembled media that he's "feeling great, healthy" and "looking to get reinstated to the National Football League," Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Per Wagoner, Aiyuk submitted paperwork to be reinstated to the NFL in late October, and since then both the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association have been involved in an attempt to reach a resolution that's agreeable to both the wide receiver and the 49ers. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Thursday that Aiyuk's efforts to secure his release may be hampered by the roughly $13 million in bonus forfeitures that he owes the team, which could mean arbitration comes into play and delays the process. Friday's meeting between Aiyuk, his agent Drew Rosenhaus and San Francisco brass was only the first step. If the sides reach an agreement, the 49ers will have three options: release Aiyuk, trade him before Tuesday's deadline or add him to their 53-man roster.

items.head: Brandon Aiyuk meets with 49ers, says he's healthy, 'looking to get reinstated'
items.body: Brandon Aiyuk met with the Niners on Friday to begin hammering out a path toward a divorce that has been more than two years in the making.

items.head: Money owed may be hurdle in securing release
items.body: Aiyuk's effort to secure his release by reporting to the 49ers' facility Friday could be complicated by roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture he owes the team, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports. Pelissero notes that the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in trying to reaching a resolution that is agreeable to both Aiyuk and the 49ers. It's possible that the embattled wideout could ultimately agree to pay back the money in order to potentially have an opportunity to move on with another club, but there's also a chance the issue goes to arbitration. Aiyuk is planning to show up at San Francisco's facility Friday, though that is unlikely to bring the matter to a close. In fact, it could take an extended period of time to sort out a path forward, especially if arbitration is brought into play.

items.body: Lamar Jackson told his Ravens teammates that he plans to return later this season, sources told NFL Network.

items.head: Multiple factors at play in possible return
items.body: Jackson's odds to play again this season depend on his recovery from a right thumb injury, and also whether or not new QB Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens in the playoff picture long enough to make a return late in the season possible for Jackson, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. The Ravens already have cycled through three starting QBs this season, and with Tyler Huntley sidelined for the rest of the campaign due to a turf-toe injury and Jackson out indefinitely, the team agreed to a trade with the Cardinals for Brissett, which became official Friday. Brissett was serviceable until he wasn't in Arizona, finishing his 2026 season there with 1,719 yards on 63 percent passing, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight appearances, and he'll have top talents in RB Derrick Henry and WR Zay Flowers to work with in his new locale. It remains to be seen if Baltimore, which is three games in the loss column behind Pittsburgh and Cincinnati in the AFC North, can get back to winning ways, but Brissett's performance seemingly will dictate if Jackson makes another appearance by Week 18.

items.head: Ravens refuse to blame historic rut on loss of Lamar Jackson
items.body: The Ravens say one of the worst stretches in team history cannot be pinned on the loss of the injured Lamar Jackson.

items.head: Will have surgery and go on IR
items.body: Jackson is slated to have surgery to address his right thumb injury and will be placed on injured reserve, per coach Jesse Minter,  Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports. Wacker also notes that Jackson's injury could potentially be season-ending according to Minter, with more context on that front presumably slated to arrive after the QB's thumb is checked out further. With Tyler Huntley dealing with a toe injury, Baltimore's QB situation is in flux in Week 9, and beyond. Joe Fagnano finished up Sunday's game against the Bills, and it's likely the Ravens will add signal-caller depth ahead of Thursday's game against the Jaguars.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's game
items.body: Jackson (right thumb) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bills. After previously being deemed questionable to return, Jackson has now been confirmed to be unavailable for the rest of the contest. In his absence, Tyler Huntley has taken over the Ravens' QB duties versus Buffalo. Prior to his first-quarter exit, Jackson didn't complete his only passing attempt.

items.head: Could benefit from Robinson's absence
items.body: Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports. A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.

items.head: Why Packers can't protect Jordan Love or rush successfully
items.body: The two-year demise of the Packers' offensive line began on March 10, 2025 and has no end in sight.

items.head: Buried by Minnesota pass rush in loss
items.body: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

items.head: QB Jordan Love, Packers frustrated after blowout loss at home to Vikings
items.body: Jordan Love and the Packers expressed their frustration after a 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

items.head: 'Balling' Jordan Love wows teammates with big performance at Patriots
items.body: The way Packers quarterback Jordan Love played in Sunday's win over the Patriots left some of his teammates in awe and others speechless.

items.head: Another prolific performance in win
items.body: Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed once for a 13-yard score in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. He also ran in a two-point conversion. Love continued to attack downfield with great efficacy in the significant road upset for the Packers. Love averaged 12.8 yards per attempt while amassing his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, a figure bested only by the 387-yard tally he managed in Week 1. Love generated his second straight three-touchdown day through the air as well, connecting with Matthew Golden (five yards), Savion Williams (10 yards) and Christian Watson (39 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes and kicking off the scoring on the day with a 13-yard rush just 1:41 into the contest. Love is up to 2,618 passing yards with a 19:6 TD:INT and a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

items.head: Source: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew has surgery to repair right UCL
items.body: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II had surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday, a source told ESPN.

items.head: Underwent UCL surgery Monday
items.body: Minshew (elbow) underwent UCL reconstructive surgery Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. It's a season-ending procedure and will likely keep Minshew sidelined until training camp next summer. The veteran quarterback suffered the injury in Week 9 but somehow kept playing through it, completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. It's Carson Beck's show moving forward, as the Cardinals play out the string on another lost season in what has become a never-ending rebuild.

items.head: In line for surgery on torn UCL
items.body: Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right throwing elbow last Sunday at Seattle and is slated to undergo season-ending surgery, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Minshew incredibly played through the injury in Week 9, logging all 53 offensive snaps and completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in his first start replacing the since-departed Jacoby Brissett. Schefter added that Minshew still is determining the timing of the procedure, but he plans on having it. With Minshew out for the rest of the campaign, rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is taking over under center for the Cardinals.

items.head: Will miss rest of season
items.body: Minshew (elbow) will undergo UCL surgery and is out for the season, Theo Mackie of AzCentral reports. With Minshew already on injured reserve, the surgery confirms he won't return for Arizona this season. Carson Beck is now Arizona's starting QB for Week 11 against the Rams and beyond.

items.head: Placed on IR
items.body: The Cardinals placed Minshew (elbow) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Gardner Minshew II (Elbow) is Doubtful
items.body: Per Adam Schefter of ESPN,  Minshew (elbow) is reportedly seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will require season-ending surgery to address a torn UCL.

items.head: Set to undergo testing on arm/elbow
items.body: Minshew is slated undergo testing on his right elbow/arm in the wake of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks, according to Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site. Minshew took over as the team's starting QB in advance of Week 9 action, and now his status for this weekend's game against the Rams is unclear. In the event that Minshew is unavailable versus Los Angeles, Carson Beck would be next in line for Arizona's signal-caller reps.

items.head: Brings in 26-yard pass in Week 10 loss
items.body: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' TE1 in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets of Dak Prescott, With Spann-Ford and five other Cowboys skill-position players logging one catch each. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again be the Cowboys' top tight end for Week 11 on Nov. 22, against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.

items.head: Two snags in victory
items.body: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts. Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the year, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine regular-season contests so far.

items.head: Does little with season-high seven targets
items.body: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

items.head: Zero targets in first game since extension
items.body: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year extension worth up to $26.8 million, which puts him under contract with the Cardinals through the 2029 season. He didn't have any offensive stats to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck under center for the first time this season. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 regular-season games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

items.head: Signing extension through 2029
items.body: Higgins is signing a contract extension with the Cardinals through 2029, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. Higgins was scheduled for free agency after this season, and he's taken on a larger role as the year has progressed, helping the Cardinals get by with limited talent at wide receiver. Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and won't be of much fantasy interest unless McBride misses time.

items.head: Two grabs versus Seattle
items.body: Higgins caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

items.head: Hauls in 31-yard pass in Week 10 defeat
items.body: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and the former has caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck, IR) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't bring much confidence heading into Week 11 against the Chiefs on Nov. 22.

items.head: Zero targets in Week 10 loss
items.body: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't show up on the box score otherwise during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck under center, and Arizona finished with a 17:37 time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the Cardinals pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the Cardinals skill-position players (other than McBride), especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against the Chiefs.

items.head: Taking over starting role
items.body: Virgil will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of azcardinals.com reports. A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday against the Rams in what will be the first career start for rookie QB Carson Beck.

items.head: One catch against Seattle
items.body: Virgil caught one of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect with each other for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took quite a hit in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

items.head: Hauls in 21-yard pass in Week 10 loss
items.body: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle. Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck on the field. The offense struggled to move the ball down the field and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with a 17:37 time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first quarter. Fehoko's 26 offensive snaps led all Arizona wide receivers, and with Michael Wilson (neck, IR) out for the rest of the season, the former should continue to operate in an elevated role heading into Week 11 against the Chiefs on Nov. 22.

items.head: Set for more snaps
items.body: Fehoko will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of azcardinals.com reports. Fehoko is a 2021 fifth-round pick who turned 29 earlier this month and has been targeted on just two of 37 routes for the Cardinals this year. He mostly seems to have stuck around the league because his size is useful for special teams and blocking, but Fehoko now has a chance to get more snaps on offense, if only because Arizona's WR depth chart has been decimated. He has a chance to start this Sunday against the Rams in QB Carson Beck's first career start.

items.head: Climbs up depth chart
items.body: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports. Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However, with the Cardinals trading away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. After Bourne made an early exit in this past Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory over the Cowboys, Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026. He wasn't much of a factor in the Cardinals' comeback win, however, earning just one target (for a 17-yard reception) while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideouts Michael Wilson (ribs) and Reggie Virgil and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.

items.head: Logs five carries in return
items.body: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries, although the Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).

items.head: Good to go
items.body: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.

items.head: Logs full practice Thursday
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced in full Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Bam Knight (Concussion) is Out
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced Thursday without a yellow non-contact jersey, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Practicing Wednesday
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

items.head: Bam Knight (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: Knight (concussion) officially didn't practice Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Absent from Thursday practice
items.body: Knight (concussion) wasn't present for Thursday's practice, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. Assuming Knight goes down as a non-participant Thursday, his lack of activity so far this week doesn't give him a good chance to gain clearance from the concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game at Seattle. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) hitting IR on Tuesday, Tyler Allgeier is poised to lead the Cardinals backfield until Knight is back in action, at which point there's expected to be more of a even split between the two.

items.head: Absent from practice Wednesday
items.body: Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. Knight is in concussion protocol after playing just 18 offensive snaps in last Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) headed to injured reserve and out for at least the next four weeks, Knight figures to have a key backfield role alongside Tyler Allgeier, but it might be a challenge for Knight to gain clearance for Sunday's game against Seattle.

items.head: Held without catch in Week 10 loss
items.body: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties moving forward now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.head: Bears QB Caleb Williams has moved on from 4-INT game, but frustration lingers
items.body: Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Cubs outfielder was named NL MVP, and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror.

items.head: Caleb Williams unfazed by 4 interceptions as Bears pull out win vs. Bucs
items.body: Caleb Williams refused to let his four interceptions rattle his confidence as he put the Bears in position to beat the Buccaneers on a walk-off field goal.

items.head: Shrugs off four INTs in fourth straight win
items.body: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards. Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

items.head: Inside the evolution of Caleb Williams' MVP candidacy
items.body: Williams has the fourth-shortest odds to win MVP as the Bears are currently favored to win the NFC.

items.head: Impressive performance against elite defense
items.body: Williams completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for one yard in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Williams helped set the tone for the Bears' statement road victory by leading a 17-play, 80-yard march that absorbed 8:32 of the first quarter, one that the third-year signal-caller capped off with a one-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Williams then managed the game effectively from that point forward, avoiding mistakes while leaning on a workhorse performance from D'Andre Swift (27 carries, three touchdowns) and an often dominating effort from his defense. Williams now has a three-game streak of interception-free performances and is up to 1,267 passing yards through five contests heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: Zero catches despite season-high snap count
items.body: Burks failed to haul in either of his two targets during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded one tackle on special teams. With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being shipped off to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, at the Nov. 10 deadline, the Colts turned to Burks, Laquon Treadwell and Anthony Gould to serve as the top wideouts for Week 10. Burks' 34 offensive snaps were a season high and second among Indianapolis' wide receivers, but the rookie seventh-rounder failed to record a catch for the fifth time in 10 regular-season games, with one of his intended passes from Daniel Jones being intercepted by Michael Taaffe midway through the second quarter. Gould is working through a toe injury, so Burks could step into a bigger role on offense if the former is unable to play against the Texans on Thursday.

items.head: Taking over larger role
items.body: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbook-Ikhine is also on the roster.

items.head: Notches one reception in Week 9
items.body: Burks played 17 of the Colts' 64 offensive snaps in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys, finishing with a zero-yard reception on his lone target. A rookie seventh-round pick out of Oklahoma, Burks has seen sparse playing time through the Colts' first nine games. He's logged less than one-third of the snaps in each of those contests and has posted a 6-60-0 receiving line on nine targets go with 21 yards on three carries. Despite his modest output to date, Burks could nonetheless be primed for more opportunities in the Indianapolis passing game over the second half of the season. Tight end Tyler Warren will likely rank as the team's top pass-catching option, but the Colts should have plenty of targets left over after trading away Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. Meanwhile, top wideout Alec Pierce (heel) lacks a clear timeline to return from injured reserve.

items.head: Churns out 37 yards in Week 10 loss
items.body: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday. Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

items.head: Zero catches in return from six-game absence
items.body: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. Njoku's snap count Monday was predictably capped, seeing as he was on injured reserve for the Chargers' six prior games while recovering from a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. Njoku could see more involvement in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Returns to action Monday
items.body: Njoku (fibula) is officially listed as active Monday night's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports. Since being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku -- who last played in Week 2 -- logged five consecutive limited practice listings before upgrading to full participation Saturday and being deemed questionable for Monday's contest. With his return to the lineup now confirmed, Njoku will bolster a TE corps that also includes Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. In his only full game with the team this season, Njoku caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Cardinals. Now that he's back in the mix, the 2017 first-rounder has an opportunity to reclaim enough of a role in the 0-8 Chargers offense to merit fantasy lineup consideration at his position in deeper fantasy formats going forward.

items.head: Returning for Monday night game
items.body: The Chargers activated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens. After completing his second week of practice upon being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku had been listed as questionable heading into Monday. The Chargers ultimately came away encouraged enough by how Njoku looked during practice to activate him, giving the team a third option at tight end for the Week 11 matchup. Due to his blocking prowess, Charlie Kolar will likely lead the position group in snaps Monday, but Njoku could usurp Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' top pass-catching tight end as he takes the field for the first time since Week 2.

items.head: David Njoku (injury) is Active
items.body: The Chargers reinstated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Questionable to face Baltimore
items.body: Njoku (fibula) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Ravens. Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.

items.head: Logs another limited practice
items.body: Njoku (fibula), who is still on IR, was limited in practice Friday. Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return -- in his lone full game of the season so far (Week 1 against Arizona), he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards.

items.head: Limited at practice
items.body: Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday. Njoku remained limited at the team's first practice of the week as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The tight end was a limited participant at the team's three practices last week, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Ravens.

items.head: Not activated ahead of Week 9
items.body: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log. Njoku returned to practice this week, but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

items.head: Only one catch in Week 10 win
items.body: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore. Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, and the return of the latter has squeezed Gadsden out of the gameplan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Returns Monday night
items.body: Gadsden (eye) returned to Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Questionable to return Monday
items.body: Gadsden (eye) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Only two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests).
