The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

items.head: Five snags in defeat
items.body: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.

items.head: Active in Week 8
items.body: Gadsden is active for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Rams. The second-year tight end has had a relatively quiet first season to date in coordinator Mike McDaniel's offense, posting a 12-103-1 line on 21 targets through six games. Gadsden did get back on the Chargers' offense's radar before the Week 7 bye, recording three receptions for 17 yards on five targets over 33 snaps in Week 6 against the Chiefs after being blanked over 39 plays in Week 5 against the Broncos. It remains to be seen if Los Angeles, which declined to make a change at playcaller during the bye, cooked up some improvements during the idle week, and if Gadsden will be more involved moving forward after flashing plenty of upside as a rookie in 2025 with a 49-664-3 line across 15 regular-season contests.

items.head: Hauls in two passes vs. Baltimore
items.body: Kolar caught two of three passes for 16 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. Kolar's 41 offensive snaps were by far the most among Chargers tight ends, well ahead of a returning David Njoku (19) and Oronde Gadsden (12), although the latter briefly left Monday's game due to an eye injury. That said, Kolar was held to two catches or fewer for the second time in three games, and he has not seen a red zone target from Justin Herbert since Week 6 against the Chiefs. Kolar has amassed a 15-145-0 receiving line on 23 targets across seven regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Tallies three catches against Houston
items.body: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

items.head: One catch against Rams
items.body: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

items.head: Tallies two catches against Baltimore
items.body: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (1), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell will continue to operate in rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Totals 36 yards against Houston
items.body: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets. The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

items.head: Leads team in rushing in loss
items.body: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.

items.head: Minimal impact in Week 10 win
items.body: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Cleared to face former team
items.body: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens. Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.

items.head: Keaton Mitchell (injury) is Active
items.body: Mitchell (hip) remained limited at practice Friday.

items.head: Limited in practice again
items.body: Mitchell (hip) remained limited at practice Friday. It's a new injury for Mitchell, who was also limited Thursday when the Chargers filed their first practice report for the upcoming Monday night game at Baltimore. He'll have some extra motivation, facing his former team in primetime as his current team seeks its first win of the season.

items.head: Limited by hip issue Thursday
items.body: Mitchell (hip) was limited at practice Thursday. In this past Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Mitchell carried seven times for 33 yards and caught three of his four targets for 34 yards, while losing a fumble.The 24-year-old, who is currently operating in a backfield time share with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal in his first campaign with the Chargers, now has two more chances to upgrade his practice participation level ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Leads Chargers RBs with 67 yards
items.body: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble. Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

items.head: Totals 23 yards in loss to Rams
items.body: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

items.head: Sits out practice again
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was a non-participant in Tuesday's practice.

items.head: Estimated as DNP on Monday
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant on Monday's practice report. After missing Sunday's loss to the Browns, Harrison opened the new week with another missed practice due to his hamstring issue. If he's unable to return in time for Thursday night's game against the Colts on a short week, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell would likely soak up the vast majority of the snaps at wideout.

items.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. (Hamstring) is Out
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.

items.head: Not seen at Friday's practice
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Harrison also missed Thursday's session, so the WRs apparent absence Friday doesn't bode well for his chances of playing Sunday against the Browns. If Harrison ends up out this weekend, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte would be available to handle WR targets that don't go to top option Nico Collins.

items.head: Downgrades to 'DNP' Thursday
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.head: Dealing with hamstring injury
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. It's a new injury for the Texans' newest wideout, who has produced just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets through three games with Houston. Harrison ran just 14 routes on 40 dropbacks last Sunday against the Chargers, tying him with Kayshon Boutte for fourth among Texans wideouts. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell appear to have emerged as the Nos. 2 and 3 receivers behind Nico Collins.

items.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.head: Two catches during blowout win
items.body: Harrison caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Harrison ranked seventh on the team in targets, and although C.J. Stroud connected with four different wide receivers for five total touchdowns, Harrison was not one of them. Harrison has now reeled in six of 11 targets for 60 yards and a score over three contests with the Texans, and he will remain hard to trust from a fantasy perspective in Week 10 versus Cleveland.

items.head: Luther Burden III (injury) is Active
items.body: Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.

items.head: Back at practice Monday
items.body: Burden (concussion) was spotted participating in the Bears' unofficial practice session Monday, AllCHGO.com reports.

items.head: Concussed in Sunday's win
items.body: Burden has a concussion, head coach Ben Johnson revealed after Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports. Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.

items.head: Exits late in Sunday's game
items.body: Burden (undisclosed) was helped off the field in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports. Burden took a big hit up high and fumbled the ball on the play on which he got injured. He eventually headed to the blue medical tent. Prior to getting hurt, Burden caught seven of nine targets for 97 yards and a touchdown, with most of his yards coming on a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.

items.head: Luther Burden III (Undisclosed) is Questionable
items.body: Burden (undisclosed) was helped off the field in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Stays busy in Week 8 win
items.body: Burden secured seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Burden tied Colston Loveland for the team lead in both receptions and targets, and he was on the receiving end of Caleb Williams' one touchdown pass of the night. The second-year wideout's scoring grab came from one yard out in the first quarter and was his third of the season, and Burden now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets over the last three games heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: What Broncos are doing to try to make Bo Nix more consistent throughout games
items.body: Nix has a knack for coming through big late in games, but the Broncos want him to play better earlier to lessen the fourth-quarter drama.

items.head: Tosses two TDs in Week 9 win
items.body: Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries. The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

items.head: Engineers another fourth-quarter comeback
items.body: Nix completed 20 of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City. He added four rushing yards on three carries and threw a two-point conversion to Jaylen Waddle. The Broncos were staring at a 24-13 deficit heading into the fourth quarter, but late comebacks are nothing new for Nix. The QB hit Nate Adkins for a two-yard score with about nine minutes left before connecting with Jonah Coleman on a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up the game-winning TD plunge by the rookie RB just after the two-minute warning. It's the 15th time that Nix has led Denver on a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime, the most by any quarterback in the first three seasons of his career since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970. While he's thrown multiple TDs just twice in the first eight games of the season, Nix has gone five straight contests without tossing an INT. He'll take a 9:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 road tilt against the Panthers.

items.head: Solid production with three catches
items.body: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

items.head: Logs full practice listing Friday
items.body: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation. After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.

items.head: Rashod Bateman (injury) is Active
items.body: Bateman (calf) was limited in practice Thursday.

items.head: Limited practice Thursday
items.body: Bateman (calf) was limited  in practice Thursday. Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully, and thus avoid an injury designation, prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.

items.head: Rashod Bateman (Calf) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Catches 22-yard pass in loss
items.body: Bateman caught one of three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills. Bateman actually led the Ravens in receiving yards on a day in which three quarterbacks attempted passes for Baltimore. Since posting a 7-88-1 receiving line in Week 2 against the Saints, Bateman has totaled 12 grabs for 200 yards and no scores over his last six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal while Zay Flowers is healthy.

items.head: Career-high yardage total in loss
items.body: Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

items.head: One reception in Week 10 win
items.body: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a  night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest number of receptions with big plays, but clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

items.head: Lone catch goes for 58-yard TD
items.body: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

items.head: Four grabs in loss to Rams
items.body: Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Johnston's four grabs marked a new personal single-game high through six games this season. One of the least efficient wideouts in the league, Johnston entered Sunday with just eight grabs for 165 yards on 22 targets. He hasn't been playable in fantasy football for weeks and will square off with a stingy Houston secondary in Week 9.

items.head: Bolts getting reinforcements for Week 8
items.body: Johnston's role in the passing game will shrink slightly in Week 8 against the Rams given that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) have been cleared to play, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports. Both Johnston and McConkey were sidelined for Week 5, but the latter entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 6 loss to the Chiefs. Johnston logged 17 targets through his first three games of the regular season, although he's seen only five passes from Justin Herbert over his last two outings, which Johnston turned into two catches for 101 yards. The Chargers are averaging only 168.2 passing yards per game this season -- which ranks 28th in the NFL -- and they face a Rams defense that boasts the fourth-best pass defense in the league (186.3 passing yards allowed per game).

items.head: Career-best yardage total in win
items.body: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.

items.head: Full practice participant
items.body: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice. After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

items.head: Tre' Harris (injury) is Active
items.body: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.

items.head: Dealing with shoulder issue
items.body: Harris (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday. With teammate Ladd McConkey sidelined by a back injury in Week 9, Harris played 59 of the Chargers' 68 offensive snaps, drawing a team-high seven targets. It seems like he may have picked up an injury of his own along the way though, which makes his availability for Week 10 worth monitoring. He'll have two more chances to manage a full practice before the Chargers publish their last injury report of the week Saturday.

items.head: Tre' Harris (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Three catches in blowout loss
items.body: Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

items.head: Season-best effort in Brissett's debut
items.body: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

items.head: Efficient in first win of season
items.body: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.

items.head: Justin Herbert, defense help lift Chargers past Ravens on MNF
items.body: The Chargers' defense stifles Baltimore's running backs, and Justin Herbert steps up in Los Angeles' first win.

items.head: Five reasons why Chargers' offense, Justin Herbert have struggled in 2026 season
items.body: Are injuries the biggest reason behind the Chargers' offensive struggles? Are Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton both taking steps back? We looked at the tape for answers.

items.head: Not on injury report
items.body: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Likely to play through finger injury
items.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh says X-rays on QB Justin Herbert's finger negative
items.body: X-rays on the injured middle finger of Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert's left hand came back negative for a fracture, coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday.

items.head: Impressive in team debut
items.body: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

items.head: Ravens QB Jacoby Brissett immersed in 'crash course' for Chargers tilt
items.body: New Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett says he's focused on Monday's game against the Chargers, not the team's plans at quarterback for the remainder of the season.

items.head: In line to start next Monday
items.body: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports. Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who is currently on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into his approach to a potential return to action.

items.head: Jacoby Brissett brings hope but realistic expectations for spiraling Ravens
items.body: The Ravens know what they're getting in acquiring veteran journeyman QB, but does Jacoby Brissett know what he's in for?

items.head: Shipped to Baltimore
items.body: The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals that will send Brissett to Baltimore, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The deal is expected to be completed over the weekend. Brissett was set to become a free agent this offseason and was demoted from the starting role earlier this week, making him an expendable piece for the Cardinals, who will move forward with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck as their quarterbacks. Baltimore, meanwhile, had a critical need for an experienced signal-caller after losing Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (foot) to injuries that will send both quarterbacks to injured reserve and potentially keep them out for the rest of the season, so Brissett will fill a void. Since the trade won't be made official for a few more days, Brissett won't be available for the Ravens' Thursday night game against the Jaguars. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will direct the Baltimore offense against Jacksonville, but Brissett could step in as the Ravens' new starter beginning with a Week 10 matchup against the Chargers.

items.head: Loses starting gig, now No. 3 QB
items.body: Head coach Mike LaFleur said that Brissett will be removed from the starting role and serve as the Cardinals' No. 3 quarterback in Sunday's game in Seattle, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. The Cardinals will move forward with Gardner Minshew as their starting quarterback, after he came on in relief of a struggling Brissett in Week 8 against Dallas and three touchdown passes en route to leading Arizona to a come-from-behind 33-30 victory in overtime. After putting up gaudy numbers over 12 starts in a pass-happy Arizona offense in 2025, Brissett had taken a notable step back statistically through the first eight games of this season, completing 63.3 percent of his passes for 1,719 yards (5.6 YPA), 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions to go with 87 yards and another score on the ground. Rather than serving as the direct backup to Minshew, the 33-year-old Brissett will drop to third on the depth chart in order for rookie third-round pick Carson Beck to be active on game days and potentially see his first NFL action later on this season.

items.head: Gets pulled early in Week 8
items.body: Brissett completed 10 of 23 passes for 118 yards, no touchdowns and one interception and turned three carries into seven yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win at Dallas. He also was pulled for backup QB Gardner Minshew near the end of the third quarter. At the time of Brissett's last offensive snap with 3:38 left in the third quarter, the Cardinals were trailing 17-3, after which Minshew led the team on four straight TD drives to force overtime. Along with a Week 2 stinker against the Seahawks -- when he went 17-for-28 passing for 95 yards, one TD and one INT -- this marked one of Brissett's two least productive outings of the season. Afterward, head coach Mike LaFleur told Darren Urban of the team's official site that he won't name a Week 9 starter between Brissett and Minshew just yet, only saying, "I thought we needed a spark." Considering the considerable influence Minshew had on Arizona's third win of 2026, it wouldn't be surprising if he's under center instead of Brissett next Sunday in Seattle.

items.head: Two catches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

items.head: Set for key role again?
items.body: Dike may have a significant role on offense with Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out for Sunday's game against Jacksonville. Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again this Sunday.

items.head: Three grabs against Kansas City
items.body: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs. Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. Dotson is fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. He's not a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

items.head: Two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

items.head: Secures two catches in loss
items.body: Dotson caught two of five targets for 95 yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay. Dotson and the rest of the Falcons offense were held in check for the majority of Sunday's loss. The wide receiver did provide Atlanta's biggest highlight play of the day, connecting with quarterback Michael Penix for a 76-yard gain on the team's final possession of the day in the fourth quarter. Dotson's 95 yards were a season high, and he has now reeled in 14 of 31 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

items.head: Salvages night with two TDs
items.body: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry has now failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

items.head: Sources: Ravens not expected to deal RB Derrick Henry before NFL trade deadline
items.body: Ravens RB Derrick Henry is not expected to be traded by the NFL trade deadline, league sources told ESPN.

items.head: Another tough night in loss
items.body: Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. He also completed one pass attempt for minus-3 yards. With Joe Fagnano under center, the Jaguars unsurprisingly had the luxury of loading up to slow down Henry, and Jacksonville already came into the contest boasting an elite run defense to begin with. Henry therefore ran into a proverbial brick wall for most of the night, and he finished under 60 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive game. However, help is on the way, as impending trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett could be ready to make his first start for the Ravens as soon as a Week 10 home matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

items.head: Rushing TD in loss
items.body: Henry rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Bills on Sunday. It was a nightmare of an afternoon for the Ravens offense, which lost both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) during the first half and struggled to move the ball with emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano at the helm. Henry's rushing opportunities ultimately suffered as Baltimore's deficit grew, but he managed to punch in a two-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter before matters got out of hand. It's been a relatively rough three-game stretch for Henry following a 102-yard effort on the ground against the Falcons in Week 5, and with reports emerging Jackson will be placed on injured reserve, the talented back's best hope for reasonable game scripts for the foreseeable future lies in Huntley's ability to regain health.

items.head: Sees one target in loss to Detroit
items.body: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions. The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of snaps, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. He's also been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. Raridon is averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

items.head: Produces 52 yards in Week 9 loss
items.body: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

items.head: Quiet Sunday despite extended opportunity
items.body: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.

items.head: Reaches end zone in blowout win
items.body: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers. Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

items.head: Records 34-yard touchdown grab vs. Las Vegas
items.body: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday. It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count, when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock on a 34-yard touchdown pass late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 receiving line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next game will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Three grabs vs. Arizona
items.body: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (oblique), but the former is dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. If that were the case, then Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the production floors of Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

items.head: Scores TD on only Week 8 reception
items.body: Kupp caught one of three targets for a seven-yard touchdown Monday in a loss to the Bears. Kupp had another low target share, but he at least made the most of his only catch by hauling in a seven-yard TD early in the fourth quarter. That score probably isn't going to be enough to inspire confidence in him in fantasy, though, given that the veteran wideout has drawn three or fewer targets in six of his eight games this season. Kupp's seven receiving yards Monday also were a season-low mark, and there simply doesn't seem to be much room for any wideout aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to regularly find success in Seattle's offense given Smith-Njigba's massive target share. With that said, Kupp at least will have a favorable matchup in Week 9, as he'll face an Arizona defense that has surrendered 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

items.head: No production in Week 10
items.body: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

items.head: Hauls in second TD of 2026
items.body: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on a bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share would take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

items.head: Cleared for action
items.body: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.

items.head: No practice due to illness
items.body: Higbee didn't practice Wednesday due to an illness, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports. With Higbee's addition to the Rams' Week 10 injury report Thursday, the team's top three tight ends on the active roster are dealing with health concerns, as Colby Parkinson has been limited by a rib injury, while Davis Allen downgraded from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later due to an oblique issue. As a result, Friday's practice report will be telling for who among the trio may be available Sunday in Arizona.

items.head: Just one catch in Week 9 victory
items.body: Higbee caught one of five targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

items.head: Another quiet performance Week 8
items.body: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory. Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

items.head: Logs two catches against Arizona
items.body: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the one-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the gameplan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes on 25 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

items.head: Ready to play
items.body: Colby Parkinson (rib) and Tyler Higbee (illness) have been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Parkinson hasn't shown much hint of matching last year's TD-fueled fantasy production, but he could see more targets in the coming weeks with both Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are the favorites for WR snaps, likely leaving the RBs and TEs to handle a larger-than-usual portion of Matthew Stafford's targets. Of course, the Rams will probably want to run the ball more often while their top receiving weapons are sidelined.

items.head: Remains limited in practice
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) was limited at Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports. While Parkinson continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps due to the rib issue that sidelined him in Week 8 against the Chargers, fellow TE Tyler Higbee showed up on Thursday's injury report as a DNP due to an illness, and reserve option Davis Allen went from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later. Friday's practice report will unveil the odds of each player to suit up Sunday at Arizona.

items.head: Still limited by ribs
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Parkinson has seemingly been banged up all season, and the ribs are just the latest issue for the tight end. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) vacating more than 45 percent of the Rams' targets, Los Angeles figures to lean heavily on its tight ends to try and get by without its top two receivers and top pass-catching tight end. Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will likely have prominent every-down roles in the coming weeks.

items.head: Grabs all four targets Week 9
items.body: Parkinson notched four catches for 13 yards on four targets in a 20-13 win over Washington on Sunday. Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles in receptions, though he didn't turn them into many yards. Still, it was his third straight contest with at least four catches, so Parkinson looks to be developing into a favorite target of QB Matthew Stafford. That could come in handy in Week 10 and beyond, as Stafford is going to need to turn to other pass catchers to help make up for the massive production being lost in the absence of Puka Nacua, who is expected to land on IR due to a knee injury.

items.head: Active versus Washington
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Commanders. Parkinson, who was inactive in Week 8, managed to log a limited practice Friday, before being listed as questionable for the contest. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) -- who was initially slated to return to action this week -- but subsequently ruled out -- still not in the mix, the return of Parkinson -- who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played -- is a welcome boost to a Rams TE corps that also includes Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare.

items.head: Still DNP on Thursday
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports. Parkinson hasn't practiced since being injured in Week 7, and he looks headed for a possible second straight absence. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) looking like he has a chance to return from injured reserve Sunday against the Commanders, it could be Ferguson, Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen handling tight-end duties.

items.head: No catches against Carolina
items.body: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. Fant failed to connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 receiving line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.head: Upgrades to full Thursday
items.body: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice. Fant was limited at Wednesday's practice, but the veteran TE faced no limitations Thursday, suggesting that he'll be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He has worked as the Saints' No. 2 option at the position behind Juwan Johnson.

items.head: Noah Fant (injury) is Active
items.body: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.

items.head: Working through back issue
items.body: Fant (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. Fant may have tweaked his back during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9, when he finished with one catch on two targets for 12 yards. He'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's NFC South tilt against the Panthers. Fant has accumulated 12 catches on 18 targets for 96 yards and three touchdowns through seven regular-season games.

items.head: Noah Fant (Back) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: One catch in Week 9 win
items.body: Fant caught one pass for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland. The veteran tight end logged 47 percent of the offensive snaps but is mainly a blocker at tight end, while Juwan Johnson handles most of the pass-catching duties. Fant has four catches for 30 yards over his last four games and is not even remotely on the fantasy radar.

items.head: Quiet in Week 10 loss
items.body: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second-most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets during Sunday's loss, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

items.head: Two catches against Cleveland
items.body: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

items.head: Five touches on offense vs. Indianapolis
items.body: Wright turned three carries into minus-two yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-three yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 yards per carry on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

items.head: Jaylen Wright (Quadriceps) is Out
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is listed as inactive Sunday against the Lions.

items.head: Not slated to play Sunday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) isn't in line to play in Sunday's game against the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Wright was held out of drills Wednesday due to a quad injury before capping Week 9 prep with back-to-back limited practices. That left him questionable to suit up Sunday, but assuming he's listed among the Dolphins' inactives about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be in street clothes this weekend. Kaytron Allen (quadriceps, questionable) and Carlos Washington are the other options to handle complementary reps behind No. 1 RB Ollie Gordon.

items.head: Will practice Friday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) will practice Friday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Averaging a miserable 1.9 yards per carry this season, Wright has no fantasy appeal other than being Ollie Gordon's ineffective backup.

items.head: Jaylen Wright (Quadriceps) is Questionable
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) will practice Friday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was limited in Thursday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports. Wright has been battling various issues all season and hasn't been effective when on the field, yet he's still operating as the Dolphins' lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon. Wright is averaging a microscopic 1.9 yards per carry this season.

items.head: Returns to practice Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is taking part in practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Wright didn't practice Wednesday, so Thursday's practice appearance is a step in the right direction, but the extent of his participation remains to be seen. Ollie Gordon has cemented himself as the lead back for the Dolphins, while Wright hasn't exceeded six touches in a game this season.

items.head: Does little with two touches
items.body: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-four yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, will likely come on special teams.

items.head: Kaytron Allen (Quadriceps) is Questionable
items.body: Allen (quadriceps) was a limited participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday.

items.head: Plays only four snaps in Week 10 loss
items.body: Ridley played four offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. Even though Carnell Tate (shoulder) was sidelined for a second consecutive week, Ridley was barely involved in the Titans' offensive gameplan. Ridley's four offensive snaps were by far a season low, and his role figures to shrink even more given that Tate is expected to return for Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22. Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) could be sidelined for that contest, although those offensive snaps would likely go to Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and even practice squad wideout Xavier Restrepo rather than Ridley.

items.head: Saleh calls Ridley's incident at Nashville airport 'minor miscommunication'
items.body: Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend that coach Robert Saleh called a "minor miscommunication" when asked about it after the team returned from the bye on Monday.

items.head: Involved in airport 'incident' over weekend
items.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports. Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.

items.head: Titans WR Calvin Ridley involved in incident at Nashville airport
items.body: Titans WR Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, details of which have not been released.

items.head: Good to go vs. Cincinnati
items.body: Ridley (hip) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. Ridley has been officially cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a hip injury. The veteran wide receiver has only five catches on 10 targets for 81 yards through six regular-season games, but he has the opportunity Sunday to operate in an expanded role due to the absence of rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder).

items.head: Expected to play in Week 8
items.body: Ridley (hip) is in line to play in Sunday's game against the Bengals, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. After sitting out in Week 7 due to a hip injury, Ridley kicked off Week 8 prep with back-to-back limited sessions before upgrading to full Friday and entering the weekend listed as questionable. Assuming he's deemed active about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be working in a Titans receiving corps without top WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) for the first time this season.

items.head: Questionable for Week 8
items.body: Ridley (hip) is officially questionable for Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati. Ridley didn't play last week due to a hip injury, but he was able to upgrade to full practice participation this Friday. Although Tennessee hasn't cleared him to suit up against the Bengals just yet, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports that the veteran wideout is set to play. Ridley's expected return is especially timely given that No. 1 wideout Carnell Tate (shoulder) has been ruled out.

items.head: No catches in blowout loss
items.body: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals. Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track Week 11 versus the Eagles.

items.head: Finds end zone on Sunday Night Football
items.body: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

items.head: Double-digit carries in win
items.body: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a prominent role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a rather valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.

items.head: Totals 19 yards against Tennessee
items.body: Perine rushed four times for 10 yards and caught his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans. The Bengals were chasing the Titans on the scoreboard much of the afternoon, and Chase Brown and Perine combined for just 16 carries, as Joe Burrow fired off 48 pass attempts. Perine is a touchdown-or-bust desperation RB3 in fantasy whose main value comes in the form of being Brown's backup. Cincinnati has been linked to a potential trade for a running back ahead of next week's deadline.

items.head: One catch on SNF
items.body: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals. Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

items.head: Reels in one pass during win
items.body: Gray caught one of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

items.head: Secures one reception in Week 9 win
items.body: Gray caught his only target for 11 yards Sunday in a 35-12 win against the Jets. Gray was a minor factor in the passing game, with his lone reception gaining 11 yards late in the third quarter. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Travis Kelce paced Kansas City with 72 receiving yards on four catches. Gray had a nice two-game run with a combined six catches for 97 yards across Weeks 6 and 7, but since then he's tallied just three receptions for 26 yards and a touchdown across his subsequent two games.

items.head: Short TD in loss to Denver
items.body: Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. The Chiefs' TE2 caught a four-yard score in the third quarter, his first touchdown of the season. Kansas City uses plenty of 12 personnel, deploying both Travis Kelce and Gray on offense, but Gray handles more of the blocking duties. On the season, he has 14 grabs for 173 yards and a touchdown. There isn't much meat on the bone here for fantasy purposes.

items.head: One catch in victory
items.body: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sideline while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, but that likely contributed his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

items.head: Back in game after getting checked for head injury
items.body: Coleman, who was evaluated for a head injury, was later cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Jets. Coleman previously headed to the blue medical tent after taking a big hit during the contest, per Matt Parrino of News 4 Buffalo. However, after getting checked out, Coleman returned to the field to rejoin a WR corps that also includes DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir.

items.head: Posts three receptions in Week 9 victory
items.body: Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets. Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Set to play in Week 9
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota. Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.

items.head: Limited at practice again
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Friday. Coleman is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4, listed as a limited participant Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder injury. There's been no indication it's serious, so Coleman seems on track to play Monday night at Minnesota. Fellow Bills wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) also is gearing up to play.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday. It's a new injury for Coleman, who is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4. With both DJ Moore (knee) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) healthy last Sunday against the Ravens, Coleman caught just one pass for four yards on three targets.

items.head: Keon Coleman (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.

items.head: Back on Philly's practice squad
items.body: Blue was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Monday. Blue was let go by the Eagles after suiting up for the team in Weeks 8 and 9, a span in which he didn't record a carry and caught his only target for nine yards. Now that he's back on the team's practice squad, the 2025 fifth-rounder will give Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley-led RB corps an added depth option ahead of Week 11 action.

items.head: Cut loose by Philly
items.body: The Eagles waived Blue on Tuesday. Philadelphia is now left with Saquon Barkley as the lone running back on its 53-man roster, but Elijah Mitchell will most likely be signed off the practice squad to replace Blue. After being signed off the practice squad himself in late October, Blue suited up in the Eagles' last two games but played just eight total snaps on offense while recording no rushing attempts and a nine-yard reception. His main contributions came on special teams, where he served as the Eagles' primary kickoff returner and gained 268 yards on 12 runbacks (22.3 average).

items.head: Behind Raiders fans' tribute to Fernando Mendoza's mother
items.body: Tom Joanides' social media campaign became a meaningful tribute when Mendoza scored in his first NFL start.

items.head: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza vows to learn from first NFL start, a loss to Seahawks
items.body: Fernando Mendoza completed 17-of-29 passes for 143 yards and had a passer rating of 71.5 in his first regular-season start for the Raiders.

items.head: Up and down in first NFL start
items.body: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.

items.head: Sources: Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza soon even if no Cousins trade
items.body: The Raiders had a plan to start Fernando Mendoza in Week 12 against the Browns even if they had not traded Kirk Cousins, sources told NFL Network.

items.head: Why the Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter
items.body: The Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter shortly after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.

items.head: Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders' sit-and-learn plan: Is he ready to start?
items.body: The Raiders had a plan for Fernando Mendoza in Year 1 and stuck to it as long as they could. But he's now QB1 earlier than expected, and they have to trust he's ready.

items.head: Fernando Mendoza relishes 'once-in-a-lifetime' opportunity as Raiders' QB1
items.body: No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza said Wednesday it's a "once-in-a-lifetime" opportunity to be the Raiders' starting quarterback, while his teammates and coach expressed their confidence in his ability to lead the offense.

items.head: Raiders name Fernando Mendoza starting QB after trading away Kirk Cousins
items.body: No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was officially named the Raiders' starting quarterback on Tuesday after the team traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.

items.head: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald 'optimistic' QB Sam Darnold returns after bye week
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is "optimistic" QB Sam Darnold will return to his starting role after the team's bye week.

items.head: Trending toward Week 12 return
items.body: Coach Mike Macdonald noted ahead of Seattle's Week 11 bye that the team is "really optimistic" Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) is "going to be able to get a full week's worth of work and be able to play" Nov. 29 against the 49ers, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

items.head: Expected back after Week 11 bye
items.body: Darnold (quadriceps), who won't play this coming Sunday at Las Vegas, is expected to return in Week 12 at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 after a Week 11 bye, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports. Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

items.head: Not ready to return in Week 10
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Darnold (quadriceps) will be out another week, per John Boyle of the team's official site. Meanwhile, Macdonald noted that the Seahawks got a "good exam for Drew (Lock). He's dealing with an oblique, and I think it's something we can manage." Lock's status is thus worth monitoring ahead of this weekend's game against the Raiders, but Macdonald's comment suggests that the QB will be available to continue to fill in for Darnold, with Jalen Milroe in reserve.

items.head: Could miss Week 10
items.body: Darnold (quadriceps) may miss Seattle's Week 10 game at Las Vegas, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Darnold already has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, and the combination of the quadriceps injury and cracked ribs he suffered last Monday against the Bears is threatening to sideline him for multiple weeks. The Seahawks have a Week 11 bye on the schedule, so getting him healthy for the stretch run from late November through early January may sway the team's decision-making. As long as Darnold is out, Drew Lock (right elbow) will direct Seattle's offense.

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Head coach Mike Macdonald announced that Darnold won't play Sunday against the Cardinals due to a quadriceps injury, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports. In addition to a quad issue that Darnold sustained late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Macdonald revealed that the quarterback suffered a rib injury early in that contest. The pair of health concerns may have played a part in Darnold's subpar performance, which included 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception on 17-for-34 passing and two carries for 20 yards. With Darnold out for the first time since Week 2, backup QB Drew Lock will draw the Week 9 start under center for the Seahawks.

items.head: Middling numbers in Week 8 loss
items.body: Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding two rushes for 20 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Darnold averaged just 5.5 yards per attempt and took three sacks from a Bears defense that made an impact addition in Jeffery Simmons on Thursday via trade with the Titans. Darnold's 50.0 percent completion rate was a season low for him in non-injury-shortened games, and the veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the sixth consecutive contest. Darnold did toss multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 4, connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43 yards) and Cooper Kupp (seven yards) for his pair of scoring strikes. Darnold will take an unsightly 10:9 TD:INT heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.body: inactive

items.head: Jelani Woods (Coach's Decision) is Out

items.head: Set to fill backup spot
items.body: Gabriel "will serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest with Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.

items.head: Ja'Tavion Sanders (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Needs thumb surgery, IR possible
items.body: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Addison requires surgery on his thumb and is a candidate for injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Jordan Addison (Thumb) is Out
items.body: Addison (thumb), who listed is questionable for Sunday's contest at Green Bay, is in line to be a game-time decision, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Jordan Addison (Thumb) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Solid yardage on two catches
items.body: Addison secured two of three targets for 28 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.

items.head: Leads team in receiving in loss
items.body: Addison caught three of eight targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions. Addison's big play was a 51-yard catch over the top of the defense in the fourth quarter to set the offense up at the 10-yard line. T.J. Hockenson scored a go-ahead touchdown two plays later. Addison's eight targets on the day were one fewer than Justin Jefferson, but it was the former who paced the team in receiving yards. Playing in a Minnesota offense that doesn't push the ball down the field much or focus on its outside receivers, Addison has just 16 catches for 249 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets through six games this season. He'll be a fantasy WR4 with upside next Monday night against a leaky Bills secondary.

items.head: Max Brosmer (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Joining active roster
items.body: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday. Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

items.head: Falcons WR Drake London cleared after being checked for concussion
items.body: Falcons wide receiver Drake London has been cleared after being removed from Sunday's game against the Chiefs late with a possible concussion.

items.head: Cleared of head injury
items.body: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

items.head: Drake London (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: London is being evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.

items.head: Leading receiver in Week 9 loss
items.body: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

items.head: Forgettable afternoon in loss
items.body: London brought in one of six targets for eight yards in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. Michael Penix was picked off four times by the Buccaneers' defense throughout the rainy afternoon while completing only 33.3 percent of his passes, so London's near career-worst numbers were a bit more understandable in that context. The talented wideout had come into the day with at least 62 receiving yards in five straight contests, and he should have a chance to bounce back when the Falcons face off with the Bengals in Madrid next Sunday.
