items.head: Returns Sunday
items.body: London (head) returned to Sunday's contest at Tampa Bay, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports. London hit the sideline to be tested for a possible concussion but has since been cleared to return to the contest. He had no catches (on two targets) at the time of his exit in the middle of the first quarter.

items.head: Possible concussion Sunday
items.body: London is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports. QB Michael Penix was intercepted on a pass intended for London in the middle of the first quarter, after which the wide receiver hit the sidelines for the concussion check. London was sitting on no catches (on two targets) at the time of his departure.

items.head: Shane Buechele (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: The Bills elevated Buechele from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

items.head: Set to join Tampa Bay practice squad
items.body: Rush is in line to sign with the Buccaneers' practice squad, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. Rush will give Tampa Bay added QB depth with starter Baker Mayfield dealing with an injury to his foot and ankle area that he sustained Sunday. Jalon Daniels is currently Mayfield's top backup ahead of Week 11 action, while Easton Stick is on the team's practice squad.

items.head: TBD on whether surgery is needed
items.body: Coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that it has yet to be determined whether Willis (abdomen) will need surgery to address his groin/core injury.David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

items.head: Dolphins hopeful QB Malik Willis will be back this season
items.body: Coach Jeff Hafley said Miami sees Malik Willis as its starter regardless of when he returns from his groin injury.

items.head: Surgery not ruled out
items.body: The Dolphins hope Willis (abdomen) will return this year but haven't ruled out season-ending surgery, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports. With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury, and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "he'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

items.head: Expected back this season
items.body: Though Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Wednesday that he doesn't have a timetable for the potential return of Willis (abdomen), he does expect the QB back at some point this season, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Headed for IR with core-muscle injury
items.body: The Dolphins are expected to place Willis on injured reserve after an MRI on Monday revealed a core-muscle injury, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Malik Willis (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Pedestrian numbers in Week 9 loss
items.body: Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for seven yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Willis was back under 200 passing yards for the first time in three games, and he failed to throw at least one touchdown pass for the first time since Week 4. The 2022 third-round pick connected with seven different targets overall, and following the game, Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post reported that Willis was dealing with both groin tightness and a tight hamstring during the game. Willis and the Dolphins' Week 10 matchup is a Colts team that could trade away multiple key players before Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Tosses two TDs in loss to Pats
items.body: Willis completed 21 of 32 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England. He gained two rushing yards on his only carry. The 27-year-old QB hit Malik Washington for a one-yard score just before halftime to give the Dolphins a 13-3 lead, but Willis' 35-yard strike to Kevin Coleman late in the fourth quarter was too little, too late after the Patriots dominated the second half. After throwing just one touchdown over the first four games of the season, Willis has a 5:3 TD:INT in the last three contests while adding two scores on the ground. He'll likely need to be even more productive in Week 9 as he attempts to keep pace with Jared Goff and the Lions.

items.head: Titans getting more after adding more to QB Cam Ward's plate
items.body: The Titans offense has functioned better since putting more on quarterback Cam Ward's plate, even if it hasn't translated to more wins yet.

items.head: Produces two TDs in loss to Jags
items.body: Ward completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.

items.head: Where does Cam Ward stand coming out of the bye?
items.body: Ward has nine games left to convince the Titans he should be their QB when they open the new stadium in 2027.

items.head: First 300-yard passing game in OT loss
items.body: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion. Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

items.head: Goes without reception in Week 10
items.body: Dulcich failed to haul in either of his two targets while logging 42 of 69 offensive snaps in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord threw for 209 yards on 32 attempts in his first NFL start, but he couldn't forge much of a connection with Dulcich, who was held without a catch for the second time this season. With Malik Willis (core) out for at least three more contests while on injured reserve, Dulcich will have more time to build a rapport with McCord, but the tight end was far from a reliable fantasy option even when Willis was directing the offense. Despite playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Dolphins' nine games, Dulcich has been limited to 24 receptions for 270 yards and has yet to find the end zone.

items.head: Quiet in loss to Detroit
items.body: Dulcich caught two of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

items.head: Four grabs in Week 8 loss
items.body: Dulcich caught four of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Dulcich has yet to score a touchdown this season, but the tight end is settling in as one of Malik Willis' favorite targets. He has at least four catches in four of his last five games but has reached 50 receiving yards in just two of seven contests. Dulcich is in the large bucket of low-floor, low-ceiling TE2 options in fantasy, but he does get a plus Week 9 draw against the Lions.

items.head: Cleared for Week 8
items.body: Dulcich (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. After back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Dulcich upgraded to full Friday and is in the clear for Sunday. Dulcich is coming off a productive 5-86-0 receiving line on five targets last Sunday against the Jets.

items.head: Giants QB J.J. McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers
items.body: After only three starts and four games playing for New York, the quarterback's numbers are staggering.

items.head: Impressive numbers in loss
items.body: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

items.head: Won't be limited in Week 10
items.body: McCarthy (hip pointer) is "good to go" and isn't expected to be limited for Thursday's game against the Commanders, James Palmer of NFL Network reports. McCarthy missed much of the third quarter of this past Sunday's win at Philadelphia due to a hip pointer but was able to return to action, completing 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing four times for 22 yards. Considering he ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, he seemingly was in the clear for Thursday's matchup, and Palmer's report indicates McCarthy will take on every rep, leaving Jameis Winston as the No. 2 on the sidelines.

items.head: Practices fully, ready for Thursday
items.body: McCarthy (hip) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice.

items.head: Taking part in practice Tuesday
items.body: McCarthy (hip) was spotted on the field for the media-access portion of Tuesday's practice, Art Stapleton of The Bergen Record reports.

items.head: Managing hip issue
items.body: McCarthy (hip) is listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. McCarthy exited Sunday's win at Philadelphia for a spell in the third quarter due to a hip injury but returned to action. Head coach John Harbaugh told Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News on Monday that McCarthy has a hip pointer but is expected to play Thursday versus the Commanders. McCarthy likely will need to be listed as full Tuesday and/or Wednesday to head into Week 10 action without a designation.

items.head: Giants 'feel fairly good' about QB J.J. McCarthy (hip) playing Thursday
items.body: Giants coach John Harbaugh says he feels "fairly good" about quarterback J.J. McCarthy's availability this week after he suffered a hip injury in Sunday's win against the Eagles.

items.head: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
items.body: The Pittsburgh passer is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."

items.head: Two more TD passes
items.body: Rodgers completed 15 of 29 passes for 143 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed two times for minus-1 yard during Sunday's 38-18 loss at Cincinnati.

items.head: Aaron Rodgers makes fantasy football history, now No. 2 on all-time scoring list
items.body: With Aaron Rodgers' score on Sunday, he reaches another fantasy football accolade in his HOF-worthy career.

items.head: Three catches versus Las Vegas
items.body: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

items.head: Two short TDs against Arizona
items.body: Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown. Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

items.head: Pair of catches in Week 8 loss
items.body: Barner brought in two of five targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Barner was third in receiving yards and targets, although the tight end still finished below 30 receiving yards for the sixth time this season. Barner remained in a minor role despite the fact the Seahawks were down Rashid Shaheed (knee), and with 21 receptions for 203 yards and zero touchdowns, the third-year pro remains behind the pace of his career-best 52-519-6 line from last season. Barner will look to capitalize on a favorable matchup against the Cardinals defense in a Week 9 home matchup on Sunday.

items.head: One catch in return to lineup
items.body: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. After missing the previous tow games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

items.head: Full practice Wednesday
items.body: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Shaheed suffered a knee injury during a Week 7 win against the Chiefs and missed the last two games as a result. Now that he's unhindered on the practice field, though, he'll resume his standing as Seattle's No. 2 WR and primary kick and punt returner

items.head: Rashid Shaheed (injury) is Out
items.body: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

items.head: Rashid Shaheed (Knee) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Misses another practice
items.body: Shaheed (knee) didn't participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Shaheed has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from the knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 8 loss to Chicago. The wide receiver's chances to play Sunday versus Arizona seem thin, so Tory Horton could serve as the team's No. 3 option at wide receiver again in Week 9.

items.head: Rashid Shaheed (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Shaheed (knee) didn't participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.

items.head: DNP on Wednesday
items.body: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Shaheed missed Monday night's loss to the Bears, which allowed Tory Horton to log a season-high 43 offensive snaps, which he turned into a 3-26-0 receiving line on six targets. Horton would again be in line for WR3 duties if Shaheed needs to sit Sunday against Arizona.

items.head: Iffy for Week 9
items.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Tuesday that Shaheed (knee) has a chance to play Sunday against the Cardinals, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports. Shaheed was sidelined for the first time all season in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears, after his knee injury kept him from practicing throughout the week. In Shaheed's absence, Tory Horton handled elevated snaps as the Seahawks' No. 3 wideout behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, while George Holani served as the team's top kickoff returner. Shaheed may need to turn in a full practice at some point during Week 9 prep to put himself on track to return to action Sunday.

items.head: Two catches in loss
items.body: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

items.head: Three catches in loss
items.body: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.

items.head: Five grabs in Week 8 win
items.body: Mayer caught five of six targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. Mayer's six targets were second on the team behind Brock Bowers' 10, and only Bowers (26) ran more routes than Mayer's 20 on Kirk Cousins' 27 dropbacks. The tight end has just one touchdown this season but has remained an integral part of Las Vegas' passing attack. He's already surpassed his 2025 catches and yards totals, posting 36 grabs for 351 yards through eight games this season. Mayer will be a fantasy TE2 for next Sunday's date with the 49ers.

items.head: One catch in Week 10 win
items.body: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers. Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.

items.head: Touchdown streak snapped
items.body: Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta. Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.

items.head: Reaches end zone in OT victory
items.body: Gesicki caught four of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 43-36 overtime win against the Titans. Gesicki was able to reach the end zone for the fifth straight game, connecting with Joe Burrow for a 25-yard score in the fourth quarter. The tight end's four catches and 76 receiving yards were both his highest totals since Week 1 versus Tampa Bay. Gesicki has now caught 17 of 24 targets for 241 yards and six scores over seven contests to open the regular season.

items.head: Gets into end zone in loss
items.body: Metcalf brought in two of six targets for 54 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion catch in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night.

items.head: Stymied by Bengals in loss
items.body: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.

items.head: Four grabs in Week 10 loss
items.body: Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

items.head: Garners 18 touches in win
items.body: Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards and brought in eight of nine targets for 39 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. Brown averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry, but as customary, his rushing opportunities were capped in a Bengals offense that typically takes a pass-heavy approach irrespective of game script. Brown did benefit from that philosophy as a receiver, however, as he tied his second-highest total of receptions on the season. Brown's fantasy outlook will remain relatively modest for a Week 11 road matchup against the Commanders on Monday night, Nov. 23 thanks to Cincinnati's offensive approach.

items.head: Quiet in Week 9 win
items.body: Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

items.head: Solid all-around day in OT win
items.body: Brown rushed 12 times for 55 yards and brought in eight of nine targets for 46 yards in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over the Titans on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Brown led the Bengals in rushing with an efficient performance, and he finished with his best yardage total on the ground since Week 3. Brown's very busy day as a receiver was second only to his 11-catch, 71-yard effort against the Jaguars in Week 4, and his lost fumble, his second of the season, came early in the fourth quarter and led to a Titans touchdown. Brown is in line to fill  his usual voluminous dual role in a Week 9 international matchup against the Falcons in Madrid next Sunday.

items.head: Only seven touches in Week 10
items.body: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.

items.head: Spectacular night in win
items.body: Chase brought in 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Cincinnati. Chase posted one of his signature 200-yard performances, with Sunday night's qualifying as the fourth of his storied career and marking his third instance accomplishing it against an AFC North rival. Needless to say, all three components of Chase's receiving line led the Bengals by a wide margin on the night as well, and after failing to hit the century mark in yardage in any of the first six games of the season, the star wideout has recorded at least 141 receiving yards in three straight. Chase is now up to a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets across nine games heading into a Week 11 Monday night home road matchup against the Commanders on Nov. 23.

items.head: Dominates in Madrid
items.body: Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

items.head: First 100-yard game of season
items.body: Chase secured 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over the Titans on Sunday. Chase finally struck for his first 100-yard effort of the campaign in Sunday's wild win, finishing with team-high reception and target totals, as well as runner-up status in receiving yards. Chase was also on the receiving end of one of Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes, corralling the first one of the day from 30 yards out early in the second quarter. Chase has now scored in three straight games, and after season-best totals across all three components of his receiving line Sunday, the All-Pro receiver will head into a Week 9 matchup against the Falcons in Madrid with no shortage of momentum.

items.head: Four catches versus Houston
items.body: Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans. A running back in name only, Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79 empty yards, while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games where the Browns are projected to play from behind.

items.head: Notches 11 touches in OT loss
items.body: Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards while catching three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss against the Saints. Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.

items.head: Records six grabs in loss
items.body: Sampson rushed one time for seven yards and caught six of eight targets for 62 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. Sampson was out-carried 11 to one by Quinshon Judkins, but the former has carved out a role as the preferred pass-catching back for Cleveland since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. Over the last two games, Sampson has turned 11 targets into nine catches for 94 yards while adding seven carries for 52 yards. Sampson will have some PPR fantasy appeal during weeks when the Browns are projected to trail on the scoreboard.

items.head: Reaches pay dirt in Week 10
items.body: Freiermuth recorded two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-18 loss in Cincinnati. Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option (five in his nine appearances).

items.head: Active in Week 10
items.body: Freiermuth (illness) is active for Sunday's game at Cincinnati, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

items.head: Pat Freiermuth (Illness) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Two catches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

items.head: Game-winning TD in overtime win
items.body: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four games. With Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.head: Five catches in team debut
items.body: Allen brought in five of seven targets for 61 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Allen will play for the 49ers in Sunday's game at Dallas after being acquired in a trade earlier this week, David Lombardi of The San Francisco Standard reports.

items.head: Veteran WR Keenan Allen feeling energized by trade to 49ers
items.body: Keenan Allen said while he wasn't expected to get traded, landing with a contending team in the 49ers has him feeling energized.

items.head: Fantasy impacts of the NFL trade deadline: What to know on Cousins, Allen trades
items.body: NFL trade deadline day is here. We have the latest fantasy news and analysis for every key deal.

items.head: Shipped to San Francisco
items.body: The 49ers acquired Allen from the Colts on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Four catches in loss
items.body: Allen caught four of eight targets for 26 yards during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Allen led the team in targets, but he was only able to compile 26 yards, his lowest output since Week 2. The wide receiver hasn't reached the end zone in his last five games, and the Colts' offense as a whole has struggled mightily recently. On the year, Allen has reeled in 40 of 58 targets for 351 yards and one score over eight contests, and his next chance to reach paydirt will come in Week 10 versus the Dolphins.

items.head: Leads team in receiving in loss
items.body: Allen caught all seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars. The veteran wideout finished second on the team in targets, three behind Tyler Warren on a day Colts QBs attempted 30 passes. When on the field this season, Allen has been a consistent target-earner who runs routes that are friendly to quarterbacks in the short areas of the field. Not a big-play threat whatsoever at this stage of his career, Allen is averaging a career-low 9.0 yards per catch on 36 grabs this season. He has just one touchdown and is a low-upside WR4 for fantasy purposes headed into next Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

items.head: Goose egg in Week 10 win
items.body: Coker failed to catch any of his four targets in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. While it looked like Coker was going to be in line for a breakout 2026 season after his 8-138-2 receiving performance in the Week 1 opener, Coker has been held to 23 catches for 255 yards and one touchdown over his last seven games. At this point, he can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows something in the box score again. This was a pristine on-paper spot versus New Orleans in the dome, and next Sunday's home date against Baltimore won't be any easier.

items.head: Stays quiet in Week 9 loss
items.body: Coker caught four of five targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.

items.head: Six catches in Week 10 win
items.body: Kittle brought in six of nine targets for 74 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.

items.head: Four catches in Week 9 win
items.body: Kittle caught four of seven targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Kittle had at least three more targets than any teammate Sunday but finished 28 receiving yards shy of Jordan Watkins' team-leading total, while Brock Purdy's two touchdown passes went to Christian McCaffrey and Watkins. Sunday's output marked Kittle's third-lowest yardage total of the season, but the star TE recorded at least four catches for a seventh consecutive game. He'll look to add to his season totals of 38 catches for 483 yards and five touchdowns in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

items.head: Quiet in Mendoza's first start
items.body: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech actually led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

items.head: Four catches in defeat
items.body: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fourth time in the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Held catchless by Jets
items.body: Tucker did not catch his only target Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets. Despite quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 247 yards, Tucker had only one ball thrown his way. In fact, only one Raiders wideout -- Jalen Nailor -- had a reception, as Cousins targeted tight ends on 16 of his 26 passes. Tucker had caught either four or five passes in each of his prior six games and collected at least 97 receiving yards in three of those contests, though he finished below 45 yards in the other three. It's notable that he logged a season-low 52 percent offensive snap share against the Jets, but he should be in for better days ahead, beginning with a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

items.head: Totals 109 scrimmage yards, two TDs in win
items.body: Samuel rushed three times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 31 yards and another score in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.

items.head: Set to return in Week 10
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) practiced on a limited basis Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.

items.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. (Hamstring) is Out
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) was a limited practice participant Wednesday, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Trending toward practicing Wednesday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) is on track to return to practice Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports. That's a positive development for Samuel who logged a trio of 'DNPs' last week. His potential return this weekend against the Cowboys would be a welcome one for the 49ers' depleted WR corps. With that in mind, Mike Evans (Achilles) is viewed as iffy for the contest, so a key role in the team's passing attack could await Samuel if he is able to return for his first game action since Week 5.

items.head: Ruled out for Sunday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Neither Samuel nor Mike Evans (Achilles) made a serious bid to play in San Francisco's first game after a Week 8 bye. Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing are the healthy WRs on the active roster, with Demarcus Robinson (ankle) a candidate to come off injured reserve this week or next.

items.head: Misses open portion of practice
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) didn't participate in the early portion of Friday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. With Samuel absent from the initial stage of practice Friday after sitting out Wednesday and Thursday's sessions, he's trending toward an absence Sunday against the Raiders, as is fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles). Confirmation of the duo's status is set to arrive later Friday once the 49ers' final Week 9 injury report is posted.

items.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 144-yard quarter sparks Seahawks in win over Raiders
items.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, finished with a season-high 171 yards on eight catches, with 144 coming in the third quarter to help the Seahawks turn a three-point halftime deficit into a 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

items.head: Reels off season-high 171 yards
items.body: Smith-Njigba gathered in eight of 10 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 21-13 win at Las Vegas.

items.head: Season low in receiving yards
items.body: Smith-Njigba reeled in seven of 10 targets for 51 yards during Sunday's 17-3 win against the Cardinals. Smith-Njigba was working with backup QB Drew Lock for the third time this season, as the latter was filling in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib). The result was a season low in receiving yards, which was only the second time this season in which Smith-Njigba failed to reach the century mark. Despite the subpar outing for him, he surpassed 1,000 yards on the campaign for a third straight season, with eight games still to go. Darnold may also be sidelined next Sunday at Las Vegas, which again could impact Smith-Njigba's chances to produce as he has most weeks in 2026.

items.head: Another 100-yard effort in loss
items.body: Smith-Njigba brought in six of 11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Smith-Njigba was in his usual position of leading the Seahawks across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he crossed the 100-yard mark for the seventh time in eight games this season with a pair of catches on Seattle's final drive of the night. His target total also was his sixth double-digit tally of the campaign, and the absence of Rashid Shaheed (knee) helped reinforce JSN's downfield role even further. Smith-Njigba now will head into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday just 15 yards short of his third consecutive 1,000-yard campaign and only a touchdown shy of tying the career-high 10 he recorded over 17 regular-season games last season.

items.head: Solid with 17 touches Sunday
items.body: Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards and brought in his only target for four yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

items.head: Eclipses century mark in win
items.body: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately just managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.

items.head: Tops 20 carries again
items.body: Williams churned out 56 yards on 24 carries and notched one catch (on two targets) for one yard during Sunday's 33-30 overtime defeat to the Cardinals. After failing to crack 20 rushes in any of the Cowboys' first six games of the season, Williams now has two such outings over the last two weeks. However, he averaged a season low in a single contest with 2.3 YPC on Sunday, and his TD streak also was snapped at five outings. Williams has a stranglehold on Dallas' backfield with 134 carries to date, while the rest of the team's RBs have combined for 37 through eight weeks. Williams will seek better results next Sunday versus the wayward Colts on the road.

items.head: Another TD in high-scoring loss
items.body: Lamb secured seven of 13 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

items.head: Standout numbers again in win
items.body: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

items.head: Seven more catches in Week 8
items.body: Lamb recorded seven catches (on 11 targets) for 58 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals. QB Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' passing game couldn't get much going against Arizona's defense throughout Week 8, and Lamb thus put together one of his least productive outings of the campaign. Despite the very modest performance for his standard, Lamb still has a standout 60-709-6 line on 92 targets through the first eight contests, setting himself up nicely for his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard campaign. He next takes aim at the stumbling Colts next Sunday on the road.

items.head: Ties career high with five TDs in loss
items.body: Prescott completed 30 of 51 passes for 343 yards with five touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for seven yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. He also ran for a two-point conversion.

items.head: Dak Prescott: Cowboys can make playoffs without making trade
items.body: Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott thinks the Cowboys have enough talent to be a playoff team without a trade-deadline addition.

items.head: Another 300-yard tally in win
items.body: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

items.head: Records two total TDs on Sunday
items.body: Prescott was 19-for-29 passing for 195 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions while rushing seven times for 20 yards and one more TD during Sunday's 33-30 overtime defeat to the Cardinals. Arizona's defense had been plenty exploitable this season, allowing 243.7 yards per game and 17 TDs through the air to opposing QBs heading into Week 8 action. Even with his main skill-position talents available Sunday, though, Prescott didn't crack 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 1. He salvaged his day with his first TD on the ground of the campaign, which supplemented a nine-yard TD connection with WR Ryan Flournoy. Prescott and the Cowboys offense will look to get back on track next Sunday versus an exploitable Colts defense on the road.

items.head: Keeps rolling in wild Week 10 win
items.body: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added two carries for 21 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.

items.head: Three total TDs in Week 9 win
items.body: Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. He added seven rushing attempts for 40 yards and a touchdown. Purdy gave the 49ers a 14-0 lead with a one-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, then added a 12-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey in the second quarter and a 37-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins in the third. Unfazed by the numerous injuries to San Francisco's wide receivers, Purdy has a 17:5 TD:INT through the air to go with a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Cowboys. Having led the 49ers to a 7-1 record, the fourth-place finisher in the 2023 MVP race is making a strong case for the award again at the halfway point of the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Makes little impact in return
items.body: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.head: Returning to action Sunday
items.body: Etienne (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers. Etienne had been listed as questionable after the Saints activated him from injured reserve Saturday. His return gives New Orleans another option in the backfield for his first game action since Week 3.

items.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: The Saints activated Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.

items.head: May return in Week 10
items.body: Etienne (hamstring) said Friday that "the week of practice went well," and that he hopes to be active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Etienne (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.

items.head: Coach non-committal on Week 10 return
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the Saints haven't yet determined whether Etienne (hamstring) will return from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports. "We'll see," Moore said. "He's progressing well. We'll gather some more information and make a decision."

items.head: Not practicing yet
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports. Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

items.head: Career-high totals in return
items.body: Pickens brought in 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

items.head: Clear for return in Week 10
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.head: Trending toward Sunday return?
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) moved well in Thursday's practice, which coach Brian Schottenheimer said is a positive sign for the wide receiver's availability for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Another limited session
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports. As he was a week ago, Pickens continues to operate with practice restrictions, giving him just one more chance this week to get back to full Friday, at which point the Cowboys may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers. He's looking to limit his absence to only one contest due to a hamstring injury.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was in uniform and taking part in individual drills during Thursday's practice, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.

items.head: Expected to practice Wednesday
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) is expected to take part in Wednesday's practice, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.

items.head: Status for Week 10 remains uncertain
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) has a chance to play Sunday against San Francisco, but his practice reps will likely again be capped this week, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports. Pickens was limited in practice all of last week and ultimately didn't suit up Sunday against Indianapolis. There had been some optimism that he'd be able to participate in that contest, so there's likely a decent chance that he'll be able to return to action versus the 49ers. Nonetheless, Pickens could again be given a designation heading into this weekend if he doesn't manage at least one full practice before the Cowboys' final injury report is released Friday.

items.head: George Pickens (Hamstring) is Out
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.

items.head: Overshadowed by rookie in Week 10 loss
items.body: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.

items.head: Big day in OT win over Browns
items.body: Olave caught seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland. The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards once again, but Juwan Johnson was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD of the day. Olave is the clear top option in the New Orleans passing attack, but with Jordyn Tyson finally making his pro debut Sunday, secondaries may have someone else to worry about in the second half of the season. Olave will take a 56-734-2 line on 83 targets into a Week 10 battle against the Panthers.

items.head: Career-high receiving yardage tally in win
items.body: McCaffrey rushed 13 times for 62 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 161 yards and two more scores in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion pass.

items.head: Two TDs on 20 touches in Week 9
items.body: McCaffrey rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. McCaffrey got banged up in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Falcons, but a Week 8 bye allowed his hamstring to heal and the star running back handled 20 touches Sunday while scoring twice to bring his season total to 10 touchdowns. He capped San Francisco's opening drive with a one-yard touchdown run and added a 12-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter. Rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black led the 49ers with 70 rushing yards on 11 carries, but McCaffrey remains the lead back heading into a Week 10 trip to Dallas, during which CMC will try to extend a seven-game touchdown streak.

items.head: Full workload expected Sunday
items.body: McCaffrey is expected to take on a full workload Sunday against the Raiders, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. McCaffrey was limited to a 52 percent snap share when he missed a portion of the 49ers' Week 7 loss in Atlanta due to a left hamstring injury, but he still put up 13 touches for 100 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD. With the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he appears set to handle the 17.5 touches per game that he averaged in healthy outings in Weeks 1 through 6, which translated to 540 total yards and seven touchdowns.

items.head: Set to play Sunday
items.body: McCaffrey (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. McCaffrey was able to mix into drills Thursday as limited and again Friday, which was enough for him to gain clearance to suit up in Week 9. He was hampered by a left hamstring injury during the 49ers' last game in Week 7 in Atlanta, when he handled a season-low 52 percent snap share but still notched 100 yards from scrimmage and a rushing TD on 13 touches.

items.head: Practicing Friday
items.body: McCaffrey (hamstring) took part in the open portion of Friday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports. McCaffrey already has one capped session (Thursday) under his belt this week and again appears set to be listed as at least limited Friday, at which point the 49ers may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game versus the Raiders.

items.head: Officially limited Thursday
items.body: McCaffrey (hamstring) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. McCaffrey followed up Wednesday's lack of activity with some on-field work one day later, but he may need to practice fully Friday in order to avoid a designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders. He's tending to a left hamstring injury from a Week 7 loss in Atlanta, when he managed just a 52 percent snap share and churned out 100 yards from scrimmage and a rushing TD on 13 touches.

items.head: Christian McCaffrey (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: McCaffrey (hamstring) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Three TD passes despite receiver injuries
items.body: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Just one TD in Week 9 win
items.body: Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry. The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games, after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

items.head: Practices fully Wednesday
items.body: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports. Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ramas offense Sunday in Washington.

items.head: Managing arm soreness
items.body: Stafford left the locker room after Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers with a bag of ice wrapped on his right arm, and Rams coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday that the quarterback has been dealing with some arm soreness, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports. McVay added that he'll defer to Stafford on the topic of how he's feeling ahead of this weekend's game against the Commanders. In any case, the Rams will issue their first injury report of the week Wednesday, at which point it'll become clear if the QB's arm issue impacts his practice reps.

items.head: Subdued performance in Week 8 win
items.body: Stafford completed 17 of 25 passes for 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday. Stafford didn't have to take on too much with his team's defense largely keeping a still-reeling Chargers offense at bay. The veteran signal-caller finished with his second-lowest passing yardage total of the season, while his pass-attempt tally tied the season-low figure he'd generated back in Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia, against the Rams. However, Stafford extended his streak of games with at least one TD pass to four when he connected with Puka Nacua from 18 yards out with 3:41 remaining in the third quarter. Stafford will look to continue successfully weathering the absence of Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) during a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

items.head: Held to three catches in win over Saints
items.body: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans. The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

items.head: Salvages day with late TD
items.body: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

items.head: Career-best scrimmage yards total in win
items.body: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.

items.head: Is Chuba Hubbard the biggest X factor to spark a Panthers turnaround?
items.body: Meet Carolina's team captain, a locker room leader and a relentless running back who is "chasing greatness myself."

items.head: Comes up short of 100 scrimmage yards
items.body: Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and caught four of five targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to Denver. The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.

items.head: Stellar production in easy win
items.body: Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Hits paydirt against Washington
items.body: Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

items.head: Leads ground attack in win
items.body: Corum rushed 11 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday. Corum led the Rams in rushing yards despite logging five fewer carries than Kyren Williams, and, like the latter, Corum was able to get into the end zone. Corum's score came early in the third quarter on a winding 23-yard run, his second in as many games. The third-year back now has double-digit carries in consecutive games for the second time this season, and he's averaging a career-best 5.2 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

items.head: Not much on five touches in Week 10
items.body: Allgeier mustered five carries for 14 yards and didn't gather in his only target during Sunday's 34-6 defeat to the Rams.

items.head: Accrues 19 touches Sunday
items.body: Allgeier compiled 17 carries for 46 yards and caught two of three targets for no yards during Sunday's 17-3 defeat at Seattle. Allegeier has reeled off 10-plus touches in four straight contests, a span in which he's turned 65 touches into 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. He's been the beneficiary of repeated ankle injuries to rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, who must remain on IR for at least three more outings after Sunday's matchup, and the other current top RB on the active roster (Bam Knight) is in the concussion protocol, which will require clearance from an independent neurologist for his next game action. As a result, Allgeier is set up to retain a significant workload until Knight gets the all clear to return.

items.head: Set for lead-back duties
items.body: Allgeier is slated to work as Arizona's No. 1 running back for at least the next four weeks after Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports. Allgeier previously led the Cardinals' backfield when Love was sidelined due to a different ankle injury Weeks 6 and 7, but Allgeier is now slated for a longer period in that role. Love was hurt late in the first quarter in his return to action Sunday against Dallas, and Allgeier ran wild after his departure, finishing with a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five receptions. In addition to Love getting hurt, Bam Knight suffered a concussion and is iffy to be able to suit up this Sunday against Seattle, so the backfield could belong to Allgeier, Evan Hull and a practice-squad signee (likely Jerome Ford). Though Allgeier found substantial success in Week 8, he came into the contest averaging just 2.9 yards per carry on 61 totes. He'll also be facing a Seattle defense in Week 9 that is tied for the second-fewest yards per carry (3.8) allowed to running backs this season, so a repeat performance by Allgeier would be surprising.

items.head: Breaks out after RB injuries
items.body: Allgeier reeled off 147 yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and gathered in all five targets for 44 yards and one more TD during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win in Dallas. Fellow RBs Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) left in the second and third quarters, respectively, and were unable to return, leaving Allgeier as the only healthy and available backfield option the rest of the way. Allgeier didn't really get going until QB Gardner Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter, as the running back recorded a 63-yard touchdown run, another 52-yard carry and a five-yard TD grab on the next two drives to account for most of his output. Considering Love has been dealing with ankle issues for most of the season and already has missed two games, and Knight is subject to the protocol for head injuries, Allgeier may be in line for a boost in workload in the short term.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Allgeier (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Allgeier kicked off Week 8 prep as a non-participant due to a toe injury, but he was able to log back-to-back limited sessions to end it, which was enough to get the all-clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll be welcoming back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) to the Cardinals backfield after a two-game absence, so the breakdown of reps between those two and potentially Bam Knight remains to be seen.

items.head: Totals 66 yards, TD behind CMC
items.body: Black rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys. He added two catches for 13 yards on two targets. The rookie running back has tallied double-digit carries in three straight games and played 26 of 65 offensive snaps behind Christian McCaffrey's 39 snaps. CMC was also extremely productive out of the backfield against Dallas' Swiss-cheese defense, turning 17 touches into 243 total yards and three touchdowns. Black is more involved than most of McCaffrey's backups have been in recent seasons, and the rookie is offering some standalone RB2/3 valuation in one of the league's most efficient offenses. Over the last three games, Black has rushed 34 times for 186 yards (5.5 YPC) and two touchdowns.

items.head: Rushes for team-high 70 yards
items.body: Black rushed 11 times for 70 yards but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.

items.head: Nine touches in Week 10
items.body: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks. Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has earned 54 runs along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

items.head: Unproductive against Niners
items.body: Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he failed to produce with 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. Washington has done nothing to suggest he's warranted more carries for Las Vegas. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has shown nothing as a pass catcher. Washington is nothing more than a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.

items.head: Workload breakdown a 'week-to-week' decision
items.body: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Washington and Ashton Jeanty will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak said that he "absolutely" believes that Jeanty can be a bell cow running back, but at least for the time being, he looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington. Jeanty has seen his carry count drop or hold steady in each successive game since Week 1, culminating in the 2025 first-round pick logging just two carries in this past Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets, while Washington carried a career-high 25 times for 83 yards. The split in carries may not be quite as dramatic in weeks to come, but Washington appears to have earned himself a sizable piece of the pie while he's averaging 4.3 yards per tote to Jeanty's 3.1 mark through eight games. Jeanty remains the Raiders' clear cut top option on passing downs over Washington, who has recorded just three receptions for 11 yards on six targets so far this season.

items.head: Career-high 25 carries in Week 8 win
items.body: Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. Washington got 25 carries to Ashton Jeanty's two, though Jeanty notched 64 receiving yards on four targets while Washington wasn't involved as a pass catcher. Head coach Klint Kubiak revealed after the game that Jeanty's meager rushing workload was by design, per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, though Kubiak added that added that Jeanty is "still going to be a big part of our team" moving forward. Sunday marked the first time Washington has notched double-digit carries in a regular-season game. The rookie fourth-round pick is averaging 4.3 yards per carry compared to Jeanty's 3.1 YPC heading into a Week 9 road game against the 49ers.

items.head: Leading receiver in loss to Jags
items.body: Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

items.head: Finds end zone in Week 10 loss
items.body: Pollard carried the ball nine times for 33 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.

items.head: Cleared for Week 10 action
items.body: Pollard (finger/rest) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

items.head: Sits out Thursday's practice
items.body: Pollard (finger/rest) didn't practice Thursday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. Since rest is included among the reasons Pollard didn't practice Thursday, he's likely to resume practicing in at least some capacity Friday. After staying put at the trade deadline, Pollard is poised to retain the lead role in Tennessee's backfield for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Pollard compiled 292 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns across Tennessee's last two games prior to a Week 9 bye.

items.head: Tony Pollard (Finger) is Questionable
items.body: Pollard (finger/rest) didn't practice Thursday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

items.head: Stays put in Tennessee after deadline
items.body: The Titans opted not to move Pollard ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, despite him drawing interest from teams, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.

items.head: Titans reportedly not interested in trade
items.body: While Pollard has reportedly drawn interest from teams looking for running back help ahead of the NFL's upcoming trade deadline, Albert Breer of SI.com, Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport note via ESPN.com that the Titans are not interested in trading him. As the trade deadline looms, there's been plenty of speculation surrounding a handful of fantasy-relevant running backs, including Pollard, who may be on the move. At this stage, he's trending toward staying put, but it's still worth keeping an antenna up on his situation through Tuesday. To date, Pollard has handled the bulk of Tennessee's carries (133), with backups Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singleton having logged a combined 25 carries.

items.head: Five TDs in last two games
items.body: Pollard rushed 21 times for 117 yards and two touchdowns while catching three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. Pollard rumbled for a 40-yard touchdown in the first quarter and added a one-yard rushing TD in the third quarter, giving him five rushing scores in the last two games. He scored only once in the first six games of the season, but Pollard's recent hot streak has him up to six touchdowns, surpassing his total of five from each of his previous two regular seasons in Tennessee. Pollard was also brought down in Tennessee's end zone for a safety to break a 21-21 tie in the final minute of the third quarter. The surging running back has rushed for 246 yards over the past two games but could have a tough time maintaining his momentum after the Titans' Week 9 bye, as he'll return to action in a daunting Week 10 matchup against Jacksonville's league-best run defense.

items.head: No Spears for Week 8
items.body: Pollard will have a chance to easily pace the Titans backfield against Cincinnati on Sunday due to the absence of Tyjae Spears (knee), Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. Pollard enters the weekend on the heels of the best performance of his career with the Titans, when he turned 25 carries into 129 yards and three touchdowns and added three catches (on as many targets) for 26 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Browns. Cincinnati's defense gives up 116.3 rushing yards per game (19th in the NFL), but the unit likely will hone in more on Pollard given Spears and even rookie WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) are sidelined.

items.head: Tallies 120 all-purpose yards in loss
items.body: Washington secured all three targets for 50 yards, threw a 34-yard touchdown on his one pass attempt and returned four punts for 36 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

items.head: Two receptions in loss
items.body: Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season while his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has only reached the end zone once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

items.head: Snags short TD in loss to Pats
items.body: Washington caught five of six targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England. The five grabs led the team on the afternoon, and Washington capped his performance with a one-yard TD from Malik Willis just before halftime. It was Washington's first score of the season in seven games, and he'll take a 31-329-1 line on 45 targets into a Week 9 meeting with the Lions.

items.head: Good to go for Week 8
items.body: Washington (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. Washington practiced fully Friday after limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. The Dolphins' WR1 in terms of playing time and targets, Washington still hasn't found the end zone this season, producing 26 catches for 289 yards on 39 targets. He's a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy.

items.head: Gets 13 touches Sunday
items.body: Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.

items.head: Matches Washington with six carries
items.body: Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The Raiders largely abandoned the run after falling down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.

items.head: Workload to be decided on week-to-week basis
items.body: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Jeanty and Mike Washington will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports. Jeanty is averaging just 3.1 yards per tote on the season and has seen his carry count gradually decline with each successive game. After rushing a season-high 23 times in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins, Jeanty logged just two carries (for nine yards) in this past Sunday's win over the Jets, while Washington handled 25 carries (for 83 yards). According to McFadden, Kubiak said that he believes Jeanty can "absolutely" be a bell cow running back, but the second-year player out of Boise State looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington until his production on the ground improves. Jeanty is still locked in as the Raiders' clear top back on passing downs, as he ranks first or tied for first with all NFL running backs in targets (49), receptions (37), receiving yards (376) and receiving touchdowns (three).

items.head: Gets two carries to Washington's 25
items.body: Jeanty rushed twice for nine yards while catching three of four targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. Jeanty ceded the vast majority of rushing opportunities to Mike Washington, who rushed 25 times for 83 yards. Most of Jeanty's yardage came on a 45-yard catch on the first play of the fourth quarter. Jeanty has excelled as a pass catcher, and he now has more receiving yards (376) than rushing yards (337) this season. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, head coach Klint Kubiak said after the win that Jeanty getting just two carries was "my call" and added that Jeanty is "still going to be a big part of our team" heading into the Raiders' Week 9 road game against the 49ers.
