Jeanty added that it was "communicated" to him before the game that he would get fewer carries but stressed that winning is more important to him than his workload.

items.head: Tosses two TDs in Week 10
items.body: Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions along with six carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory in Las Vegas.

items.head: Cleared to start Sunday
items.body: Lock (right elbow/oblique) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Brady Henderson on ESPN reports.

items.head: Encouraging results regarding oblique injury
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Lock's tests on his oblique injury were "good," and the issue is something the QB is expected to manage ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders,  Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports. As a result, it seems likely that Lock's practice reps will be managed this week in order to prepare him for another starting assignment, with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold -- who was inactive in Week 9 -- not ready to return to the lineup this weekend. The Seahawks have a bye in Week 11, which may afford Darnold enough time to return to action Nov. 29 against the 49ers, but barring any setbacks it looks like Lock is bound to fill in again, backed up by Jalen Milroe.

items.head: Seahawks to start QB Drew Lock vs. Raiders, giving Sam Darnold more time to heal
items.body: The Seahawks plan to start quarterback Drew Lock on Sunday against the Raiders, giving Sam Darnold another week to recover from his injuries.

items.head: Drew Lock overcomes oblique injury in fill-in start for Sam Darnold, Seahawks
items.body: Already dealing with an injury to his throwing elbow, Drew Lock hurt his oblique in the third quarter of Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field.

items.head: Injures oblique during Week 9 win
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said after Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals that Lock sustained an oblique injury during the game, leaving Lock's availability for Week 10 against the Raiders up in the air, Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times reports. Lock finished the win over Arizona, completing 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown while adding five rushing attempts for 16 yards. His lone touchdown pass was a seven-yard connection to AJ Barner with 15 seconds left in the first half. Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sat out Sunday's win and may not be ready to return against the Raiders. If both Lock and Darnold sit out, 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe would make his first regular-season start.

items.head: Set for Week 9 start
items.body: Lock (right elbow) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Lock logged three consecutive limited sessions this week due to the right elbow injury that has contained him to inactive status and emergency third quarterback the last two games. However, with his status now cleared up for Week 9 action, he's set to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for at least one contest. In two previous appearances (one start) in place of Darnold in Weeks 1 and 2, Lock completed 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and had two carries for 13 yards. Jalen Milroe will back up Lock on Sunday.

items.head: Drew Lock (injury) is Active
items.body: Lock (right elbow) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

items.head: Posts career-best receiving line Sunday
items.body: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards. Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting any volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

items.head: First TD of career
items.body: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas. This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Gains 37 total yards in return
items.body: Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards and brought in two of four targets for eight yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Making his return from a four-game stay on injured reserve due to a chest injury, Price ended up leading the Seahawks' ground attack in carries and rushing yards. Price's return coincided with the season debut of Zach Charbonnet (knee), who logged six carries in his own right in a game whose script eventually turned unfriendly to the running game. Monday may have served as a preview of what might be expected in terms of the division of labor between the two players, but more information will be gleaned during a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday that should afford both backs more opportunities.

items.head: Activated for Monday night game
items.body: The Seahawks reinstated Price (chest) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. As Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Monday, Price will be back in action for Seattle after a minimum-length four-game stint on IR. Price, who initially sustained a chest injury in Week 2 before being deactivated after experiencing an aggravation, carried 28 times for 119 yards and added four receptions for 21 yards on seven targets through Seattle's first three games. Though he closed Week 8 prep with a pair of full practices, Price may have to settle for a more muted role as part of a backfield committee in his return to action. Zach Charbonnet (knee) has been cleared to make his 2026 debut Monday, and Emanuel Wilson could also factor into the mix after rushing for a season-high 100 yards in last week's win over the Chiefs.

items.head: No designation for Week 8
items.body: Price (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game against the Bears, but he remains on injured reserve, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. The Seahawks designated Price for return from IR on Thursday, and he proceeded to be limited that day and full Friday. Now that he's been given clearance for his first game action since Week 3 due to a chest injury, the team still needs to activate him from IR by Monday afternoon in order for him to be available in Week 8. Fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) also doesn't have a designation this week, so Seattle's backfield suddenly is crowded, with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani also in the mix.

items.head: Practices fully Friday
items.body: Price (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Since the Seahawks designated Price for return from injured reserve Thursday, he logged a limited session in his first chance to do so, followed by Friday's uncapped practice. How he's listed on Saturday's injury report will determine if he has a chance to return in Week 8 against the Bears, and if he's anything but 'Out' he'll need to be activated from IR by Monday afternoon and then be deemed active that evening. Meanwhile, fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) went from full Thursday to limited Friday, seemingly indicating he may be trending in the wrong direction to make his season sebut.

items.head: Hauls in 65-yard reception in Week 10 win
items.body: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday. Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

items.head: Racks up 20 rushes in Week 10
items.body: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.

items.head: Racks up 17 touches
items.body: Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals. The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.

items.head: Nine touches in season debut
items.body: Charbonnet (knee) rushed six times for 23 yards and brought in three of four targets for six yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Charbonnet took the first carry of the night for Seattle, gaining an encouraging five yards on his first tote since tearing his left ACL in a divisional-round win over the 49ers in January. He also subsequently rattled off a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but he was limited on his other touches and ultimately had four fewer rush attempts than Jadarian Price. Charbonnet's snap share and touches should gradually increase, and a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals could serve as a good platform for his workload to see a nice bump.

items.head: Works with starters in warmups
items.body: Charbonnet was "the first running back getting handoffs" during warmups before Monday's game against the Bears, Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports. Charbonnet is set to see his first action of the season Monday night, and with him first in line during warmups it appears he will jump right into Seattle's starting lineup. While Charbonnet will likely be the first man up in the backfield, he is coming off knee surgery and will be one of four Seahawks running backs available -- Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani being the others -- so it's unclear exactly what type of workload he will handle in his season debut.

items.head: Will play Monday
items.body: Charbonnet (knee) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Charbonnet has been officially cleared to make his 2026 regular-season debut, marking the end to his rehab from a torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained in mid-January during the Seahawks' playoff run. The Seahawks' backfield will be whole for the first time this season, seeing as both Charbonnet and Jadarian Price (chest) have been cleared to play Monday, with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani providing depth.

items.head: Practices in limited capacity
items.body: Charbonnet (knee) was a limited participant in Friday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Charbonnet opened Week 8 prep with a full practice Wednesday, which marked his fourth consecutive such listing on Seahawks injury reports. Having said that, his downgrade to limited could signify a setback of sorts as the running back seeks his first game action since Jan. 17, when he suffered a torn ACL in his left knee. Meanwhile, ellow RB Jadarian Price (chest), who was designated for return from injured reserve this week, went from limited Thursday to full Friday. In the end, Saturday's practice report will reveal both players odds to suit up Monday against the Bears.

items.head: Holds his own in first start
items.body: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.

items.head: Emerges with big line in Week 10 loss
items.body: Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble. Dallas played catchup for much of the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-most so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

items.head: Two catches in Week 9
items.body: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts. Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy has now reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Could see added looks with Pickens out
items.body: With George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, Flournoy is slated to move into the No. 2 WR role opposite CeeDee Lamb in Sunday's game against the Colts, while Jonathan Mingo will be the team's No. 3 receiver, Todd Archer of ESPN reports. With Lamb already seeing high volume on a regular basis, Flournoy -- who has been targeted four times in each of his last two games -- could see added opportunities in Week 9, along with Mingo to some degree. To date, Flournoy has compiled a 30/342/2 receiving line on 42 targets in eight games, but he could be worth a lineup look Sunday for those scrambling to find a Pickens pivot.

items.head: Catches TD in overtime loss
items.body: Flournoy caught three of four targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals. Flournoy ran 26 routes on Dak Prescott's 38 dropbacks against Arizona, and with Dallas moving more toward three-wide sets and away from multiple tight-end sets while decreasing Jake Ferguson's (ankle) playing time, Flournoy has been a big beneficiary in recent weeks. Over the last four weeks, Flournoy has recorded 238 yards and two touchdowns on 18 grabs across 21 targets. He's achieved WR4 valuation in fantasy and would receive a major boost if CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens ever went down with an injury.

items.head: Two TDs despite just five touches
items.body: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets. With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

items.head: Logs full practice Thursday
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) was a full practice participant Thursday. Kamara was listed as a non-participant Wednesday due to the combination of rest and back, but his return to all drills one day later gives him the all-clear ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Panthers. He may be welcoming back fellow RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) in Week 10 after the latter was designated for return from IR and so far has managed a pair of limited sessions, while Audric Estime is coming off a 16-touch showing this past Sunday versus the Browns.

items.head: Returns to practice
items.body: Kamara (back) returned to practice Thursday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports. The veteran returned to practice after resting a back injury in Wednesday's session. His participation level has yet to be released but Kamara is trending in the right direction heading into the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Another developing situation for the Saints is a potential return for Travis Etienne (hamstring), who practiced Thursday.

items.head: DNP on Wednesday
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Limited role in overtime win
items.body: Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards while catching three of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against the Browns. Kamara operated as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind Audric Estime (15-72-1) in Week 9. Estime was claimed off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday, and he immediately supplanted Kamara as the team's lead back. Kamara has yet to exceed 40 rushing yards in a game this season, and he has scored just one touchdown over the team's last four contests combined.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Browns. Kamara went from DNP due to rest/back Wednesday to limited Thursday and finally full Friday, paving the way for him to be available to the Saints backfield. With fellow RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) sidelined this weekend, it'll be Kamara and Kendre Miller to handle the load Sunday.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) was limited at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. Kamara followed up Wednesday's absence from practice with some activity one day later as he eases into the week due to a lingering back issue. Friday's injury report will reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game against the Browns.

items.head: Records five catches in Week 10
items.body: McBride tallied five catches on as many targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.

items.head: Notches at least seven catches again
items.body: McBride recorded seven catches (on eight targets) for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss at Seattle. With QB Jacoby Brissett getting traded to Baltimore this past week, McBride was on the receiving end of passes from Gardner Minshew, and the result was the tight end's fourth-fewest receiving yards in a game this season and also the fourth time he didn't reach the end zone through nine contests. On a positive note, McBride extended his streak with at least seven receptions to 11 outings, which matches the second-longest streak in NFL history, trailing only the 14 Antonio Brown put together from 2014-2015. McBride may have a tough task on his hands next Sunday against the Rams' surging defense.

items.head: Another productive performance
items.body: McBride hauled in seven of eight targets for 72 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory at Dallas. The Cardinals offense experienced a QB change from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew late in the third quarter, but McBride was undeterred, extending his streak of seven-plus catches to eight consecutive contests to begin the season while also scoring his fifth TD of 2026 on a 14-yard connection with Minshew with 2:11 remaining in regulation. Overall, McBride has a 66-544-5 line on 86 targets just shy of the midpoint of the campaign, putting him on pace to surpass most of his career-high marks (126-1,239-11 on 169 targets) from a season ago. It's unclear who between Brissett and Minshew will be under center next Sunday at Seattle, but McBride and WR Michael Wilson (ribs), assuming the latter suits up, will be the top options in the passing game.

items.head: Slight volume increase in Sunday's win
items.body: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not even step into one if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

items.head: Sources: Jaguars telling teams they aren't trading WR Brian Thomas Jr.
items.body: The Jaguars plan to keep wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

items.head: Staying put in Jacksonville
items.body: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Not targeted in Week 9 win
items.body: Thomas wasn't targeted in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens. Thomas played just 19 of 56 offensive snaps and ran only 11 routes on Trevor Lawrence's 26 dropbacks. It's become clear that Thomas is no longer a big part of the offense and needs an injury ahead of him or a trade out of Jacksonville to become relevant in season-long fantasy. He has just one catch for a 12-yard touchdown over his last four games.

items.head: Appealing trade target for number of teams
items.body: Thomas "has been the area of interest for a lot of other teams" leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports. Since delivering an 87-1,282-10 receiving line over 17 games as a rookie in 2024, Thomas' production has cratered in the ensuing two seasons. He's been firmly behind fellow wideouts Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) in terms of snap share through the Jaguars' first seven games of 2026 and has drawn more than three targets in just one of those contests. Though the vertical threat Thomas presents makes him an appealing target for teams seeking a big-play receiver ahead of the deadline, Rapoport acknowledges that it's unclear if the Jaguars have much motivation to move him. Despite his declining role within the Jacksonville offense, Thomas remains under contract through next season at relatively modest cap hits of $4.01 million in 2026 and $4.66 million in 2027.

items.head: Snags red-zone TD in easy win
items.body: Thomas caught one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. Thomas got the scoring started against Indianapolis, securing a red-zone touchdown with 5:30 left in the opening quarter. With the Jaguars throttling the Colts, Trevor Lawrence dropped back just 17 times all afternoon. On 17 pass attempts between Lawrence (14) and Quinn Ewers (three), 11 different Jaguars drew at least one target. Through seven games this season, Thomas has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns on 22 targets. A low catch rate and diminished snaps have led to Thomas' name being circulated in trade rumors 10 days ahead of the trade deadline.

items.head: Career-best performance in Week 10 win
items.body: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

items.head: Gets into end zone Thursday
items.body: Washington secured two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. He also returned one punt for 11 yards. Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.head: Remains quiet in Week 8 win
items.body: Washington brought in one of two targets for 16 yards and rushed once for 10 yards in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday. The Jaguars had little need to be aggressive through the air with the Colts non-competitive throughout the afternoon. Trevor Lawrence ultimately put up only 14 pass attempts and Quinn Ewers added another three in mop-up duty, leaving little for Washington and the rest of the air attack to produce with. Washington has a 27-432-4 receiving line on 48 targets through seven games heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the reeling Ravens on Thursday night.

items.head: Tosses three TDs in big win
items.body: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.

items.head: Solid numbers in comfortable win
items.body: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while rushing once for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 33-16 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.head: Highly efficient on low-volume day
items.body: Lawrence completed 10 of 14 passes for 210 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing three times for 10 yards in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday. Lawrence helped the Jaguars to a commanding 28-0 halftime lead with scoring strikes to Brian Thomas (12 yards) and Nate Boerkircher (31 yards), and he added a 25-yard TD toss to Bhayshul Tuten as time expired in the third quarter. Lawrence eventually gave way to Quinn Ewers late in the blowout win, but not before completing 71.4 percent of his passes and throwing at least three touchdown passes for the fourth time on the campaign. Lawrence now has 1,690 passing yards with a 17:4 TD:INT and has added 80 rushing yards heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Ravens on Thursday night.

items.head: Secures three catches in Week 10 win
items.body: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry. Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

items.head: Heads to medical tent during Sunday's game
items.body: Concepcion (undisclosed) headed to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Texans, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

items.head: Finds end zone for first time
items.body: Concepcion caught four of six targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added three yards on his only carry. Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie did the rest by eluding a couple defenders. It was Concepcion's first career NFL touchdown, and he sports a 37-437-1 line on 55 targets through his first nine games for the Browns. If Sanders takes over from Deshaun Watson (concussion) on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays for Concepcion.

items.head: Returns to Sunday's game
items.body: Concepcion returned to Sunday's game against the Saints after previously appearing to injure his right leg, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Cabot initially reported that Concepcion couldn't put weight on his right leg after an sustaining an apparent non-contact injury. However, following the injury scare, the rookie WR is back on the field to reclaim his key role in the Browns' passing offense.

items.head: Leaves game with leg injury
items.body: Concepcion, who was helped off the field Sunday, appeared to be having trouble putting pressure on his right leg, Ross Jackson reports. Per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer, it was a non-contact injury for Concepcion, who had caught both of his targets in the game for 11 yards. For now,  Denzel Boston, Jerry Jeudy, Tylan Wallace, Malachi Corley and Isaiah Bond are Cleveland's available WRs.

items.head: KC Concepcion (Leg) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Comes back to Earth in Week 8 loss
items.body: Concepcion caught three of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. After a breakout game last Sunday against the Titans, which saw Concepcion record eight grabs for 129 yards on 10 targets, the rookie wideout came crashing back down against a divisional foe. Concepcion's four targets were a distant fourth on the team behind Harold Fannin (12), Denzel Boston (11) and Dylan Sampson (eight), and his four looks were good for just a 10.3 percent target share. Concepcion will try to rebound next Sunday against the Saints, but he's shown little upside, with zero touchdowns and just two games with more than 50 receiving yards.

items.head: Ineffective playing through toe injury
items.body: Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans. The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it again versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game
items.body: Boston (toe) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of The Athletic reports. Boston missed practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but was able to log a limited session Friday, with coach Todd Monken being quoted as saying that the 2026 second-rounder was "trending in the right way" heading into the weekend. With his active status confirmed, in absence of any in-game limitations or setbacks, Boston is positioned to maintain his key role in a Cleveland WR corps that also features KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy. Through his first nine regular-season games as a pro, Boston leads him team with 507 receiving yards, while having hauled in 32 of his 60 targets in that span along with three TDs.

items.head: Not at practice Thursday
items.body: Boston (toe) wasn't present for Thursday's practice, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports.

items.head: Says toe feels better
items.body: Boston (toe) said Thursday that he's hoping to return to practice and "definitely feel(s) better" after sitting out Wednesday's practice, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Denzel Boston (Toe) is Questionable
items.body: Boston isn't expected to practice Wednesday due to a toe injury, Daniel Oyefusi reports.

items.head: Just misses century mark in New Orleans
items.body: Boston caught six of seven targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. The 98 yards led the Browns on the afternoon, and Boston showed some immediate chemistry with Shedeur Sanders, connecting with the QB on a 60-yard strike in the third quarter that nearly resulted in a touchdown. The rookie receiver was also the target on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game in OT, but the pass got broken up. Boston also set a new career high in receiving yards with the performance, and if Sanders takes over for Deshaun Watson (concussion) under center on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays. Through his first nine NFL games. Boston's delivered a 32-507-3 line on 61 targets.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.

items.head: Denzel Boston (injury) is Active
items.body: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.head: Short TD catch in another blowout win
items.body: Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The Jaguars just keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown in this one but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

items.head: Two grabs in another blowout win
items.body: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens. The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans in nine days.

items.head: Two snags in blowout victory
items.body: Strange caught both of his targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over Indianapolis. Strange was able to make it seven games in a row with multiple catches to open the 2026 campaign. The tight end tied running back Bhayshul Tuten for the team lead in receiving yards, exceeding 50 yards for the third time in the last four games. Strange has now reeled in 28 of 35 targets for 334 yards and a touchdown over seven contests this season.

items.head: Two grabs in Week 10 win
items.body: Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.

items.head: Paces team in receiving yards
items.body: Shakir secured all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night. Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.

items.head: Has TD called back, finishes with 5-64
items.body: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.

items.head: Logs 39 total yards in Week 10
items.body: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards. With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

items.head: Good to go for Week 10
items.body: Lloyd (knee) is not listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday. The running back appears ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Vikings after missing Week 9 against New England. With Josh Jacobs (finger) set to miss some time, Lloyd figures to be part of the backfield mix, joining Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong.

items.head: MarShawn Lloyd (Knee) is Out
items.body: Lloyd (knee) is listed as inactive Sunday at New England, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.

items.head: Dealing with knee issue
items.body: Lloyd was limited at practice Thursday due to a knee injury. Lloyd's addition to the Packers' practice report midweek is something to monitor, especially because it may indicate a health concern that occurred during Thursday's session. Ultimately, Friday's injury report may provide some clarity into the situation.

items.head: MarShawn Lloyd (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Lloyd was limited at practice Thursday due to a knee injury.

items.head: Modesat numbers in Week 10 loss
items.body: Johnson carried the ball 10 times for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. The former Steeler led the Packers' backfield in totes and rushing yards, with MarShawn Lloyd chipping in 39 scrimmage yards on seven touches. Johnson has produced modest but decent numbers over the last two games, averaging a 4.6 YPC on 24 carries as the top early-down option for Green Bay. Josh Jacobs (finger) could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but if he isn't cleared, Johnson could find himself atop the depth chart again in Week 12 against the Rams.

items.head: Could lead backfield again Week 10
items.body: Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Thrives in lead role
items.body: Johnson rushed 14 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. Josh Jacobs exited the game in the first quarter due to a hand injury, leaving Johnson in a lead role that the Steelers' 2025 third-round pick filled effectively. Johnson's carry and yardage totals were both new career highs by a fairly wide margin, and he also punched in his first career touchdown on a two-yard run with under five minutes remaining in the first half. The impressive showing combined with Jacobs' injury and that of MarShawn Lloyd (knee), who was inactive Sunday, could leave Johnson in possession of the top role again in a Week 10 home divisional showdown against the Vikings next Sunday.

items.head: Gets nine touches to Hall's 15
items.body: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.

items.head: Cedes majority of work to Hall
items.body: Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.

items.head: Sharing backfield with Hall
items.body: Jets coach Aaron Glenn declined to elaborate on the distribution of carries between Allen and Breece Hall, who will return from a five-game absence for Sunday's matchup with Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. Allen averaged 18.6 carries for 100.8 yards and 0.4 TDs over the past four games, adding 2.6 catches for 14.0 yards on 3.4 targets while playing at least 78 percent of snaps each week. He won't get that kind of workload with Hall back in the lineup, but it is possible that this turns into a hot-hand situation where Allen still has a chance to take the majority of carries if he outplays his backfield mate. Both Glenn and Hall said earlier this week that Hall is still viewed as the starter.

items.head: Career-high 147 rushing yards in Week 8
items.body: Allen rushed 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Allen made a fifth consecutive start in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps) and exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fourth consecutive game. The 2024 fourth-round pick set a new career high with 147 rushing yards, surpassing Allen's 116 yards on the ground in the Week 5 win over the Browns. Allen scored his third rushing touchdown of the season on a 21-yard run in the third quarter to give the Jets a 30-21 lead, but the Raiders closed the game on a 17-3 run to drop the Jets to 2-6. If Hall's ready to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs, the Jets could opt for a backfield split between Allen and Hall.

items.head: Headed for another start Sunday
items.body: Allen is slated to serve as the Jets' starting running back Sunday against the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. For a second week in a row, fellow running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) is listed questionable to play, but he was inactive in Week 7, and he's considered unlikely to play again in Week 8, per Rapoport. Assuming Hall is officially ruled out when the Jets release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff, Allen should be headed for another heavy workload out of the New York backfield. In the Jets' last four games sans Hall, Allen combined for 83 touches for 421 yards from scrimmage and one rushing touchdown.

items.head: Shut down by Minnesota
items.body: Kraft caught one of four targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

items.head: Single-digit yardage on three touches
items.body: Kraft brought in one of three targets for one yard and rushed twice for eight yards in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. The athletic tight end didn't get in on any of the fun on a day when Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Kraft's stat line set (receptions, receiving yards) or tied (targets) season lows, while his work on the ground included a pair of season-high figures. Nevertheless, it was an utterly forgettable showing for Kraft, who'll look to atone in a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

items.head: Zero grabs in Week 10
items.body: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

items.head: Logs full practice Wednesday
items.body: Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City.

items.head: On track to practice Wednesday
items.body: Worthy (hamstring) is slated to practice Wednesday, " Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.

items.head: Xavier Worthy (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Won't return to contest
items.body: Worthy (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against the Jets. Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com previously noted that Worthy immediately grabbed his hamstring and was unable to put weight on his leg after sustaining his injury Sunday. That Worthy was so quickly ruled out for the remainder of the contest is certainly concerning in terms of his status for next week's game against the Falcons. In his absence versus the Jets, Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong and Nikko Remigio are available to work behind top WR Rashee Rice.

items.head: Exits Sunday's game
items.body: Worthy left Sunday's game against the Jets with an apparent leg injury, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Per Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com, Worthy immediately grabbed his hamstring and was unable to put weight on his leg before heading to the blue medical tent to get checked out. Prior to his exit from the contest, Worthy caught all six of his targets for 48 yards.

items.head: Leader receiver in Week 10 loss
items.body: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

items.head: Patrick Mahomes stars for Chiefs, strikes early connection with Josh Downs
items.body: Even with an elbow injury, Patrick Mahomes was able to have his best performance of the year to lead the Chiefs to a dominant 35-13 win over the Falcons.

items.head: Five-TD day in win
items.body: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

items.head: Team sought more opinions on QB's elbow
items.body: In addition to the Chiefs team doctors reviewing Mahomes' (throwing) elbow scans, the team sought further feedback from renowned doctors from the Kansas City Royals and Texas Rangers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Sources: Chiefs had renowned baseball doctors weigh in on Patrick Mahomes' elbow
items.body: The Chiefs sought medical opinions from two renowned baseball doctors last week on Patrick Mahomes' injured elbow, sources told ESPN.

items.head: No injury designation
items.body: Mahomes (elbow) was a full practice participant throughout the week and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Atlanta.

items.head: In line to work through elbow issue Sunday
items.body: Mahomes (elbow/knee) has had "limited swelling" and "limited pain" in his right (throwing) elbow in recent days, and is in line to start Sunday's game against the Falcons, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.

items.head: Patrick Mahomes (injury) is Questionable
items.body: Mahomes (right elbow/knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Held in check by Vikes
items.body: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.

items.head: Does Packers' Christian Watson + Matthew Golden = 3,000 yards?
items.body: Watson and Golden are on pace to join a rare club of WR pairs who combined for 3,000 yards.

items.head: Career-high yardage total in win
items.body: Watson secured seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. Watson repeatedly got the best of Christian Gonzalez and the rest of a talented Patriots secondary, recording team- and career-high receiving yardage totals along the way. Watson burned New England for four catches of 20-plus yards, including a game-long 49-yard grab, as well as a 39-yard touchdown catch in the latter portion of the third quarter. Watson's career-best line is up to a tally of 49-879-7 on 74 targets heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the Vikings next Sunday.

items.head: Will be 'full go' Sunday
items.body: Watson (ribs) will be "full go" in Sunday's game at New England, per Jay Glazer on Fox NFL Sunday. Watson suffered a broken rib during a Week 8 win against the Panthers in which he visited a Green Bay-area hospital during the game before returning to action in the second half. He finished that contest with his third 100-yard performance of the season -- 8-113-0 line on 10 targets -- but he was limited during Week 9 prep before avoiding a designation for this Sunday's matchup. Glazer's report indicates Watson should be good for his typical 80-plus percent snap share and 8.3 targets per game on the campaign.

items.head: No designation for Week 9
items.body: Watson (ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at New England. Despite being limited on all three of the Packers' Week 9 injury reports due to the broken rib he sustained during last Thursday's win against the Panthers, Watson will be available to Green Bay's offense. It stands to reason he'll wear some sort of protection around his midsection Sunday, but he nonetheless is a plug-and-play option due to his 42-708-6 line on 66 targets through the first eight games of the campaign.

items.head: Christian Watson (injury) is Active
items.body: Watson (ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: Watson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports. Watson now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt to begin Week 9 prep, which stems from the broken rib that he suffered during last Thursday's win against the Panthers. He'll have one more chance Friday to get back to full participation, at which point the Packers may tag him with a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.

items.head: Christian Watson (Ribs) is Questionable
items.body: Watson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Scores 45-yard TD in Week 10 win
items.body: Moore caught four of six targets for 90 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for four yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

items.head: Three catches in tough matchup
items.body: Moore secured three of five targets for 25 yards and rushed once for 11 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night. The veteran receiver came into the game without an injury designation related to the shoulder injury he's managing, but Moore still put together a modest performance against a tough Vikings defense that kept pressure on Josh Allen throughout the night. Moore has a combined 7-107-1 line on on 12 targets in the two contests he's suited up for since returning from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and he should have a much better chance of downfield success in a Week 10 road matchup against the Jets' vulnerable defense on Sunday.

items.head: In clear for Week 9
items.body: Moore (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest at Minnesota. While logging three straight limited practices during Week 9 prep, Moore continued to wear a red non-contact jersey due to the AC joint sprain that he's been dealing with since Week 2. Now that he's in the clear for Monday's matchup, he'll look to build upon the 16-260-2 line on 27 targets that he's racked up through five eppearances on the campaign.

items.head: DJ Moore (injury) is Active
items.body: Moore (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest at Minnesota.

items.head: Still in non-contact jersey
items.body: Moore (shoulder) remained in a red non-contact jersey at Saturday's practice, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports. Moore has been wearing such a jersey from time to time this season since suffering an AC joint sprain in Week 2 against the Lions. He's appeared in three of the Bills' five contests since then, accruing an 11-160-1 line on 19 targets. Saturday's practice report will determine if Moore has a designation for Monday's game at Minnesota.

items.head: Remains limited at practice
items.body: Moore (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Friday. Moore has managed an AC joint sprain for most of the season, typically practicing in a non-contact jersey. He'll likely be ready for Monday's game at Minnesota, coming off a 4-82-1 receiving line (seven targets) in last week's 36-10 win over Baltimore.

items.head: Wears non-contact jersey Friday
items.body: Moore (shoulder) was still wearing a non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports. Moore will likely be managing his shoulder injury for much of the remainder of the season, as he's dealing with an AC sprain that can pop out of place with contact. Moore should be fine for Monday night's game against the Vikings after returning to the lineup last Sunday against Baltimore.

items.head: Limited participant Thursday
items.body: Moore (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Moore mustered some level of activity in Buffalo's first practice of Week 9 after downplaying the knee injury that forced him out late in the Week 8 win over Baltimore. He has an extra day to recover before the Bills face the Vikings on Monday Night Football. Moore has two more chances to practice without limitations and put himself in the clear to suit up.

items.head: Hits paydirt in Green Bay
items.body: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

items.head: Quiet night in Week 9 win
items.body: Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries in an abysmal night for the Vikings' offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six toes. Jones has now seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates on Sunday.

items.head: Seven touches in Week 8 loss
items.body: Jones rushed five times for 22 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Jones shook off the knee injury that had knocked him out of a Week 7 win over the Colts to head into Sunday without a designation. However, the veteran finished with a season low in carries and rushing yards. Jones has just 13 combined rush attempts -- a number partly influenced by the aforementioned early exit against Indianapolis -- in the two games since Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve, and it remains to be seen if the modest role will persist in a Week 9 home matchup against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Jones (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Lions, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports. After sitting out Wednesday and then returning as a limited participant Thursday, Jones is good to go for Sunday's NFC North battle. Jones should handle his normal role splitting carries with Jordan Mason, while the former handles most of the passing-down work. Jones' touchdown upside going forward took a hit with Mason's return from a thumb injury last week.

items.head: Leading rusher in Week 10 win
items.body: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

items.head: Garners 42 scrimmage yards in loss
items.body: Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' opportunities were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's 5.8 yards per carry was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

items.head: Does little with eight carries
items.body: Mason rushed eight times for 20 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Playing in his second game since returning from an IR stint due to a thumb injury, Mason paced the Vikings' ground attack in carries but finished two yards behind Aaron Jones, who logged five totes. Mason also wasn't targeted for the second time in three games, and Minnesota's running game figures to continue in a fantasy-averse timeshare between the two. Mason will look to make inroads against what has been an improved Bills run defense in a Week 9 home showdown on Monday night, Nov. 9.

items.head: Sharing backfield with Jones vs. Detroit
items.body: Mason and Aaron Jones (knee) will share the backfield against the Lions on Sunday after the latter avoided an injury designation for Week 8, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports. Jones injured his knee against the Colts in Week 7, so Mason ended up leading the Vikings backfield in touches and finished with 15 carries for 68 yards while failing to haul in either of his two targets from Kyler Murray. Jones has been cleared to play in Sunday's NFC North tilt after logging a full practice Friday, so he and Mason figure to split duties for that contest while rookie sixth-rounder Demond Claiborne operates in a depth role.

items.head: Will Howard (injury) is Active
items.body: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.

items.head: Will Howard (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Nine catches in reunion with Cousins
items.body: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

items.head: Gets QB upgrade at deadline
items.body: Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Jefferson had averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 and 8.5 touchdowns per season. Though Cousins is three years older from when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and underwhelming receiver group.

items.head: Highly inefficient sans Murray
items.body: Jefferson brought in three of 11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.

items.head: Inside Justin Jefferson's miraculous catch for Vikings versus Bills in 2022
items.body: In 2022 against the Bills, Jefferson leaped up and came down with one of "the greatest catches of all time."

items.head: Justin Jefferson (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Picturesque TD catch in loss
items.body: Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Jefferson led the Vikings in receptions with the aid of a team-high target total, and the highlight of the perennial Pro Bowler's afternoon was his touchdown grab. Jefferson stuck his hand up and tapped Kyler Murray's (hamstring) pass to himself while in tight coverage in the left corner of the end zone early in the second quarter, ultimately securing a memorable one-yard score. Jefferson has topped 50 receiving yards just three times and is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, but he's found the end zone in two of the last three games heading into a Week 9 home showdown against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.

items.head: Helps lead big comeback
items.body: Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland. Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29 following a Week 11 bye.

items.head: Browns' Deshaun Watson savors 'special' win vs. Texans
items.body: Deshaun Watson, who delivered his sixth game-winning drive of the season, called the 27-24 victory over the Texans, his former team, "definitely special."

items.head: Browns' Monken: Watson over Sanders QB decision based on 'full body of work'
items.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said Wednesday his intention all along was to stick with Deshaun Watson as QB1 based on his "full body of work" this season.

items.head: Officially named Week 10 starter
items.body: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Remains in line to start Sunday
items.body: Watson (concussion) will serve as the Browns' starting quarterback in Sunday's game against the Texans, a source tells Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.

items.head: Source: Browns returning to Watson as QB1 despite Sanders' strong fill-in start
items.body: The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 against the Texans, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.

items.head: Steps in after Geno's injury
items.body: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.

items.head: Paces pass catchers in win
items.body: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 91 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

items.head: Ready to play Sunday
items.body: Fannin (groin) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.head: Limited on Wednesday
items.body: Fannin (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.

items.head: Renews chemistry with Sanders in OT loss
items.body: Fannin caught both his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. With Shedeur Sanders under center for the first time in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Fannin did little in regulation as the second-year QB instead looked for rookie wideouts Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Sanders went back to a more familiar target in OT, however, connecting with Fannin on a 39-yard TD in the extra frame that saw the tight end flatten a couple defenders with stiff arms on his way to the end zone. Fannin had a slow start to the season, but over the last three weeks he's amassed an 18-287-1 line on 23 targets, giving him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 10 clash with the Texans no matter who is throwing him passes.

items.head: Will play Sunday
items.body: Fannin (groin) will play Sunday against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. Coach Todd Monken said Fannin is "a little sore" but will be out there against New Orleans. On paper, it's a great spot for Fannin, but playing at less than 100 percent knocks him down a peg as a backend TE1 for fantasy.

items.head: Practicing Friday
items.body: Fannin (groin) is practicing Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. After being listed as a limited participant Thursday, Fannin appears to be back on the field ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints. His Friday activity is a positive sign for his availability, but it doesn't confirm whether he'll carry an injury designation into the weekend.

items.head: Added to Week 9 injury report
items.body: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Fannin wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so his appearance on it a day later is notable. It remains to be seen if Thursday's listed limitations were maintenance related or indicative of a setback, but the tight end may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Saints without an injury designation.

items.head: Gets into end zone Sunday
items.body: Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 33 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

items.head: Lower snap count downplayed by coach
items.body: Running backs coach Duce Staley said Saturday that Judkins' lower snap count against the Saints in Week 9 was "situational football," Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Judkins was on the field for a season-low 25 offensive snaps in Week 9, which was considerably lower than Dylan Sampson's 47, although the former led Cleveland's backfield with 15 carries, which he turned into 43 yards (4.3 YPC). Judkins has averaged 2.6 yards per carry over his last two outings, and he faces a Texans defense Sunday that ranks 12th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (103.0).

items.head: Little running room in Week 9 loss
items.body: Judkins carried the ball 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. The Browns' running game once again struggled, with the team averaging just 2.8 yards per carry overall, and Judkins' longest gain went for only 12 yards. Dylan Sampson saw a season-high 11 touches to Judkins' 16, and the backfield could be drifting toward a timeshare as coach Todd Monken looks for solutions. Judkins has topped 70 rushing yards in a game just once all season, and he seems unlikely to break out in a Week 10 meeting with the Texans.

items.head: Stymied by Steelers in loss
items.body: Judkins rushed 11 times for 25 yards and brought in both targets for 24 yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. Judkins dominated the Browns' rushing touches, but he was repeatedly stonewalled by an aggressive Steelers front. Judkins ultimately finished with his second-lowest rushing yardage total of the season, although he did make good use of his two pass-catching opportunities. Judkins is finding running room sparse on most weeks behind Cleveland's spotty blocking, but he remains in clear possession of the lead role heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Saints next Sunday.

items.head: Solid numbers in lopsided loss
items.body: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.

items.head: Held in check through air by Bengals
items.body: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries. It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.head: Nightmare afternoon in rainy conditions
items.body: Penix completed eight of 24 passes for 125 yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions while rushing five times for 11 yards in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered. Penix endured a career-worst all-around game in rainy conditions after coming into the afternoon with just one interception in his first five games. Only two of Penix's four picks led to Buccaneers points -- and just a pair of field goals at that -- but the Falcons defense was helpless against Tampa Bay's ground attack in the shutout. Sunday's conditions were a clear outlier, so Penix should be expected to bounce back across the pond in a Week 9 matchup against a vulnerable Bengals secondary next Sunday in Madrid.

items.head: Bijan Robinson: Falcons deserved boos in loss to Chiefs
items.body: Fans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium booed the Falcons after another poor offensive showing Sunday.

items.head: Solid numbers in blowout loss
items.body: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson now also has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Sources: Giants called Falcons to ask about Bijan Robinson before trade deadline
items.body: The Giants made a call to the Falcons before the NFL trade deadline inquiring about star running back Bijan Robinson, multiple sources told ESPN.

items.head: Big workload in loss to Cincy
items.body: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he's gotten into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.head: Manages solid rushing total in shutout
items.body: Robinson rushed 19 times for 76 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. It was a bizarre afternoon overall in very rainy conditions in Tampa Bay, and Robinson managed to salvage his day with a solid rushing yardage total. Robinson's tally on the ground was actually his best since Week 5, although his streak of games without a rushing touchdown extended to four. Robinson is still averaging 5.2 yards per carry on the season and now is up to 983 yards from scrimmage and five total touchdowns heading into next Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Bengals in Madrid.

items.head: Four catches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

items.head: Three grabs in Sunday's loss
items.body: Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.

items.head: Locked down in Week 8
items.body: Pitts caught two of five targets for six yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers. Pitts was unable to make it four straight weeks with a touchdown, and he was held to two or fewer catches for the first time since Week 3 versus Green Bay. The tight end has exceeded 50 receiving yards just one time over eight contests to open the 2026 campaign, so fantasy managers are pretty reliant on him reaching the end zone. Pitts and the rest of the Falcons' offense will have a good chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Bengals' inconsistent defense.

items.head: George Holani (Knee) is Out
items.body: Holani (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

items.head: Exits with knee injury
items.body: Holani (knee) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders. Holani exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with a knee injury. The running back sustained the injury on kick coverage. Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet are still set to receive all the rushing volume for the Seahawks in Sunday's game.

items.head: George Holani (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Gets no touches Week 9
items.body: Holani didn't log any touches or targets Sunday in a 17-3 win over Arizona. Holani logged just one offensive snap, by far his lowest count of the season. He's trending toward playing primarily on special teams now that Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back in the fold at running back for Seattle. Emanuel Wilson is also on the roster, but he didn't see any action at all Week 10.

items.head: Productive in team debut
items.body: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

items.head: Set to make debut with Chiefs
items.body: Downs is active and slated to make his debut with the Chiefs on Sunday versus the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Likely playing Sunday
items.body: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Friday that Downs looks ready to play in Sunday's game at Atlanta, Charles Goldman of AtoZ Sports reports.
