items.head: Productive with 24 touches
items.body: Gordon rushed 20 times for 76 and brought in four of five targets for 39 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

items.head: Logs 17 touches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage totals decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

items.head: Leading rusher in Week 8 loss
items.body: Gordon carried the ball 19 times for 69 yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. He failed to catch his only target. For the first time since De'Von Achane (knee) went down in Week 3 and Gordon became Miami's lead back, the second-year player was held out of the end zone. Over the last four games, Gordon has amassed 360 rushing yards and three TDs on 71 totes (5.1 yards per carry), but he's added exactly zero receiving yards to his totals. Gordon will try to begin a new TD streak in Week 9 against the Lions.

items.head: Productive with five catches in win
items.body: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

items.head: Five catches in Week 9 win
items.body: Rice secured five of seven targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.

items.head: Full participant Thursday
items.body: Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced without limitations Thursday. Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.

items.head: Limited Wednesday
items.body: Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice. Rice got back in the fold in Week 8 to the tune of an 7-53-1 line after missing time with a hamstring injury, and he is limited to start preparation for the Jets. The Chiefs could be exercising caution with their top receiver, who also rehabbed from knee surgery during the offseason. A limited session Wednesday does not mean his Week 9 status is in jeopardy, but his participation over the coming days will be telling.

items.head: Finds end zone in Week 8 return
items.body: Rice caught seven of eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. Making his return from a two-game absence due to a hamstring strain, Rice made an immediate impact when he caught an 11-yard TD from Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter for Kansas City's first points of the afternoon. The fourth-year wideout nearly had the game-winning touchdown in the final seconds of the fourth as well, but the play was wiped out by a false-start penalty. In five appearances that season, one of which lasted just six snaps, Rice has put together a 20-243-2 line on 25 targets. He'll look to build on Sunday's performance in a Week 9 clash with the Jets.

items.head: Will play this Sunday
items.body: Rice (hamstring) will play in Sunday's game against the Broncos, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official website reports. After returning to limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Rice is set for his first game appearance since Week 4. He starts off with a tough matchup at Denver against Pat Surtain & Co.

items.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown talks lederhosen, Lions' 'Human Centipede' celebration
items.body: Inspired by his mother, St. Brown paired a memorable performance with a coordinated Bavarian look alongside his Lions teammates.

items.head: Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown: Germany trip one he'll 'never forget'
items.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown, who spent childhood summers visiting Germany, said Sunday after the Lions' win in Munich that this is a trip he'll "never forget."

items.head: Two trips to end zone in Week 10 win
items.body: St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.

items.head: Active in Week 10
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) is listed as active Sunday against the Patriots in Munich.

items.head: Expected to suit up Sunday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Listed as questionable for Sunday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) was a limited participant in Friday's practice and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday.

items.head: Eight catches in Week 9 win
items.body: St. Brown brought in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. St. Brown set the pace across the board for the Lions in receptions, receiving yards and targets. St. Brown was playing through a rib issue that had limited him throughout the practice week, but he turned in an efficient effort that included his fifth straight game with six ore more catches. St. Brown's touchdown drought did extend to five games, and he'll once again aim to snap it in next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany.

items.head: Season-high 14 targets in return
items.body: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is listed as active Sunday against the Bills. Wilson emerged from a Week 8 loss to the Raiders with a concussion and required nearly two weeks to make his way through the protocol for head injuries, seemingly getting the all-clear from an independent neurologist either Friday evening or Saturday. In any case, all three of the Jets' top three injured wide receivers -- also, Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) -- are available Sunday, but Wilson should retain his standing as the clear No. 1 among the group, which has translated to a 43-527-3 line on 63 targets in eight games.

items.head: Garrett Wilson (injury) is Active
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is listed as active Sunday against the Bills.

items.head: Slated to return Sunday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is expected to be cleared to play against the Bills on Sunday, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.

items.head: Nearing clearance for Sunday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) has one more step to complete in concussion protocol, and Jets coach Aaron Glenn believes that will happen before Sunday's game against the Bills, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.

items.head: Limited again Thursday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) was present at Thursday's practice, Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports.

items.head: Returning to limited parctice
items.body: Wilson (concussion) will be a a limited participant in Wednesday's practice,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athleticreports. That's a step in the right direction for Wilson, who didn't practice last week before being ruled out for Week 9 action. Given that the wideout is still limited at this stage, Wilson has some hurdles to clear before he's cleared from the NFL's concussion protocol, however, if he's able return to action this weekend versus the Bills, he'll reclaim his lead role in a WR corps that was paced by Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell in his absence from this past Sunday's loss to the Chiefs.

items.head: Three total TDs in Week 10 win
items.body: Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

items.head: Survives Vikes D in win
items.body: Allen completed 21 of 31 passes for 234 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding six carries for 15 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night. Allen came into the night undoubtedly expecting to have to work for everything he got, and Brian Flores' aggressive defensive unit helped validate that prognosis by sacking the star signal-caller on four occasions. However, Allen was able to navigate the dangers pretty effectively, spreading the ball around to eight different targets overall. He connected with Keleki Latu from 25 yards out late in the first half for his one touchdown pass, and Allen's one turnover, a first-quarter interception at the Vikings' seven-yard line, didn't lead to any Minnesota points. Allen hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 1, but he'll take 2,027 passing yarsd and a 12:6 TD:INT alongside 285 rushing yards into a Week 10 road divisional clash against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Three total TDs in Week 8 win
items.body: Allen completed 21 of 34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He added 30 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on seven rushing attempts. Allen capped the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown plunge on which he went airborne to stretch the ball over the goal line. He struggled as a passer in the first half, including a first-quarter interception, but Allen heated up after halftime to post his highest passing yards total since a 334-yard Week 1 performance. Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore (knee) in the fourth quarter gave Allen sole possession of first place in Bills history with 259 passing touchdowns, including postseason play. He added a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid on the next drive as the Bills pulled away from a Ravens team that lost top two QBs Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Allen has led the Bills to a 6-1 record heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the 6-1 Vikings.

items.head: Breaks off 74-yard rushing TD
items.body: Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown but didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Buffalo relied primarily on its ground game in the lopsided victory, as Cook's 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter provided the cherry on top after a pair of one-yard Josh Allen rushing scores helped the Bills pull away. Cook extended his touchdown streak to eight games by scoring his ninth rushing TD over that span. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game during this productive stretch, bouncing back effectively after being held to 69 scoreless yards by the Texans in the season opener. Cook has a nice opportunity to keep rolling in Week 11, when the 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins.

items.head: Thrives again in workhorse role
items.body: Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night. Cook was repeatedly stonewalled through three quarters by a Vikings run defense that had been fairly beatable, but the star running back continued to get opportunities to test Minnesota's defensive front. That approach finally began paying off on an early fourth-quarter marathon scoring drive, one where Cook recorded runs of nine, six and 11 yards before capping off the march with a five-yard scoring rush to extend Buffalo's 13-6 lead. Cook ultimately fell just a carry short of tying his career high, and he eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the fourth time this season. The fifth-year pro's trip to the end zone extended his touchdown streak to seven games as well, and Cook will head into a favorable Week 10 road matchup just 186 rushing yards short of his fourth straight 1,000-yard campaign.

items.head: Stretches TD streak to six games
items.body: Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.

items.head: Cleared to return Sunday
items.body: After being evaluated for a head injury, Cook was cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Ravens. Cook had headed to the medical tent to get checked out, but the Bills' top back has returned to the contest. Prior to his exit, Cook had logged 20 carries for 76 yards and a TD.

items.head: Heads to medical tent Sunday
items.body: Cook (undisclosed) headed to the blue medical tent during Sunday's game against the Ravens after absorbing a hard hit, Matt Parrino reports. Prior to that, Cook -- who was able to walk off the field his own -- carried 20 times for 76 yards and a TD. While he's out of the game, Ray Davis and Ty Johnson are next up for Buffalo's backfield touches.

items.head: Quiet trip to Munich
items.body: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.

items.head: Not viewed as trade candidate
items.body: The Lions have received trade calls on LaPorta leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the team prefers to keep him with the hope of signing the tight end to a long-term deal, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Earlier in the season, LaPorta expressed his frustration with the Lions for the organization's inability to come to terms on an extension with him, but both sides still appear to be on good terms and willing to re-engage in discussions on a new deal before he becomes a free agent in 2027. The fourth-year tight end has likely helped his case for earning a lucrative contract by having thus far stayed healthy throughout the season while putting together a 35-399-3 receiving line on 49 targets over the Lions' first eight games.

items.head: Quiet on four catches Sunday
items.body: LaPorta brought in four of five targets for 32 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. LaPorta finished a distant second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on a quiet day for the Lions' passing attack. The fourth-year tight end had back-to-back 80-plus-yard efforts in Weeks 4 and 5, but he's totaled a modest 83 total receiving yards over the subsequent three contests. LaPorta will look to boost his production back up in the Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Quiet in Week 8 win
items.body: LaPorta caught three of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 19-15 win over the Vikings. He added two rushing yards on one attempt. After being limited to 1-18-0 on two targets in last Sunday's victory over the Packers, LaPorta remained quiet in a second straight divisional matchup with a formidable defense. A Week 9 date with the Dolphins will present a get-right spot for the tight end, who has 31 grabs for 367 yards and three touchdowns through seven games this season. LaPorta will be a locked-in TE1 play against Miami.

items.head: Emanuel Wilson (injury) is Active
items.body: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona.

items.head: Emanuel Wilson (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Doesn't get into Week 9 win
items.body: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals. Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

items.head: Relegated to special teams Monday
items.body: Wilson played just seven snaps -- all on special teams -- in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears. After logging double-digit carries in six of the Seahawks' previous seven games while scoring four touchdowns and averaging 66.4 scrimmage yards during that span, Wilson fell out of the game plan entirely in Week 8. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting cleared to make his 2026 debut, Jadarian Price (chest) returning from injured reserve and George Holani still on hand as an option on passing downs, the Seahawks had no reps available out of the backfield for Wilson. Unless Charbonnet or Price succumbs to another injury, Wilson's playing time on offense will likely remain scarce moving forward.

items.head: More competition for work
items.body: Wilson is welcoming back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) to the Seahawks backfield for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Seattle cleared Charbonnet to make his season debut on its final Week 8 injury report before the team activated Price from injured reserve Monday, which means the latter is available for his first game action since Week 3. Wilson operated as the Seahawks' lead runner the last four contests, racking up 85 touches for 359 yards from scrimmage and four total TDs. He'll certainly cede some of those reps to the combination of Charbonnet and Price, but the possibility exists that he ends up taking on the most work among the trio if the team eases one or both back in.

items.head: Joey Aguilar (injury) is Active
items.body: Aguilar (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Rams on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Joey Aguilar (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Catches on with Arizona
items.body: The Cardinals signed Aguilar off the Jaguars' practice squad Tuesday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Arizona has yet to announce a corresponding move, but top quarterback Gardner Minshew could be headed to injured reserve after sustaining a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks that may require season-ending surgery. An undrafted rookie out of Tennessee, Aguilar joins fellow rookie Carson Beck and veteran journeyman Josh Johnson as the healthy options in the Cardinals' quarterback room. Aguilar will likely settle in as the No. 3 option on the depth chart if Minshew is indeed placed on IR.

items.head: Four grabs in win over Pats
items.body: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.

items.head: Two touches in Week 9 win
items.body: Williams brought in one of two targets for 31 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Game-winning TD in divisional clash
items.body: Williams brought in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 19-15 win over the Vikings on Sunday. Williams ended up leading the Lions in receiving yards on the day while checking in second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receptions and targets. The fourth-year speedster also delivered the biggest catch of the day, recording a seven-yard touchdown grab with 4:35 remaining that proved to be the game-winning score. Williams has recorded all five of his touchdown receptions on the season within the last three games, and he has at least Sunday's yardage tally in three of the last four heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Dolphins.

items.body: Thornton (back) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

items.head: Only one catch in Week 10 defeat
items.body: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. The Patriots' offense looked good on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots'

items.head: Exceeds century mark in loss
items.body: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Hauls in long TD in win
items.body: Douglas caught all three of his targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins. Most of his production came on a nifty 48-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter, as Douglas took a strike from Drake Maye along the sideline but then curled back toward the middle of the field and dashed the remaining 30 yards to the end zone while out-racing four Miami defenders. It was the fourth touchdown of the season for the fourth-year wideout, a new career high, and Douglas will take a 26-332-4 line on 37 targets through eight games into a Week 9 tilt against the Packers.

items.head: Massive numbers in Week 10 romp
items.body: Gibbs carried the ball 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 99 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.

items.head: Rush TD in Week 9 win
items.body: Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. It was a relatively quiet day by Gibbs' lofty standards against a Dolphins team that's proven to have plenty of fight despite its losing record. The standout back salvaged his fantasy day with an eight-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, Gibbs' second score on the ground in as many games and ninth overall. Gibbs failed to record at least one reception for the first time this season, but he's already amassed 1,132 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns across eight games heading into next Sunday's showdown against the Patriots in Germany.

items.head: Elite production against top defense
items.body: Gibbs rushed 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown while bringing in two of four targets for 15 yards in the Lions' 19-15 win over the Vikings on Sunday. Gibbs and the Lions started relatively slowly against the Vikings' aggressive defense, netting just six first-half points. However, Gibbs continued to plug away against Minnesota's talented front, and he eventually began breaking through for multiple productive runs. Gibbs warmed up for a big second half with a 19-yard scamper just before halftime, and he went on to add a game-long 30-yard run for his one touchdown in the latter portion of the third quarter. Gibbs then helped seal the victory with gains of 17, nine and nine yards on Detroit's next-to-last drive, as well as his final 28 rushing yards of the day on the final possession. The star back ultimately finished with his second-highest rushing yardage total of the season and third of greater than 150 yards, affording him massive momentum heading into a favorable Week 9 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

items.head: Limited to two catches in Munich
items.body: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

items.head: Cleared to play Sunday
items.body: Henry (foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Lions after logging another limited practice Friday. Though Henry was limited at practice all three days leading up to the contest, the Patriots were likely managing his reps in anticipation of having the tight end available this weekend. While it's possible that the team will get top WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) back versus Detroit, RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is still out and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is banged up, so Henry figures to be a key available option for QB Drake Maye to work with, provided he avoids any setbacks with his foot.

items.head: Limited again
items.body: Henry (foot) was a limited practice participant Thursday. Henry played through the injury in last week's loss to Green Bay and has now managed back-to-back limited practices to open Week 10. items.head: Quiet day in Week 9 win
items.body: Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while also rushing four times for five yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Goff was the latest quarterback to scuffle some against a Dolphins defense that's fought hard all season, as the veteran signal-caller took three sacks and finished with a new season low in passing yards. Goff also failed to throw a touchdown for the first time this season, and he threw a pick for the second time in as many games after going without an interception for the first six contests of the campaign. Goff has completed at least 68.0 percent of his passes in three straight games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Clutch TD toss in win
items.body: Goff completed 18 of 25 passes for 176 yards with a touchdown and an interception and added three carries for no gain in the Lions' 19-15 win over the Vikings on Sunday. Goff unsurprisingly saw his production limited by the Vikings' aggressive defense, and he took four sacks overall while also tossing his first interception of the season. The veteran signal-caller also saw a 24-yard first-quarter scoring strike to Amon-Ra St. Brown overturned on replay, but Goff's beautifully thrown seven-yard TD pass to Jameson Williams in the left corner of the end zone with 4:35 remaining turned out to be the difference in the game. Goff will take 1,964 passing yards and a 15:1 TD:INT into a Week 9 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

items.head: Leading receiver in ugly loss
items.body: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

items.head: Returns to lineup Sunday

Hollins, who had landed on IR prior to Week 5 action, was activated from IR/designated to return Saturday, but still carried a 'questionable' designation ahead of the contest. In his first game action since Week 4, Hollins could make an immediate contribution to a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, but remains without A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Prior to his injury, Hollins recorded a 15/209/0 receiving line on 20 targets through four games.

items.head: Comes off IR
items.body: The Patriots activated Hollins (calf) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers. Hollins exited a Week 4 win at Buffalo in the third quarter due to a calf injury and eventually landed on IR prior to Week 5 action. He thus has missed the requisite four games while on the list, but his status now bears watching ahead of Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. With fellow WR A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined, an active Hollins could step into a prominent role in the Patriots passing game alongside position mate DeMario Douglas.

Brown (knee) out again, but Hollins never made it back to full practice participation, instead logging limited sessions Wednesday through Friday.

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Hollins (calf) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice after being designated for return from injured reserve. Hollins will be eligible for activation from IR at any point, but unless he upgrades to full participation by the end of the week, he could have a tough time gaining clearance for Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Through New England's first four games before he sustained a calf injury, Hollins produced a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets.

items.head: Could return from IR this week
items.body: Hollins (calf), who is eligible to be activated from IR this week, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald, could return to practice Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Hollins last saw game action in Week 4, but it's possible that his absence could be capped at the minimum mandated four contests. Prior to sustaining his calf injury, Hollins had recorded a 15-209-0 line on 20 targets, and if he's able to return to action Sunday against the Packers, a key role in the offense could await, with A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) Week 9 status cloudy.

items.head: Modest numbers in loss to Lions
items.body: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit. Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

items.head: First career TD in loss
items.body: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that when paired with the blowout nature of the contest afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished with as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

items.head: Struggles in Week 10 loss
items.body: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots won't put a timeline on Henderson's return, while adding via Lazar that the team is "just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and his recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." In the absence of Henderson's -- who recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" -- Rhamondre Stevenson will pace New England's backfield, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison also mixing in.

items.head: Provides medical update Friday
items.body: In a statement posted to social media Friday, Henderson -- who hasn't practiced since last Wednesday -- noted that he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms," Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. Henderson was unavailable for New England's Week 8 win over Miami due to an undisclosed illness, and he's now indicated that tests have "come back positive and reassuring," adding "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions." The running back noted that for now he is "committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health" and that his "health and long-term well-being" are his foremost priorities. In six games this season while working in a Patriots backfield that also includes Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, Henderson has carried 52 times for 203 yards a touchdown, while adding five receptions for 45 yards.

items.head: Brought up from practice squad
items.body: The Cowboys elevated Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports. With Tyler Goodson (knee) on injured reserve and Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the rest of the year, Abanikanda is expected to operate as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for the foreseeable future, starting with Sunday's game against the 49ers. Abanikanda last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he logged 22 carries for 70 yards (3.2 YPC) and added seven catches on 11 targets for 43 yards across six regular-season games with the Jets.

items.head: Prepping for RB2 job
items.body: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that Abanikanda likely will be promoted from the practice squad to replace Tyler Goodson (knee) as the No. 2 running back ahead of Sunday's matchup with San Francisco, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports. A 2024 fifth-round pick, Abanikanda has six regular-season appearances and 29 career touches -- all back in 2023 for the Jets. He offers sub-4.5 speed at 215-plus pounds, but he won't necessarily have the same role as Goodson, who earned the team's trust with solid performances after latching on earlier this fall. With Abanikanda as the No. 2 back, Javonte Williams may be tasked with even larger workloads than before.

items.head: Placed on IR
items.body: The Cowboys placed Goodson (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports. The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.

items.head: Dealing with ACL, MCL sprains
items.body: Goodson sustained ACL and MCL sprains in his knee during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, a source tells Todd Archer of ESPN.com. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

items.head: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
items.body: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.head: Set for multi-week absence
items.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" after spraining his knee in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Goodson likely will undergo further testing as the Cowboys look to hone in on a more definitive timeline for his return, but Schottenheimer's comments suggest that the reserve running back can safely be ruled out for at least Week 10 against the 49ers and Week 11 versus the Titans. Despite succumbing to the knee injury, the 25-year-old delivered his best performance of the season Sunday, finishing the day with 77 yards on 12 carries. The Cowboys currently have no other healthy running backs on the roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but one or both of practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin will be candidates for elevation to the 53-man roster while Goodson is sidelined.

items.head: Likely out for Week 10
items.body: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said Monday that Goodson is expected to miss time after injuring his knee in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports. Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys' clear No. 2 back in recent games and turned in his best performance of the season against his former Colts squad in Week 9, carrying 12 times for 77 yards while failing to corral his lone target. The running back injured his knee at some point along the way, and though he was able to check back into the contest, Goodson may have been running on adrenaline. He'll presumably undergo further testing before the Cowboys provide an update on the extent of his injury, but with Goodman on track to miss at least next Sunday's game versus the 49ers, Dallas could turn to practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin to serve in backup roles behind lead back Javonte Williams.

items.head: Strong showing against former squad
items.body: Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. Facing the team for which he played two-plus seasons from 2023-25, Goodson put together a highly efficient performance as a complementary option to Javonte Williams. Goodson's carry and yardage totals were both season highs, as was his average of 6.4 yards per carry. The Iowa product is seeing steady usage in a run-heavy Cowboys offense, and he's logged 29 carries over the last three games heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers.

Goodson returned in the third quarter of Sunday's contest and has logged an additional three carries for 26 yards. The running back heads into the fourth quarter with 10 carries for 70 yards, setting a new career high as he continues to break meaningful runs against his former team.

Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

items.head: Upgrades to full practice
items.body: Mooney (chest) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.

items.head: Considered limited Monday
items.body: Mooney (chest) was estimated to be a limited participant at the Giants' walkthrough practice Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports. Mooney reeled in a season-high three passes for 54 yards and also had a rush for minus-4 yards during Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The wide receiver may have picked up a chest injury during the victory, and as a result, he was considered to be less than 100 percent Monday. Mooney will have two more chances to be upgraded to a full participant prior to Thursday night's matchup with the Commanders.

items.head: Scores touchdown on Thursday Night Football
items.body: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants. Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jaylen Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

items.head: More playing time on tap
items.body: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports. Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.

items.head: Cleared for backup role
items.body: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

items.head: Limited again Thursday
items.body: Wentz (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday. Wentz had his left ankle stepped on by Vikings left guard Joe Huber during Monday's loss to the Bills, and while he didn't miss a snap before Max Brosmer took over for the final possession, the former has operated with practice restrictions to begin Week 10 prep. With the acquisition of Kirk Cousins on Tuesday and Kyler Murray still week to week due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Wentz is expected to return to a reserve role Sunday at Green Bay, but head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn't announced a starter for that contest as of Thursday.

items.head: Listed as limited
items.body: Wentz (ankle) is listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports. Wentz injured his ankle Monday night during his disastrous start against the Bills. The Vikings have since traded for Kirk Cousins, who likely will take over as the starter for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Coach Kevin O'Connell wouldn't commit to starting Cousins and suggested Kyler Murray (hamstring) is unlikely to play, but Cousins' familiarity with the scheme and terminology means he shouldn't need long to prepare.

items.head: Carson Wentz (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: O'Connell defers QB trade question to Vikings GM after Wentz's MNF struggles
items.body: After a historically poor performance by Carson Wentz on Monday night, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was asked if there was a chance the team would trade for a QB ahead of Tuesday's deadline. He deferred the question to GM Nolan Teasley.

items.head: Forgettable performance in spot start
items.body: Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed once for no gain in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. He also lost a fumble.

items.head: In line to draw MNF start
items.body: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer than that should Murray's injury linger. Wentz thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or otherwise are in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.

items.head: NFL outlines steps in Jalen Hurts investigation in letter to senator
items.body: The NFL provided some additional details about the investigation into how Jalen Hurts' blood clots were handled in response to an inquiry from a U.S. senator.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Williams (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports. Despite being listed as limited on all three of the Packers' Week 10 practice reports due to a groin injury, Williams has been cleared for Sunday's matchup. In his four appearances this season, he's turned his 19 touches (11 catches, eight rushes) into 153 yards from scrimmage and one receiving touchdown.

items.head: Savion Williams (injury) is Active
items.body: Williams (groin) was a limited practice participant Thursday.

items.head: Remains limited at practice
items.body: Williams (groin) was a limited practice participant Thursday. Since Williams made his season debut in Week 6 against the Cowboys, his snap share has ranged from 48 to 60 percent over the last four games, and he's made his mark on offense in each one, gathering in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and one touchdown and taking eight carries for 44 yards. A groin issue has capped his reps so far this week, and Friday's injury report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Vikings.

items.head: Savion Williams (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Reels in touchdown versus New England
items.body: Williams caught three of four targets for 25 yards and a touchdown while adding three rushes for 13 yards during Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots. Williams was able to reel in multiple passes for the third time in four games since returning from injured reserve following an ankle injury. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he secured a 10-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Jordan Love by making an acrobatic catch. Williams has now reeled in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown while turning eight carries into 44 yards over four contests this season.

items.head: Brevin Jordan (Finger) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Brevin Jordan (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Plays just five snaps
items.body: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Sunday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders. Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TD. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

items.head: Expected to back up Skattebo on Thursday
items.body: Singletary is expected to return to a change-of-pace role Thursday against the Commanders, as Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation. Singletary recorded a season-high 23 touches in Skattebo's absence during the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 but mustered only 39 yards with all that volume. Prior to that win, Singletary hadn't exceeded six carries in a game this season. Skattebo is expected to lead the backfield in his return, with Singletary likely to feature in passing situations since Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) remains on IR. Greg Desrosiers is also on the roster at RB.

items.head: Inefficient in lead role
items.body: Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards and caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Singletary blew by his previous season high of six carries, as fellow running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy were both sidelined by hamstring injuries. Skattebo has a chance to return for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, while Tracy won't be back prior to Week 12, so Singletary is likely to maintain an elevated role unless the Giants trade for another running back prior to Tuesday's deadline. Singletary didn't make the most of his added opportunities against the Eagles, averaging a meager 1.5 yards per carry.

items.head: Ticketed for RB1 duties
items.body: With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful to play Week 9, Singletary is expected to operate as the Giants' lead back Sunday against the Eagles, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports. Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is on injured reserve and required to miss at least the next four games, and Najee Harris was recently released, so it'll be Singletary's job Sunday. Practice-squad types Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah are in tow as the backups but both have little-to-no experience carrying the ball in the NFL. Volume alone will put Singletary in the fantasy RB2 mix.

items.head: Sources: Eagles to release WR Hollywood Brown per request
items.body: Receiver Hollywood Brown, who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, is being released by the Eagles upon his request, sources told ESPN.

items.head: Chris Collier (Undisclosed) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Giants' Jameis Winston 'lets the dogs out' on 4th down; Commanders don't bite
items.body: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston broke into a rendition of "Who Let the Dogs Out?" in an attempt to draw the Commanders offside on fourth down in New York's 24-21 loss.

items.head: Productive with three catches Thursday
items.body: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.head: Three catches in Week 9 win
items.body: Fields caught three of five targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The rookie wideout is a distant third in pecking order for targets behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely in the New York offense. For the season, Fields has 19 catches for 288 yards and one touchdown on 35 targets, averaging 36.0 yards per game across eight contests.

items.head: Finds end zone in Week 10 win
items.body: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.head: Three grabs in loss
items.body: Williams caught three passes for 25 yards on six targets in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the year, Williams led the team's wide receivers and tight ends in snaps and routes against Los Angeles, but it was a tough matchup against a top-tier pass defense. Williams should have better games moving forward in one of the league's pass-happiest offenses. The rookie wideout should be a full-time player down the stretch in the second half of the season.

items.head: Five catches in win
items.body: Williams caught five of seven targets for 54 yards during Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles. Williams led the team in catches and targets while finishing second behind fellow wide receiver Treylon Burks (81) in receiving yards. With Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year, Williams will have an opportunity to keep carving out a larger role for himself each week with Washington. On the year, the rookie wide receiver has now reeled in 23 of 33 targets for 259 yards and one touchdown over seven regular-season contests.

items.head: Solid involvement in Week 10 win
items.body: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. Ekeler posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (IR, groin) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

items.head: Tallies 10 touches in Week 9
items.body: Ekeler rushed eight times for 16 yards and caught two of three targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Ekeler led the team in carries, toting the rock one more time than fellow running back Rachaad White in the loss. Ekeler was also able to reel in multiple passes for the second time in three games, and he figures to remain in a relatively even backfield split with White against the Giants in Week 10.

items.head: Runs for 36 yards in SNF win
items.body: Ekeler rushed eight times for 36 yards in Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles. The veteran running back wasn't targeted in the passing game on a night when Jayden Daniels attempted 29 passes. Involved in a three-way backfield that also includes Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols (foot), Ekeler has minimal fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's matchup with the Rams' strong defense. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) is required to miss at least one more game on injured reserve.

items.head: Records game-winning TD in victory
items.body: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

items.head: Just three grabs in Sunday's loss
items.body: Diggs caught three of five targets for 51 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo ended up leading the Commanders' injury-depleted group of pass catchers with seven targets each, and the former led the team in receiving yards and caught Jayden Daniels' only TD pass. Diggs' modest showing still represented his biggest yardage total since Week 1, although he did see his two-game scoring streak come to an end. Diggs will try to ramp up his production in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.head: Scores fifth TD in Week 8 win
items.body: Diggs caught three of six targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-10 win over the Eagles. Diggs scored an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the ensuing PAT tied the score at 10-10. That was the team-leading fifth receiving touchdown for Diggs in six appearances with the Commanders. He's the top option for Jayden Daniels on paper since Terry McLaurin sustained a season-ending knee injury in Washington's previous game, though Treylon Burks (81) and Antonio Williams (54) both had more receiving yards Sunday, and Williams also drew one more target than Diggs to lead the team. Diggs is poised to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against the stout Rams secondary.

items.head: Overcomes turnovers in win
items.body: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, he subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. Daniels ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.head: First turnover of season in loss to Rams
items.body: Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. He also gained 16 rushing yards on four carries and lost a fumble. The lost fumble was the first giveaway of the season for Daniels in six games. The third-year QB also struggled to sustain drives while working with a badly depleted wide receiver room, and his lone TD was a seven-yard toss to Van Jefferson -- a player who had zero catches on the year coming into Sunday -- in the second quarter. Injuries have derailed the first half of the season for the Commanders, but Daniels will try to spark his team to life in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.head: Modest numbers in Week 8 win
items.body: Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown while rushing twice for 23 yards in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Eagles. Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter and led four drives that ended in successful field goals before Rachaad White sealed the deal with a one-yard touchdown run late in the fourth quarter. Diggs has been on the receiving end of four of Daniels' six touchdown passes this season. Daniels threw for 300 yards in a Week 6 loss to the 49ers prior to Washington's Week 7 bye, but he hasn't exceeded 233 passing yards in any of his 11 other regular-season outings since the start of the 2025 campaign. Sunday night's win over Philadelphia marked Daniels' first win since Week 5 of the 2025 season, when Washington defeated the Chargers. The Commanders will take a 2-4-1 record into a Week 9 home game against the Rams.

items.head: Middling production in Week 10 loss
items.body: Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

items.head: Giants' Nabers calls Fox analyst Olsen's body language critique a 'lie'
items.body: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said Tuesday he posted on social media after the game because he thought the critique from Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen about his body language and being a bad teammate was a "lie."

items.head: Giants' Malik Nabers takes issue with Greg Olsen, Fox for comments during game
items.body: Malik Nabers took the issue with Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen for criticizing his body language during the Giants' win Sunday.

items.head: Quiet in Week 9 win
items.body: Nabers caught five of eight targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers recorded at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye but failed to extend that streak in Sunday's low-scoring win, during which J.J. McCarthy (hip) and Jameis Winston combined to throw for just 198 yards. The star wide receiver led the team with eight targets but finished third in receiving yards behind Darnell Mooney (54) and Isaiah Likely (53). Nabers had his hands on what would have been a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter but failed to secure a diving catch attempt. McCarthy left in the third quarter but managed to return later in the second half, and he can be tentatively penciled in as the starting QB for Thursday's home game against the leaky Commanders pass defense.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia. Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.

items.head: Malik Nabers (injury) is Active
items.body: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

items.head: 'Full go' for Week 9
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Nabers (knee) "practiced fully" Friday and will be "full go" for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Matt Citak of the Giants' official site reports. That's not to say Nabers won't be tagged with a designation once the Giants post their final Week 9 injury report Friday, but it appears his absence from Thursday's practice due to a knee issue was merely a blip on the radar. He's strung together four consecutive 100-yard performances, a stretch in which his receiving line sits at 36-509-2 on 51 targets. Nabers' presence will be key for New York's offense led by new starting QB J.J. McCarthy.

items.head: Looks ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) was catching passes during Friday's walkthrough and "should be 'good' to go" For Sunday's game against the Eagles, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports. After sitting out Thursday's practice due to the knee issue, Nabers appears to be trending in the right direction for Sunday's game at Philadelphia. Still, the Giants' final injury report will provide the clearest indication of whether the wide receiver takes a designation into the weekend.

items.head: Returns, finishes with four catches
items.body: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards. Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.

items.head: Chig Okonkwo (injury) is Active
items.body: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.

items.head: Turns in full practice
items.body: Okonkwo (hip) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice. Now that he's gotten a full practice under his belt this week, Okonkwo should be in the clear for Thursday's game against the Giants. The veteran tight end has emerged a more integral part of the Washington passing game over the last four games, having cleared 70 percent snap shares in each of those contests while putting together a 19-218-0 receiving line on 24 targets.

items.head: Dealing with hip issue
items.body: Okonkwo was deemed a limited participant on Washington's estimated practice report Monday due to a hip injury, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Okonkwo appears to have gotten hurt in Sunday's loss to the Rams, though he logged his usual offensive snap share (74 percent) and finished with s solid 6-57-0 receiving line on seven targets. The Commanders didn't actually practice Monday, so the tight end's level of activity -- if any -- Tuesday should provide more clarity about whether he's at risk of missing Thursday's clash against the Giants. Washington has been hurt by injuries to its wideout corps, and Okonkwo has stepped up with 57 or more receiving yards in three of the team's past four games.

items.head: Chig Okonkwo (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: Okonkwo caught six of seven targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.

items.head: Six snags in loss
items.body: Okonkwo caught six of seven targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Okonkwo finished tied for the team lead in targets with wide receiver Van Jefferson, reeling in at least five passes for the second time in three games. The tight end's seven targets matched a season high, and he is still searching for his first touchdown as a member of the Commanders after joining the team in the offseason.

items.head: Musters two catches in Week 8
items.body: Okonkwo tallied two catches (on four targets) for 32 yards during Sunday's 27-10 win versus the Eagles. Okonkwo logged a typical 77 percent snap share in Week 8, but aside from a stellar 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter, he didn't contribute much to the Commanders offense. Overall, he's mustered just a 17-182-0 line on 24 targets in his five appearances this season, but 15 of his catches have occurred in the four full contests for Jayden Daniels in 2026, so the tight end has exhibited a rapport with the team's primary signal-caller. Okonkwo will aim for a bounceback this coming Sunday against the Rams.

items.head: Jonathan Mingo (Ankle) is Out
items.body: Mingo (ankle, foot) did not practice Thursday, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Jonathan Mingo (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Mingo (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
